The Book of Enoch (1 Enoch): A Clear English Rendering of Charles's Translation from the Ethiopic — Workshop Edition (full apparatus)
DRAFT — unpublished; under audit. Each block below is the complete worksheet for the chapter, verbatim.
This edition contains the First Book of Enoch (1 Enoch) only, in all its 108 chapters. The Second Book of Enoch (2 Enoch, surviving in Slavonic) and the Third Book of Enoch (3 Enoch, a Hebrew mystical text) are separate, later works. They are not part of this edition.
© 2026 Robert Tilford, editor. This edition is given away freely. Anyone may download, copy, print, and share it, in whole or in part, without asking permission. Attribution to the editor is requested as a courtesy; the gift is not withdrawn if it is omitted.
Notes and corrections are welcome. A reader who finds an error, or who knows of a newer reading, is invited to write to the editor: roberttilford19@gmail.com. This is a living edition. Corrections that are verified will be entered, credited to the reader who sent them, and the edition re-issued with its record updated.
A living translation, holding itself accountable.
A note on the names in this book: the Watchers' names are spelled as Charles printed them, and the same Watcher may appear under more than one spelling from chapter to chapter, because the old copies themselves vary. The spellings have not been tidied to make them agree.

To the memory of Robert Henry Charles (1855–1931), scholar of the Ethiopic text.

This edition stands on his work: his edition of the Ge'ez manuscripts, and his English translation of 1912. Without them, the First Book of Enoch would have had no road into this editor's hands, and none into plain English by this road. The rendering is ours. The bedrock is his.

# WORKSHEET — 1 Enoch, Chapter 1

> DRAFT — clear-English rendering prepared with AI assistance; a translation of a translation (Ge'ez from lost Hebrew/Aramaic and Greek stages); not reviewed by a Ge'ez scholar; not finished. State: AUDITED — G1 worker self-audit passed (see G1 Audit Record); G2 and G3 passed on 2026-10-12; G4 read-through ruled read by Robert on 2026-10-14. Never claim finished, first, or definitive.

- **Chapter:** 1 (Section I, Book of the Watchers, ch. 1–36; Introduction I–V: Parable of Enoch on the Future Lot of the Wicked and the Righteous)
- **Witness status:** Ge'ez complete + Greek control (Codex Panopolitanus, ch. 1:1–32:6) + Aramaic scraps in the section generally (4Q201 covers parts of ch. 2–9; no Aramaic wording transcribed for ch. 1 in this slice) — best-controlled section of the book, per `~/workspace/enoch/SOURCE-AUDIT.md` §1.6
- **Base route:** Route A (Charles 1912 English base) — the route taken for this edition. Route B (1906 Ethiopic control column) was not performed, and no claim to it is made
- **State:** AUDITED — G1 worker self-audit passed with notes (see G1 Audit Record, 2026-10-09). G2 independent second audit and G3 term sweep were done on 2026-10-12 and passed; the Gemini mechanical audit was ruled on by Robert on 2026-10-12; G4 Robert read-through was ruled read by Robert on 2026-10-14. This state means only that the G1 audit below was actually performed and recorded; it is not "finished."
- **Control footnotes:** witness flag + Charles-apparatus forks noted in the G1 record
- **Canonical cross-references:** noted in apparatus only

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 1

Copy verified this lane (2026-10-09; re-verified against the scanned text at G1):
- Internet Archive item `bookofenochor1en00char` — https://archive.org/details/bookofenochor1en00char — metadata: Publication date 1912, Publisher Oxford Clarendon Press, Author Charles, R. H. (Robert Henry), 1855-1931. Public domain (1912 publication). Printed translation spans pp. 5–8 (Section I, Chapter I).
- **G1 correction (2026-10-09):** the first worksheet draft normalised Charles's critical signs as `[ ]` / `{ }`. The 1912 print uses the bracket system defined on its "Abbreviations, Brackets, and Symbols" page (immediately before Section I): corner brackets for words found in one tradition only (Greek-only or Ethiopic-only), `[ ]` for interpolations, `( )` for words supplied by the editor, and thick type for emendations. The base text below restores that system in plain-text form (`⌜ ⌝` = single-tradition corner brackets; the G-only/E-only direction is given in the G1 record wherever Charles's notes settle it). The 1917 SPCK edition is a distinct, slimmer PD edition and was used only as a cross-check; it is cited as 1917 wherever used.

Base text (Charles 1912, verse numbering as in Charles; critical signs restored):

1. The words of the blessing of Enoch, wherewith he blessed the elect ⌜and⌝ righteous, who will be living in the day of tribulation, when all the wicked ⌜and godless⌝ are to be removed.
2. And he took up his parable and said — Enoch a righteous man, whose eyes were opened by God, saw the vision of the Holy One in the heavens, ⌜which⌝ the angels showed me, and from them I heard everything, and from them I understood as I saw, but not for this generation, but for a remote one which is for to come.
3. Concerning the elect I said, and took up my parable concerning them: The Holy Great One will come forth from His dwelling,
4. And the eternal God will tread upon the earth, (even) on Mount Sinai, [And appear from His camp] And appear in the strength of His might from the heaven of heavens.
5. And all shall be smitten with fear, And the Watchers shall quake, And great fear and trembling shall seize them unto the ends of the earth.
6. And the high mountains shall be shaken, And the high hills shall be made low, And shall melt like wax before the flame.
7. And the earth shall be ⌜wholly⌝ rent in sunder, And all that is upon the earth shall perish, And there shall be a judgement upon all (men).
8. But with the righteous He will make peace, And will protect the elect, And mercy shall be upon them. And they shall all belong to God, And they shall be prospered, And they shall ⌜all⌝ be blessed. ⌜And He will help them all,⌝ And light shall appear unto them, ⌜And He will make peace with them.⌝
9. And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of ⌜His⌝ holy ones, To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy ⌜all⌝ the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works ⌜of their ungodliness⌝ which they have ungodly committed, ⌜And of all the hard things which⌝ ungodly sinners ⌜have spoken⌝ against Him.

## Control column (labelled, not independently transcribed in this lane)

- **Ge'ez (Charles 1906, 23 MSS):** the ultimate source of Charles 1912. Not opened as an independent control column here — Route A only.
- **Greek (Panopolitanus 1:1–32:6; cited by Charles as 𝔊ᵃ, with Syncellus 𝔊ˢ where relevant):** control exists for this whole chapter in principle. No Greek wording was independently transcribed in this lane; every Greek-related fork recorded in the G1 record below is taken from Charles's own printed translation signs and notes (his reprint of the fragments is part of the 1912 PD volume). Syncellus quotations proper begin at ch. 6, so they do not control ch. 1 directly.
- **Aramaic (Qumran):** the Watchers section has Aramaic scraps (4Q201, 4Q202, 4Q204); the audit records 4Q201 coverage as parts of ch. 2–9. No Aramaic wording is claimed for ch. 1 here.
- **Laurence (1821, PD, check-only):** at the parallel printing consulted in the DRAFTED slice, Laurence reads "The word of the blessing" (singular) at v. 1 and supplies "[was] with God"; his verse grouping merges what Charles separates at vv. 6–8. Noted as an early rendering only; never the skeleton, and his 105-chapter numbering is not mapped onto the 108.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above; G1 micro-fixes marked *)

1. These are the words of Enoch's blessing. With them he blessed God's chosen, righteous people, who will live in the day of trouble, when all the wicked and godless will be taken away.
2. He began his parable and said: I am Enoch, a righteous man. God opened my eyes, and I saw a vision of the Holy One in heaven. The angels showed it to me. From them I heard everything, and I understood what I saw. It is not for this generation, but for a far-off generation still to come.
3. I spoke about the chosen ones, and I began my parable about them: The Holy Great One* will come out from where He lives,
4. and the eternal God will step onto the earth, on Mount Sinai, and He will appear in His full strength from the highest heaven.
5. Everyone will be struck with fear. The Watchers will shake with fear. Great fear and trembling will take hold of them to the ends of the earth.
6. The high mountains will shake. The high hills will be brought low, and will melt like wax in a flame.
7. The earth will be torn completely apart. Everything on the earth will die. There will be judgment on everyone.
8. But with the righteous He will make peace. He will protect His chosen ones, and He will show them mercy. They will all belong to God. They will do well. They will all be blessed. He will help them all. Light will appear for them, and He will make peace with them.
9. Look! He comes with tens of thousands of His holy ones, to judge everyone, to destroy all the ungodly, and to convict all people of every ungodly deed they have done, and of every hard word* that ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **v. 1 "elect"** rendered "God's chosen, righteous people" and, at vv. 3 and 8, "the chosen ones" / "His chosen ones". Term-consistency (elect / chosen) is a G3 sweep item across all 108 chapters; this slice's choice is recorded, not locked. The possessive "God's" in v. 1 is a plain-register explicitation (the base reads "the elect ⌜and⌝ righteous"); it is disclosed here and at G4 it is Robert's to keep or cut.
- **v. 2 "I am Enoch":** explicitation of the base's "Enoch a righteous man" after "he took up his parable and said". Charles's note observes that the change from third to first person is frequent in this book. Recorded, not hidden.
- **v. 3 title (G1 fix *):** the DRAFTED slice read "The Holy and Great One", following the Ethiopic (E) form. Charles's printed translation line reads "The Holy Great One", and his note states that E reads "the Holy and Great One" while the Greek appears to preserve the original at this verse. The draft was corrected at G1 to follow the base line ("The Holy Great One"); the E variant stands in this note. The title recurs (Charles lists 1:3; 10:1; 14:1; etc.) and is a G3 item.
- **v. 4 bracketed phrase:** Charles prints "[And appear from His camp]" in square brackets — his sign for an interpolation — and his note states that he bracketed it as an addition, against the parallelism and the sense, noting that E reads "And appear with His hosts". The draft follows Charles's main line ("appear in His full strength from the highest heaven") and does **not** incorporate the bracketed phrase. Disposition at G1: excluded from the draft text, retained in this note. This is the lane's standing rule for `[ ]` unless Robert rules otherwise: interpolations stay visible in the notes, out of the reading text.
- **vv. 4 and 7 supplied words:** Charles supplies "(even)" (v. 4) and "(men)" (v. 7) in round brackets — his sign for words supplied by the editor. The draft's "on Mount Sinai" and "judgment on everyone" carry those senses without brackets; the supply is recorded here so the audit can check it. Standing rule: `( )` supplies may be absorbed where the plain English needs them, always recorded.
- **Corner-bracketed words (⌜ ⌝):** words found in one tradition only, as printed by Charles (v. 1 "and" ×2; v. 2 "which"; v. 7 "wholly"; v. 8 "all" and the two lines "And He will help them all" / "And He will make peace with them"; v. 9 "His", "all", "of their ungodliness", "And of all the hard things which", "have spoken"). The draft follows Charles's printed translation in including them. Standing rule: `⌜ ⌝` words are part of Charles's translation and are drafted; any verse where including or excluding one would change the sense is footnoted as a fork (none in ch. 1 changes the sense beyond the v. 8 lines, next note).
- **v. 8 closing lines:** Charles's notes indicate that the lines "And He will help them all" and "And He will make peace with them" rest on the Greek against a shorter Ethiopic at this point (E omits the peace line, which Charles holds the verse-structure requires). The draft includes both lines, following Charles. Recorded so no reader mistakes the Ethiopic alone for the whole evidence at this verse.
- **v. 5 "Watchers":** retained as a proper name (the fallen angels of ch. 6 onward), not translated as "watchmen" or "guards". Standing term — G3 item. Charles's note at v. 5 records that the Greek at this verse reads differently ("shall believe", with an added singing passage he treats as a scribal expansion toward 2 Enoch 18); the draft follows the Ethiopic line with Charles.
- **v. 9 number (G1 fix *):** the DRAFTED slice read "every hard word" (singular) for the base's "all the hard things" (plural). Corrected at G1 to "every hard word" kept singular-generic but flagged here — on re-check the plural sense is carried by "every"; Robert may prefer "hard words" at read-through. Either wording is a G4 reader decision; the number fork is now on the record instead of silent.
- **v. 9 and Jude:** Jude 14–15 quotes this verse in the New Testament tradition; Charles's note confirms the quotation and its compressed form. Recorded here as an apparatus fact only; whether the printed draft footnotes it is.
- **"judgement / judgment":** Charles uses the British "judgement"; the draft uses "judgment". Spelling only; no wording change intended.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with Greek/Aramaic controls present in principle for the section and consulted here only through Charles's printed signs and notes. Any future claim of Greek-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed.

## G1 Audit Record — Chapter 1 (performed 2026-10-09, this slice)

**Scope of audit (per checkpoint):** fidelity to Charles 1912; bracket handling at vv. 1/4/7–9 (extended to all verses); control-column status. Method: verse-by-verse comparison of the draft against the corrected 1912 base above, re-verified against the scanned 1912 volume (IA `bookofenochor1en00char`, translation pp. 5–8, including the "Abbreviations, Brackets, and Symbols" page).

**Findings:**

1. **Base transcription (material, corrected):** the DRAFTED worksheet normalised Charles's critical signs as `[ ]` / `{ }` and described them as the 1912 system. The 1912 print in fact uses corner brackets (`⌜ ⌝`), `[ ]` = interpolation, `( )` = editor-supplied, thick type = emended. Base text corrected above; copy-verification statement rewritten. The underlying English wording of the DRAFTED base was otherwise accurate against the scan (wording verified vv. 1–9; pp. 5–8). No draft wording had been built on the notation error.
2. **Completeness:** 9 of 9 verses drafted; no verse omitted, added, or reordered. The only base material excluded from the reading text is the square-bracketed interpolation at v. 4, excluded with Charles's own stated reasons and retained in the Notes — disposition recorded, not silent.
3. **Bracket handling:** `( )` supplies absorbed and recorded (vv. 4, 7) — PASS. `[ ]` interpolation excluded and recorded (v. 4) — PASS, standing rule stated. `⌜ ⌝` single-tradition words included with Charles and inventoried (vv. 1, 2, 7, 8, 9) — PASS; the v. 8 Greek-supported lines are now flagged in the Notes.
4. **Fidelity slips found and fixed:** (a) v. 3 title followed the Ethiopic variant instead of Charles's printed line — corrected to "The Holy Great One", variant noted (G3 title item). (b) v. 9 "hard things" plural carried as singular-generic "hard word" — fork put on the record for G4 (wording held). No other wording change to the base's sense was found; plain-register explicitations ("God's chosen", v. 1; "I am Enoch", v. 2; "day of trouble" for "day of tribulation", v. 1) are disclosed in the Notes and left for Robert's read-through rather than silently normalised in either direction.
5. **Control-column status:** Greek control exists for the whole chapter (Panopolitanus) and Aramaic scraps exist for the section, but neither was independently transcribed in this lane; all Greek-related statements in this worksheet derive from Charles's printed signs and notes in the PD 1912 volume. The worksheet's claim level was corrected to say exactly that. Laurence remains check-only and was not used as a skeleton. Control status: HONEST, Route A — PASS.
6. **Banner and claims:** DRAFT banner with AI-assistance disclosure and "translation of a translation" wording intact; no "finished / first / definitive" claim anywhere in the file; the D1, D3 and D4 questions were overtaken by the Route A build, and the banner and base-route lines state Route A as the route taken. PASS.

**Result:** **G1 PASS WITH NOTES.** State advanced DRAFTED → AUDITED for Chapter 1 only. Gates since G1: the Gemini mechanical audit was ruled on by Robert on 2026-10-12 (three fixes applied); internal G2 and G3 were done on 2026-10-12 and passed; G4 read-through was ruled read by Robert on 2026-10-14; G5 is the wording sweep of 2026-10-14. Chapter 2 was not started in this slice.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 2

Copy verified this lane (2026-10-09; scanned-page verification performed at G1):
- Internet Archive item `bookofenochor1en00char` — https://archive.org/details/bookofenochor1en00char — metadata: Publication date 1912, Publisher Oxford Clarendon Press, Author Charles, R. H. (Robert Henry), 1855-1931. Public domain (1912 publication). Chapter II verified in the IA BookReader scan at G1: Chapter II ("II. 1.") begins at the foot of printed p. 8 (leaf n123) and completes on printed p. 9 (leaf n124, running head "Sect. I] Chapter II. 1–3"); the "Abbreviations, Brackets, and Symbols" page is printed p. cxii (leaf n115), immediately before Section I.
- **Bracket system (re-verified at G1 against printed p. cxii):** single corner brackets = words found in Gᵍ (the Akhmim/Gizeh Greek fragment) but not in E (Ethiopic); the double-stroked corner pair = words found in E but not in Gᵍ or Gˢ (Syncellus Greek); `⟨ ⟩` = restored words; `[ ]` = interpolations; `( )` = words supplied by the editor; **thick type = emended words.** The draft-slice transcription below originally carried this system forward from the ch. 1 G1 record without the Gᵍ/E direction split; the G1 record below supplies the directions verse by verse.
- The DRAFTED slice was built from the Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 02" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_02), cross-checked against a second Charles reproduction; at G1 its wording vv. 1–3 was verified against the scanned 1912 pages above with one spelling correction ("every thing", two words, at v. 1). The 1917 SPCK edition is a distinct, slimmer PD edition; it is cited as 1917 wherever used, never as interchangeable "Charles."

Base text (Charles 1912, verse numbering as in Charles; critical signs restored in plain-text form: `⌜ ⌝` = single corner brackets (Gᵍ, not in E); `⌜⌜ ⌝⌝` = double-stroked corner brackets (E, not in Gᵍ/Gˢ)):

1. Observe ye every thing that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, ⌜and⌝ the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order. 2. Behold ye the earth, and give heed to the things which take place upon it from first to last, ⌜how steadfast they are⌉, how ⌜none of the things upon earth⌉ change, ⌜but⌉ all the works of God appear ⌜to you⌉. 3. Behold the summer and the winter, ⌜⌜how the whole earth is filled with water, and clouds and dew and rain lie upon it.⌝⌝

## Control column (labelled, not independently transcribed in this lane)

- **Ge'ez (Charles 1906, 23 MSS):** the ultimate source of Charles 1912. Not opened as an independent control column here — Route A only.
- **Greek (Panopolitanus 1:1–32:6; cited by Charles as 𝔊ᵃ):** control exists for this whole chapter in principle. No Greek wording was independently transcribed in this lane; every Greek-related note below is taken from Charles's own printed translation signs as transcribed. Syncellus quotations proper begin at ch. 6, so they do not control ch. 2 directly.
- **Aramaic (Qumran):** the Watchers section has Aramaic scraps; the SOURCE-AUDIT records 4Q201 coverage as parts of ch. 2–9. No Aramaic wording is claimed for ch. 2 here.
- **Laurence (1821, PD, check-only):** not consulted as a skeleton in this slice; Laurence's 105-chapter numbering is never mapped onto the 108. Any Laurence parallel is reserved for G1 as an early-rendering note only.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Watch everything that happens in the sky. See how the lights in the sky do not change their paths. They all rise and set in order, each in its season, and they do not break the order set for them.
2. Look at the earth. Pay attention to the things that happen on it, from first to last. See how steady they hold, how nothing on earth changes, but all of God's works show themselves to you.
3. Look at the summer and the winter. See how the whole earth is filled with water, and how clouds, dew, and rain rest on it.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Chapter length and numbering (verified at G1):** Charles's Chapter II is short — three verses (vv. 1–3) in the 108-chapter division this lane follows. Verified against the scanned 1912 volume at G1: there is no large display heading; the main text on printed p. 8 simply begins "II. 1." after Chapter I ends; the running head on printed p. 9 reads "Sect. I] Chapter II. 1–3", confirming v. 3 inside Chapter II; Chapter III ("III.", the winter-trees observation) begins on printed p. 10. Some OCR excerpts in circulation misplace the "CHAPTER III" heading before v. 3; the scan settles the placing as this worksheet has it.
- **Corner-bracketed words — directions settled at G1 (printed p. cxii):** single corner brackets `⌜ ⌝` = found in Gᵍ (Akhmim/Gizeh Greek) but **not in E** — these are Greek-supported words the Ethiopic lacks (v. 1 "and"; v. 2 "how steadfast they are", "none of the things upon earth", "but", "to you"). The double-stroked pair `⌜⌜ ⌝⌝` = found in E but **not in Gᵍ or Gˢ** — at v. 3 the whole closing sentence ("how the whole earth is filled with water, and clouds and dew and rain lie upon it") is Ethiopic-only wording with no Greek counterpart. The draft follows Charles's printed translation in including all of them — the lane's standing rule from the ch. 1 G1 record: corner-bracketed words are part of Charles's translation and are drafted; any verse where including or excluding one would change the sense is footnoted as a fork. At v. 3 the fork is real and is recorded, not hidden: a reader following the Greek tradition alone finds the chapter ending at v. 2; the draft includes the Ethiopic sentence with Charles.
- **v. 2 "steadfast" (emendation flag — RESOLVED at G1):** verified against the enlarged scanned page (printed p. 9): "steadfast" inside ⌜how steadfast they are⌉ **is** printed in thick type — the only thick-type word in that phrase — Charles's sign (p. cxii) for an emended word. The rest of the corner-bracketed phrase prints in ordinary type. Draft wording "how steady they hold" carries Charles's emended sense; the emendation is recorded here so the audit can check it, and the word's emended status is a standing note for G3/G4 if Robert wants the reading text to signal it.
- **No supplied or interpolated material:** this chapter carries no `( )` editor-supplied words and no `[ ]` interpolations in the transcribed base. Nothing was absorbed or excluded under those standing rules in this draft.
- **v. 1 "luminaries"** rendered "the lights in the sky" — plain-register rendering of the sun, moon, and stars as a class; the term is recorded here so G3 can settle one rendering ("luminaries" / "heavenly lights" / "lights") across the book, especially against the Astronomical Book (ch. 72–82), where the class is the whole subject.
- **v. 1 "transgress not against their appointed order"** rendered "do not break the order set for them". The obedience-of-nature contrast (creation keeps its order; the addressees of ch. 5 have not) is the argument of I–V; the draft keeps Charles's plain sequence and adds no contrast wording that the base does not have.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based (transcription copy as cited above), witness-flagged, with Greek/Aramaic controls present in principle for the section and consulted here only through Charles's printed signs. Any future claim of Greek-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed, plus the G1 scanned-page verification noted above.

## G1 Audit Record — Chapter 2 (performed 2026-10-09, this slice)

**Scope of audit (per checkpoint):** fidelity to Charles 1912; scanned-page verification of the ch. 2 base in IA `bookofenochor1en00char`; the v. 2 "steadfast" thick-type flag resolved; bracket handling per the standing rules. Method: verse-by-verse comparison of the draft against the base above, with the base itself verified against the scanned 1912 volume in the IA BookReader (leaves n115 = printed p. cxii "Abbreviations, Brackets, and Symbols"; n123 = printed p. 8; n124 = printed p. 9; n125 = printed p. 10), including enlarged page views for the thick-type check.

**Findings:**

1. **Base verification (material, settled):** Chapter II ("II. 1.") begins at the foot of printed p. 8 and completes on printed p. 9 (running head "Sect. I] Chapter II. 1–3"). The DRAFTED slice's base wording vv. 1–3 (from the Wikisource transcription) is accurate against the scan with one spelling correction: v. 1 "every thing" is two words in the 1912 print (worksheet base corrected). No draft wording had been built on the error. The chapter-division flag from the DRAFTED slice is settled: v. 3 stands inside Chapter II; Chapter III ("III.") begins on printed p. 10 with the winter-trees observation, followed by "IV." and "V. 1." on the same page.
2. **Bracket system, directions resolved:** the 1912 "Abbreviations, Brackets, and Symbols" page (printed p. cxii) distinguishes what the ch. 1 worksheet carried generically: single corner brackets = Gᵍ but not E; double-stroked corner pair = E but not Gᵍ/Gˢ; `⟨ ⟩` = restored; `[ ]` = interpolations; `( )` = editor-supplied; thick type = emended. Applied here: vv. 1–2 corner-bracketed words are Greek-supported (Gᵍ, not in E); the v. 3 closing sentence is Ethiopic-only (E, not in Gᵍ/Gˢ). The worksheet's bracket inventory was correct as transcribed; the Gᵍ/E directions are now on the record (see Notes). ## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Editor-supplied words — `( )`:** the base supplies "(in the winter)" in round brackets — Charles's sign for words supplied by the editor. The draft's "in winter" absorbs the supplied sense; the supply is recorded here so the audit can check it. Standing rule (from ch. 1 G1): `( )` supplies may be absorbed where the plain English needs them, always recorded.
- **Double-stroked corner bracket — `⌜⌜` (E, not in Gᵍ/Gˢ), closing not printed:** the opening double corner before "seem" marks, on the bracket direction settled at ch. 2 G1 from printed p. cxii, Ethiopic wording with no counterpart in the Greek witnesses, starting at "seem". **Where Charles intended that bracket to close is not settled by the 1912 print:** neither scan inspected at G1 (IA `bookofenochor1en00char` and IA `cu31924067146773`, both printed p. 10) prints a closing double corner anywhere in the verse, and the Wikisource transcription likewise carries the opening only. The draft follows Charles's printed translation in including the whole verse — the lane's standing rule: corner-bracketed words are part of Charles's translation and are drafted; any verse where including or excluding one would change the sense is footnoted as a fork. Here the fork is recorded, not hidden: at minimum the "seem as though they had withered…" picture rests on the Ethiopic line from "seem" onward for an unsettled span; a reader following the Greek tradition alone does not have that Ethiopic-only wording, however far it runs. The trees that keep their foliage two to three years until the new growth comes are the evergreen-type trees of the observation; the draft keeps Charles's "till the new comes" as "until the new leaves come", supplying "leaves" from the verse's own "foliage" — recorded as a plain-register explicitation for G4.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 5

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 05" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_05), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Scanned-page verification done at G1 against the two IA 1912 copies (leaves n125–n128 = printed pp. 10–13) — one material wording correction ("joy" → "grace", v. 7a) and two bracket additions ("which", "God" in v. 2) applied from the scans.

Base text (Charles 1912, verse numbering as in Charles; as printed on pp. 10–13 in two independent scans — see G1 Audit Record):

1. Observe yeᵃ how the trees cover themselves with green leaves and bear fruit: wherefore give ye heed ⌈and know⌉ with regard to all ⌈His works⌉, and recognize how He that liveth for ever hath made them so. *(ᵃ = superscript reference mark, not a bracket — settled at G1.)*
2. And ⌈all⌉ His works go on ⌈thus⌉ from year to year ⌈for ever⌉, and all the tasks ⌈which⌉ they accomplish for Him, and ⌈their tasks⌉ change not, but according as ⌈God⌉ hath ordained so is it done.
3. And behold how the sea and the rivers in like manner accomplish ⌈and change not⌉ their tasks ⌈from His commandments⌉.
4. But ye—ye have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of the Lord, but ye have turned away and spoken proud and hard words with your impure mouths against His greatness. Oh, ye hard-hearted, ye shall find no peace.
5. Therefore shall ye execrate your days, and the years of your life shall perish, and the ⌈years of your destruction⌉ shall be multiplied in eternal execration, and ye shall find no mercy.
6a. In those days ye shall make your names an eternal execration unto all the righteous, b. and by you shall ⌈all⌉ who curse, curse, c. ⌈And all⌉ the sinners ⌈and godless⌉ shall imprecate by you, 7c. and for you the godless there shall be a curse. 6d. ⌈And all the . . . shall rejoice, e. and there shall be forgiveness of sins, f. and every mercy and peace and forbearance: g. there shall be salvation unto them, a goodly light. i. And for all of you sinners there shall be no salvation, j. but on you all shall abide a curse¹.
7a. But for the elect there shall be light and grace and peace, b. and they shall inherit the earth.
8. And then there shall be bestowed upon the elect wisdom, and they shall all live and never again sin, either through ungodliness or through pride: but they who are wise shall be humble.
9. And they shall not again transgress, nor shall they sin all the days of their life, nor shall they die of (the divine) anger or wrath, but they shall complete the number of the days of their life. And their lives shall be increased in peace, and the years of their joy shall be multiplied, in eternal gladness and peace, all the days of their life.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Watch how the trees cover themselves with green leaves and bear fruit. So pay attention and know, about all His works, and see that He who lives forever made them so.
2. All His works go on this way from year to year, forever. They carry out for Him all their tasks, and their tasks do not change — but as God has ordained, so it is done.
3. And see how the sea and the rivers do the same: they carry out their tasks and do not change, by His commandments.
4. But you — you have not been steadfast, and you have not done the Lord's commandments. You turned away and spoke proud, hard words with your unclean mouths against His greatness. O you hard-hearted ones, you shall find no peace.
5. So you will curse your days, and the years of your life will perish, and the years of your destruction will be multiplied in endless cursing, and you shall find no mercy.
6a. In those days you will make your names an eternal curse to all the righteous, b. and by you all who curse will curse, and all the sinners and the godless will curse by your name; 7c. and for you, the godless, there shall be a curse. 6d. And all the ... shall rejoice, e. and there shall be forgiveness of sins, f. and every mercy and peace and forbearance: g. there shall be salvation for them, a good light. i. And for all of you sinners there shall be no salvation, j. but on all of you shall rest a curse.
7a. But for the elect there shall be light and grace and peace, b. and they shall inherit the earth.
8. And then wisdom shall be given to the elect, and they shall all live and never sin again — not through godlessness and not through pride. But those who are wise shall be humble.
9. They shall not transgress again, nor sin all the days of their life, nor die by the divine anger or wrath. They shall live out the full number of the days of their life, and their lives shall grow in peace, and the years of their joy shall be multiplied, in endless gladness and peace, all the days of their life.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 5:** the charge that closes the Introduction I–V: ch. 2 (ordered sky and earth), ch. 3 (winter trees), ch. 4 (summer sun) were the observations; ch. 5 turns to the reader — "But ye..." (v. 4), then the lot of the wicked (vv. 5–6) and the lot of the elect (vv. 7–9). The draft keeps Charles's contrast structure and adds none.
- **"execrate" (vv. 5–6):** kept as "curse" in plain register — "you will curse your days", "an eternal curse", "in endless cursing", "curse by your name". The repeated root is preserved; recorded for the G3 term sweep.
- **"(the divine) anger or wrath" (v. 9):** Charles's parenthetical ( ) supply — kept parenthetical in the base; draft absorbs "divine" as "the divine anger or wrath" (cf. ch. 2–4 standing rule: editor-supplied ( ) words are absorbed without comment but recorded here). The build as made records absorbed supplies in the Notes; the question whether they are signalled in the reading text stands settled by that practice.
- **Bracket identities — SETTLED at G1:** every bracketed phrase in ch. 5 (v. 1 "and know", "His works"; v. 2 "all", "thus", "for ever", "which", "their tasks", "God"; v. 3 "and change not", "from His commandments"; v. 5 "the years of your destruction"; 6b "all"; 6c "And all", "and godless"; 6d opening only, "And all the . . . shall rejoice,") carries **single thin corner brackets** in print = words in Gᵍ (Akhmim Greek) but not in E (Ethiopic), per the key on printed p. cxii. No double-stroked corner pairs, no `[ ]`, no `⟨ ⟩` occur anywhere in ch. 5. Round parentheses occur once: "(the divine)" in v. 9, Charles's editor-supply. The transcription's "Observe ye⌉⌉" at v. 1 is NOT a bracket: print shows "Observe ye" with a superscript "a" (a textual reference mark), settled at G1; the "1" after "a curse" in 6j is likewise a superscript footnote-reference mark, not a bracket closing.
- **The ". . ." (v. 6d):** a dotted lacuna printed inside the bracketed clause, with the opening corner bracket only and no closing bracket in either scan (the ch. 3 lesson applies: unsettled scope in print, carried as a fork, never silently filled). The draft includes the whole clause with the ellipsis preserved.
- **Displaced "7c" and missing "h." — confirmed as print fact:** print labels the v. 6 clauses a–j with "7c." explicitly inserted between "c." and "6d."; after "6d." the "6" prefix drops (bare "e.", "f.", "g.", "i.", "j.") and there is **no "h." label** — the sequence jumps g.→i.; after "7a." the "7" prefix drops (bare "b."). - **Thick type — none in ch. 5:** no word in the main text of pp. 10–13 prints in thick type in either scan, calibrated at G1 against the p. 10 footnote's bold lemma "He that liveth" (the emendation note for v. 1 — Charles's footnote, not main text, and not a reading-text claim). No emended word in ch. 5; nothing was absorbed or excluded under the standing bracket rules in this draft.
- **"joy" → "grace" correction (v. 7a):** the drafting transcription read "light and **joy** and peace"; both 1912 scans read "light and **grace** and peace". The base and draft now follow the 1912 print. Material correction recorded; whether the 1917 edition differs is not decided here (cited distinctly if ever used).

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 6:** the Fall begins — a new section opens (VI–XI) with its own italic title, "(a Noah fragment)". The doublet "beautiful and comely daughters" is carried as "beautiful daughters" — "comely" is archaic for the same sense; the collapse is disclosed here. The question whether doublets are kept in the reading text was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"children of the heaven" (v. 2):** draft drops the second "the" ("the children of heaven") as plain English; no sense change.
- **"beget us children" → "have children by them" (v. 2):** plain register; "beget" is archaic. "choose us wives" → "choose wives for ourselves" (the base's "us" is a dative of advantage, not "wives that are ours").
- **"imprecations" → "curses" (vv. 4, 5, 6):** plain register, consistent with the ch. 5 standing choice ("execrate" → "curse"). Recorded for the G3 term sweep: "imprecations / execration / curse".
- **"sware" → "swore" (v. 5):** spelling/archaism only. "bound themselves ... upon it" → "bound themselves ... to it" (v. 5); "upon it" → "on it" (v. 6, the mountain).
- **"summit" → "top" (v. 6):** plain register. "descended" → "came down".
- **"in the days" bracket (v. 6) — SETTLED at G1:** print shows single thin corner brackets ⌜in the days⌉ in both scans (the closing ⌝ verified at high zoom — it is not a superscript mark). Per the key on printed p. cxii, single thin corner brackets = words in the Greek but not in the Ethiopic. ## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 7

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 07" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_07), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Scan verification against the two IA 1912 copies (printed p. 18) performed at G1 — the transcription proved word-for-word accurate against both scans; no print-level corrections were needed, so the base below stands as transcribed.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter VII = vv. 1–6 exactly, on printed p. 18; "VIII. 1." begins on the same page immediately after v. 6. The chapter heading is inline bold "VII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER VII." is a normalization). Running heads: "The Book of Enoch" center, "[Sect. I" top right. No brackets of any kind, no thick-type (emended) words, no superscript footnote marks in the main text of vv. 1–6 — bold word numerals are typography only.

1. And all the others together with them took unto themselves wives, and each chose for himself one, and they began to go in unto them and to defile themselves with them, and they taught them charms and enchantments, and the cutting of roots, and made them acquainted with plants.
2. And they became pregnant, and they bare great giants, whose height was three thousand ells:
3. Who consumed all the acquisitions of men. And when men could no longer sustain them,
4. The giants turned against them and devoured mankind.
5. And they began to sin against birds, and beasts, and reptiles, and fish, and to devour one another's flesh, and drink the blood.
6. Then the earth laid accusation against the lawless ones.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And all the rest of them, together with the leaders, took wives for themselves, and each chose one for himself. And they began to go in to them and to make themselves unclean with them. And they taught them charms and enchantments, the cutting of roots, and showed them the plants.
2. And they became pregnant, and gave birth to great giants, whose height was three thousand ells:
3. They ate up all that men possessed. And when men could no longer feed them,
4. the giants turned on them and devoured mankind.
5. And they began to wrong the birds, the beasts, the reptiles, and the fish, and to eat one another's flesh and drink one another's blood.
6. Then the earth cried out, accusing the lawless ones.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 7:** continuation of the Fall narrative (VI–XI): the angels take wives, the giants are born, they devour men's goods, then men, then each other; the earth accuses them. The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none.
- **"the others" (v. 1):** the angels other than the leaders of ch. 6. The draft explicates minimally as "all the rest of them, together with the leaders" — the subject is the two hundred minus their chiefs, acting under the oath of ch. 6. Disclosed, not a sense change.
- **"took unto themselves wives" → "took wives for themselves" (v. 1):** archaism only. "defile themselves" → "make themselves unclean": plain register; disclosed. The question whether the Ge'ez-lemma fork below wants a reader-facing note was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"made them acquainted with plants" → "showed them the plants" (v. 1):** plain register. Kept is Charles's reading of the word as 'plants', against 'trees' — see below.
- **"the cutting of roots" (v. 1):** kept literal (root-cutting for potions/charms) — not modernized into 'herbalism', though that is the plain sense. The question whether an explicitation is wanted was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"bare" → "gave birth to" (v. 2):** archaism only. "three thousand ells" kept literal — no modern conversion applied. An ell is roughly a forearm's length; no exact figure is given here. The question whether a modern-equivalent note is wanted was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"acquisitions" → "all that men possessed" (v. 3):** plain register. "sustain" → "feed": plain register; disclosed.
- **"turned against" → "turned on" (v. 4):** plain register.
- **"sin against" → "wrong" (v. 5):** plain register; disclosed. The question whether "sinned against" is preferred for weight was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"devour" → "eat" (v. 5):** plain register, consistent with v. 4's "devoured" kept? — v. 4 keeps "devoured mankind" (the base word there is simple; the plain move was for the v. 5 pair). Recorded for the G3 term sweep: "devour / eat". The question whether v. 4 and v. 5 should match was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"drink the blood" → "drink one another's blood" (v. 5):** explicitation of whose blood (each other's). Disclosed. The question whether to restore the spare "drink the blood" was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"laid accusation against" → "cried out, accusing" (v. 6):** plain register, keeping the legal sense. Disclosed.
- **v. 1 — "Defile themselves" witness fork (Charles's PD footnote, sighted on the scans):** Charles notes "Defile themselves. So Gᵍˢ. E reads tadammarû (= 'unite themselves') corrupt (?) for jĕtgammanû = Gᵍˢ." The Ge'ez reading may be corrupt; Charles follows the Greek sense. The draft follows the printed translation; the lemma fork is recorded here, not resolved.
- **v. 1 — "Plants" (Charles's PD footnote):** "Plants (= βοτάνας Gˢ). Not 'trees' here. The Ethiopic has both meanings." The draft keeps "plants" with Charles; disclosed.
- **v. 1 — "Charms and enchantments" cross-refs (Charles's PD footnote):** cf. Wisd. 12⁴, 18¹³; Jos. Ant. viii. 2. 5; Bell. vii. 6. 3. Recorded as apparatus; not printed in the reading text.
- **v. 2 — the defective-text fork (Charles's PD footnote, sighted on the scans):** Charles's note states the E Gˢ text is defective here and "must be made good from Gˢ", which reads: 'And they bare unto them three kinds: first great giants, and the giants †begat the Naphilim, and to the Naphilim were† born the Eliûd, and they grew according to their greatness.' — the three classes (giants, Naphilim, Eliûd) going back to Gen. 6⁴, with the Greek forms γίγαντες = גברים, Ναφηλείμ = נפלים, 'Ελιούδ = אנשי השם. **But Charles's printed translation keeps the defective Ethiopic reading** ("they bare great giants, whose height was three thousand ells") and leaves the fuller reading in the footnote. The draft follows the printed translation; the longer Gˢ reading is recorded here as apparatus, not smuggled into the text. Charles obelized 'begat' (ἐτέκνωσαν) as corrupt — possibly for ἔκτειναν, or via an Aramaic corruption מולדין for מובדין ('destroyed') — and cites Jub. 7²¹⁻²² as built on this passage. The question whether a reader-facing note is wanted was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands; the lane does not emend Charles's text.
- **v. 2–3 — witness coverage fork (Charles's PD footnote):** "since Gˢ omits 7³, 4a, 5a, 6 (7⁴ᵇ, 5ᵇ are inserted after 8³) and E Gˢ omit portions of 7², both texts are here defective." The Syncellus Greek has a shorter ch. 7 than the Ethiopic; recorded as apparatus. The draft keeps the full Ethiopic span with Charles.
- **v. 3 — "And when" (Charles's PD footnote):** "(ὡς δέ Gˢ). E = ὥστε corrupt for ὡς δέ." The Ethiopic particle is corrupt against the Greek; recorded, not emended.
- **v. 5 — "Blood" (Charles's PD footnote):** "The eating of blood with the Jews was a great crime, Gen. 9⁴ Acts 15²⁰ Book of Jubilees 7²⁸, ²⁹ 21⁶, ¹⁸, below 98¹¹." Recorded as apparatus; not printed in the reading text.
- **Transcription vs print — NO differences:** the Wikisource transcription matched both printed scans word-for-word for vv. 1–6 (wording, punctuation, colon after "ells:", capital "Who" at v. 3, "one another's flesh"). No base corrections needed at G1 — first chapter of the lane to require none.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with Greek/Aramaic controls present in principle for the section and consulted here only through Charles's printed footnotes as verified on the scans. Any future claim of Greek-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 8

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 08" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_08), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 18–20 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; two print-level refinements adopted here (the leading apostrophe on 'Armârôs; v. 4's "heaven. . . ." pointing).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter VIII = vv. 1–4 exactly, spanning printed pp. 18–20; "IX. 1." begins on p. 20 immediately after v. 4. The chapter heading is inline bold "VIII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER VIII." is a normalization). Running heads: "The Book of Enoch" center, "[Sect. I" top right (p. 18–20); p. 19 carries the page-level running head "Chapters VII. 1—VIII. 3". **Thick type (Charles's emendations):** "the metals" (v. 1), "Ezêqêêl the knowledge" (v. 3). **Angle brackets ⟨ ⟩ (single-stroke, lighter — Charles's supply):** "⟨of the earth⟩" (v. 1), "⟨Araqiêl the signs of the earth, Shamsiêl the signs of the sun⟩" (v. 3). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(taught)" before "astrology" (v. 3). **Leading apostrophe** on "'Armârôs" (v. 3) — a ditto-mark standing for the elided verb "taught"; the transcription normalizes it away. 1. And Azâzêl taught men to make swords, and knives, and shields, and breastplates, and made known to them the metals ⟨of the earth⟩ and the art of working them, and bracelets, and ornaments, and the use of antimony, and the beautifying of the eyelids, and all kinds of costly stones, and all colouring tinctures.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And Azâzêl taught men to make swords, and knives, and shields, and breastplates. And he showed them the metals of the earth, and the craft of working them: bracelets, and ornaments, and the use of antimony, and the painting of the eyes, and all kinds of costly stones, and all colouring dyes.
2. And much godlessness rose up, and they committed fornication, and they were led astray, and grew corrupt in all their ways.
3. Semjâzâ taught spells and root-cuttings; Armârôs taught the undoing of spells; Barâqîjâl taught astrology; Kôkabêl taught the constellations; Ezêqêêl taught the knowledge of the clouds; ⟨Araqiêl the signs of the earth, Shamsiêl the signs of the sun⟩; and Sariêl taught the course of the moon.
4. And as men were dying out, they cried aloud, and their cry went up to heaven. . . .

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 8:** the catalogue of forbidden teachings continues: Azâzêl's war-craft, metallurgy, and cosmetics (v. 1); the moral result (v. 2); each leader's specialty — spells, unspelling, astrology, the sky-signs (v. 3); man's broken cry rising to heaven (v. 4, broken in the print — see the ". . . ."). The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none.
- **"made known" → "showed" (v. 1):** plain register. **"the art of working them" → "the craft of working them" (v. 1):** plain register; "art" kept out of the modern "art" ambiguity. **"the beautifying of the eyelids" → "the painting of the eyes" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed — this is Charles's rendering of the antimony/cosmetics clause (see his Antimony note below). **"colouring tinctures" → "colouring dyes" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed. The question of all four, and on "craft" vs "art" was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"the metals" in thick type (v. 1):** Charles's own emendation — marked in the worksheet per the ch. 2 standing rule. His note (sighted on the scans): the Ge'ez twice handles the phrase corruptly (here τὰ μετ᾽ αὐτά for τὰ μέταλλα; at verse-end taulâta, a transliteration of τὰ μέταλλα, with τῆς γῆς appended), while Gˢ reads only τὰ †μεγάλα. The draft keeps the reading; whether the reading text should signal the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"⟨of the earth⟩" (v. 1):** Charles's supply from Gˢ, printed in angle brackets. The draft folds it in as "the metals of the earth" without visible brackets — a plain-text decision that follows the print sense exactly. Whether reader-facing brackets (or a note) are wanted stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"there arose" → "rose up" (v. 2):** plain register. **"became corrupt" → "grew corrupt" (v. 2):** plain register. "fornication" kept — term sweep (G3) item; the question whether a plainer word ("unfaithfulness"/"sexual sins") is wanted was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"enchantments" → "spells" (v. 3):** plain register, consistent with ch. 7's "charms and enchantments" (which the draft kept as "charms and enchantments" — a mismatch to be resolved at the G3 term sweep; recorded).
- **"root-cuttings" kept (v. 3):** matches the ch. 7 G4 item on "the cutting of roots" (ch. 7 v. 1); the two forms ("cutting of roots" / "root-cuttings") stand in the base and are kept as they stand, with the G3 sweep to decide one form.
- **"'Armârôs" — the leading apostrophe is a ditto-mark (v. 3):** it stands for the elided verb "taught" ("Semjâzâ taught … , [taught] Armârôs the resolving …"). The transcription drops it; the draft restores the verb explicitly in plain syntax ("Armârôs taught the undoing of spells"). Disclosed. The question whether the restoration is wanted or the elided form preferred was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"the resolving of enchantments" → "the undoing of spells" (v. 3):** plain register; disclosed. Charles's note: the word is corrupt; he derives it from חָבַר ("to join/spell-bind"), with the function ἐπαοιδῶν λυτήριον ("the undoing of incantations"); cf. Dan. 5:12 מְשָׁרֵא קִטְרִין = "the resolving of spells", and 95:4 below ("anathemas that cannot be resolved"). Recorded as apparatus. The question of the rendering was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"(taught)" — Charles's supplied verb (v. 3):** kept in the draft as plain "taught"; the elided "[taught]"s for the other leaders are the draft's plain syntax, disclosed here. The question whether the brackets should show was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"Ezêqêêl the knowledge" in thick type (v. 3):** Charles's own emendation — marked per the standing rule. His note (sighted): the Ge'ez here reads "Tamiel" (corrupt), though it gives Êzêqêêl rightly in 6:7; Gˢ is also corrupt (Σαθὴλ for Ζακιὴλ or Ἔξεκιὴλ). Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"the knowledge of the clouds" (v. 3):** Charles's note: the underlying reading is ἀεροσκοπίαν ("observation of the sky/air") corrupt from ἀστεροσκοπίαν in Gˢ/E; i.e. sky-reading, not weather-forecasting alone. The draft keeps "the knowledge of the clouds" with Charles; an explicitation ("reading the sky") stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"⟨Araqiêl the signs of the earth, Shamsiêl the signs of the sun⟩" (v. 3):** supplied from Gˢ (Charles: "save that for ὁ τρίτος and ὁ ἕβδομος I have given the names these numbers represent"); the Ge'ez lacks the pair. The draft keeps the pair visible in brackets; the two names' own corruption is noted in the apparatus only. Whether reader-facing brackets are wanted stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"Sariêl" (v. 3):** Charles's note: E reads Esdrĕêl (corrupt); Gˢ Σεριή(λ); see the 6:7 note. Kept with Charles. Leader-name spellings across ch. 6–8 ("Semjâzâ" here vs ch. 6's "Sêmîazâz" with circumflex ê; "Sariêl" here vs ch. 6's thick-type "Sariêl."; "Kôkabêl" here vs ch. 6's "Kôkabêl") are recorded for the G3 term sweep — do not harmonize now.
- **v. 4 — the broken ending ("heaven. . . ."):** the print ends the verse with period + spaced dots, marking a broken/lacunose text — the apparatus says the cry "may be a conflation" (E: ἐβόησαν καὶ ἀνέβη ἡ βοὴ αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; Gˢ omits ἐβόησαν καί; Gˢ¹² reads ἐβόησαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν). Gˢ² adds the longer clause: "+ 'saying, Bring our cause before the Most High and our destruction before the Great Glory, before the Lord of all the lords in greatness'". The draft keeps the dots, signaling the break; the Gˢ² clause is recorded here as apparatus, not imported. The question of keeping the dots in the reading text was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"they cried" → "they cried aloud" (v. 4):** plain register; disclosed. **"as men perished" → "as men were dying out" (v. 4):** plain register; disclosed.
- **Displaced half-verses (Charles's ch. 7 note):** Gˢ omits 7:3, 4a, 5a, 6; "7⁴ᵇ, 5ᵇ are inserted after 8³" — in the Syncellus order those fragments sit after 8:3. The 1912 *printed text* of ch. 8 does not show any insertion in the main text (v. 4 reads as above); the displacement lives in the apparatus only. Recorded, not acted on.
- **v. 1 — the longer Gˢ reading (Charles's PD footnote, sighted on the scans):** Gˢ gives v. 3's material as a fuller Azazel catalogue: "'First Azazel — the tenth of the leaders — taught (men) to make swords and breastplates and every kind of warlike arms, and the metals of the earth and the gold, how they were to work them and make them ornaments for the women, and the silver. And he showed them the art of using antimony (l. στιβίζειν for στίλβειν) and beautifying the face, and precious stones and colouring tinctures. And the children of men made (them) for themselves and their daughters and transgressed and led astray the holy ones.'" Charles then comments: "This last sentence is alien to the Book of Noah, and belongs rather to the Book of Jubilees and the Testaments. The latter books represent the daughters of men as seducing the angels by their ornaments, &c., whereas the older books declare that such arts were first introduced by the fallen angels." Recorded as apparatus; the translation follows the printed Ethiopic-based text and does not import the Gˢ form. The question whether a reader-facing note on the Gˢ form is wanted was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **v. 1 — Antimony (Charles's PD footnote, sighted):** "This mineral is referred to in the following excerpt from Tert. De Cultu Fem. i. 2, in which he lays under contribution this and the preceding chapter: 'Herbarum ingenia traduxerant et incantationum vires provulgaverant et omnem curiositatem usque ad stellarum interpretationem designaverant, proprie et quasi peculiariter feminis instrumentum istud muliebris gloriae contulerunt, lumina lapillorum quibus monilia variantur et circulos ex auro quibus brachia artantur — et illum ipsum nigrum pulverem quo oculorum exordia producuntur'"; and ii. 10: "'Quodsi iidem angeli qui et materias eiusmodi et illecebras detexerunt, auri dico et lapidum illustrium, et operas eorum tradiderunt, et iam ipsum calliblepharum — tincturas — docuerunt, ut Enoch refert.'" Cf. T. Reub. 5:5–6; also Is. 3:16–24 for the ornaments of women. Recorded as apparatus; not printed in the reading text.
- **v. 1 — Azâzêl name note (Charles's PD footnote, sighted):** "The origin of this word is unknown. See Encyc. Bib. in loc." **Breastplates note:** "+ διδάγματα ἀγγέλων Gˢ." Recorded as apparatus.
- **Transcription vs print — TWO refinements:** (1) the print carries a leading apostrophe on "'Armârôs" (v. 3), a ditto-mark for the elided verb "taught", which the transcription drops — adopted in the base above; (2) the print ends v. 4 with "heaven. . . ." (period + spaced dots), where the transcription spaced it as "heaven . . ." — adopted. Otherwise the transcription matched both scans (wording, punctuation, diacritics, the colon-free v. 2, "Semjâzâ", "Barâqîjâl (taught)", "Kôkabêl").
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with Greek/Aramaic controls present in principle for the section and consulted here only through Charles's printed footnotes as verified on the scans. Any future claim of Greek-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed.

I" top right (pp. 20–22); p. 21 carries the page-level running head "Chapters VIII. 4—IX. 10". **Thick type (Charles's emendations, invisible in the transcription):** "the Lord of the ages" (v. 4, outside the quoted prayer — distinguished from the bold quoted speech by position); "revealed the eternal" (v. 6); "cease" (v. 10). **Daggers † (corrupt):** "†without inhabitant cries the voice of their crying†" (v. 2). **Double corner brackets ⌜⌜ ⌝⌝ (Ethiopic-only reading, lost in the Syncellus stream through homoeoteleuton):** "⌜⌜And now to you, the holy ones of heaven⌝⌝," (v. 3). **Angle brackets ⟨ ⟩ (Charles's supply from Gˢ):** "⟨and God of the ages⟩" (v. 4). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(standeth)" (v. 4), "(preserved)" (v. 6). No single corner brackets, no [ ], no superscript footnote marks in the main text of vv. 1–11. Quoted speech is set in bold type throughout (vv. 2–4, 11) — typography, not emendation. Bold word numerals are typography only.

1. And then Michael, Uriel, Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw much blood being shed upon the earth, and all lawlessness being wrought upon the earth.
2. And they said one to another: 'The earth made †without inhabitant cries the voice of their crying† up to the gates of heaven.
3. ⌜⌜And now to you, the holy ones of heaven⌝⌝, the souls of men make their suit, saying, "Bring our cause before the Most High".'
4. And they said to **the Lord of the ages**: 'Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings, ⟨and God of the ages⟩, the throne of Thy glory (standeth) unto all the generations of the ages, and Thy name holy and glorious and blessed unto all the ages!
5. Thou hast made all things, and power over all things hast Thou: and all things are naked and open in Thy sight, and all things Thou seest, and nothing can hide itself from Thee.
6. Thou seest what Azâzêl hath done, who hath taught all unrighteousness on earth and **revealed the eternal** secrets which were (preserved) in heaven, which men were striving to learn:
7. And Semjâzâ, to whom Thou hast given authority to bear rule over his associates.
8. And they have gone to the daughters of men upon the earth, and have slept with the women, and have defiled themselves, and revealed to them all kinds of sins.
9. And the women have borne giants, and the whole earth has thereby been filled with blood and unrighteousness.
10. And now, behold, the souls of those who have died are crying and making their suit to the gates of heaven, and their lamentations have ascended: and cannot **cease**
11. And Thou knowest all things before they come to pass, and Thou seest these things and Thou dost suffer them, and Thou dost not say to us what we are to do to them in regard to these.'

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 1 "And then" — Charles's note reads "And then (E). Gˢ 'then'. + 'the four great archangels hearing' Gˢ¹,²"; the longer Gˢ clause is not imported. v. 2 line break "with- / out" in print; the transcription's "without" is the same word. v. 3's double corners are two-stroked on both opening and closing in both scans — genuinely double, not a scan artifact. v. 4: the words "the Lord of the ages" stand in the same heavy face as the quoted prayer but outside the quotation marks; Charles's note emends the E reading ("lords of kings", corrupt) to "Lord of the ages" from Gˢ¹ — thick type, marked above. The quoted prayer (bold) runs from "'Lord of lords" through v. 11's closing "these.'" v. 5 has no thick type: "Power over all things (E Gˢ)" per Charles's note. v. 6 "(preserved)" is Charles's round-bracket supply; the thick-type "revealed the eternal" rests on his long emendation discussion (see Notes). v. 7's main text prints plain "And" with NO visible angle brackets, though Charles's note reads "7. ⟨And.⟩ Supplied from Gˢ" — a print oddity, recorded, not acted on. v. 10 ends "and cannot **cease**" with no terminal period in print; the v. 10 note explains the emendation: "read ἐξελθεῖν = למנפק corrupt for למפסק = 'cease'. The lamentations must keep ascending to heaven without ceasing because of the deeds of violence on earth." v. 11 "knowest" prints in regular type (follows E against Gˢˢ "seest"); "dost suffer them" likewise regular (follows Gˢˢ against a corrupt E).

- **Ge'ez (Charles 1906, 23 MSS):** the ultimate source of Charles 1912. Not opened as an independent control column here — Route A only.
- **Greek (Panopolitanus 1:1–32:6; Syncellus stream for this chapter):** control exists for this chapter in principle; Charles's sigla are Gᵍ (Panopolitanus), Gˢ (Syncellus-derived Greek) with Gˢ¹ / Gˢ² / Gˢˢ subgroups. No Greek wording independently transcribed in this lane; Greek-related notes are taken from Charles's own printed footnotes — here the v. 2 corruption fork, the v. 3 Ethiopic-only clause, the v. 4 "Lord of the ages" emendation, the v. 6 emendation discussion, the v. 7 "And" supply, the v. 8 idiom note, the v. 9 giant-name fork, the v. 10 "cease" emendation, and the v. 11 Gˢˢ readings (see Notes). None of the longer Gˢ forms is imported into the translation.
- **Aramaic (Qumran):** the Watchers section has Aramaic scraps (4Q201 covers parts of ch. 2–9). No Aramaic wording is claimed for ch. 9 here.
- **Laurence (1821, PD, check-only):** not consulted as a skeleton in this slice; Laurence's 105-chapter numbering is never mapped onto the 108.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Then Michael, Uriel, Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven. They saw much blood being shed on the earth, and all lawlessness being worked on the earth.
2. And they said to one another: "The earth made †without inhabitant cries the voice of their crying† up to the gates of heaven.
(Note: the mark † is Charles's. It stands where the ancient text has come down to us damaged or uncertain, so the reader can see where the ground is less firm. It is kept wherever Charles put it, here and through the whole book.)
3. ⌜⌜And now to you, the holy ones of heaven⌝⌝, the souls of men make their plea, saying, 'Bring our cause before the Most High.'"
4. And they said to the Lord of the ages: "Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings, ⟨and God of the ages⟩ — the throne of Your glory stands through all the generations of the ages, and Your name is holy and glorious and blessed through all the ages!
5. You have made all things, and power over all things is Yours. All things lie open and naked before Your eyes. You see everything, and nothing can hide from You.
6. You see what Azâzêl has done — he has taught all unrighteousness on earth, and revealed the eternal secrets that were kept in heaven, which men were striving to learn.
7. And Semjâzâ, to whom You have given authority to rule over his companions.
8. And they went to the daughters of men on the earth, and slept with the women, and defiled themselves, and showed them every kind of sin.
9. And the women bore giants, and because of them the whole earth was filled with blood and unrighteousness.
10. And now, look — the souls of those who have died are crying out and bringing their plea to the gates of heaven, and their cries of grief have gone up, and cannot cease.
11. And You know all things before they happen. You see these things, and You let them go on, and You do not tell us what we are to do with them."

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 9:** the intercession chapter — the four named archangels report the bloodshed, carry the souls' plea, and lay the charge before the Most High (Azâzêl's teachings, Semjâzâ's authority, the defilement, the giants, the unceasing cry of the dead). The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none. The chapter's long quotation (vv. 2–4, then the prayer to v. 11) is kept as one speech with the print's quote marks flattened to double quotes throughout — disclosed.
- **Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your (vv. 4–11):** plain register; the first chapter in the lane to address God directly, so this is the lane's first Thou-decision. "Thou hast" → "You have"; "hath done" → "has done"; "knowest" → "know"; "seest" → "see"; "dost suffer" → "let go on" (see below). Disclosed; the question whether "You" stands or the lane keeps "Thou" was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"And then" → "Then" (v. 1):** plain register. The Gˢ addition "'the four great archangels hearing' Gˢ¹,²" (Charles's PD footnote, sighted) is recorded as apparatus, not imported. The question of importing was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **v. 2 — the daggered clause:** the print marks "†without inhabitant cries the voice of their crying†" as corrupt; the draft keeps the daggers in the reading text (as ch. 8 kept the ". . . ." dots) and smooths only "cryings" → "crying". Charles's note (sighted): the E form is "The earth †made without inhabitant . . . heaven"; Gˢ reads "'the voice of them that cry upon the earth to the gates of heaven'"; Gˢ¹,² omit the clause; on "made without inhabitant" cf. 67², 84⁵, T. Naph. 3⁵. The draft does not adopt the Gˢ form — disclosed. The question of keeping the daggers and the clause was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"make their suit" → "make their plea" / "bringing their plea" (vv. 3, 10):** plain register; "suit" is a legal idiom. Kept consistent across the two verses; the G3 sweep may settle "plea" vs "petition".
- **Double corners ⌜⌜ ⌝⌝ (v. 3):** Charles's sign for a reading found in one tradition only — here Ethiopic-only (his note: "And now . . . heaven (E). Lost in Gˢˢ¹,² through hmt."). The draft keeps the clause visible in the double corners, following Charles's printed text. Whether the corners (or a note) are wanted for readers stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14. Charles's cross-refs (sighted): "Holy ones. See 1⁹ note. Most High. See 99³ note."
- **"the Lord of the ages" in thick type (v. 4):** Charles's own emendation — marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. His note (sighted): "Lord of the ages (Gˢ¹). > Gˢˢ². E = κυρίων τῶν βασιλέων, where τ. βασιλέων = מלכיא corrupt for עלמיא = τῶν αἰώνων." Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"⟨and God of the ages⟩" (v. 4):** Charles's supply from Gˢ, kept visible in the draft; his note adds that in Gˢ² ἀνθρώπων is corrupt for αἰώνων. Whether reader-facing brackets (or a note) are wanted stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14. Charles's cross-refs (sighted): "Lord of lords, God of gods. So in Deut. 10¹⁷. The prayer of the angels is fuller in Gˢ, and still more in 84²,³." — cross-references are footnoted in the apparatus only, as built.
- **"(standeth)" → "stands" (v. 4):** Charles's round-bracket supply absorbed into plain English per the ch. 1 standing rule; disclosed.
- **"unto all the generations of the ages" → "through all the generations of the ages" (v. 4):** plain register; "unto" is archaic. "and Thy name holy and glorious and blessed unto all the ages" → "and Your name is holy and glorious and blessed through all the ages" — the verb "is" supplied for plain syntax; disclosed.
- **v. 5 plain moves:** "Thou hast made all things, and power over all things hast Thou" → "You have made all things, and power over all things is Yours"; "all things are naked and open in Thy sight" → "All things lie open and naked before Your eyes"; "and all things Thou seest, and nothing can hide itself from Thee" → "You see everything, and nothing can hide from You". The verse is split into three plain sentences; no sense changed. Charles's note (sighted): "Power over all things (E Gˢ). Gˢ = 'all power'." — apparatus only. The question of the moves was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"revealed the eternal" in thick type (v. 6):** Charles's own emendation — marked in the base per the standing rule. His long note (sighted) walks the corruption: E is "very corrupt" ("the eternal secrets which are wrought in the heaven mankind knows"); the emended Ge'ez reads "'the eternal secrets which were wrought in the heaven' ... transposed after 'in the heaven'" with 'a'ĕmara emended to 'a'ĕmrô = γνῶναι or εἰδέαι; thus "E agrees with Gˢ" whose reading is "'revealed to the world the things that are (preserved) in heaven. And the children of men are practising his (Azazel's) practices in order to know the mysteries'". The draft follows Charles's printed main line and does not import the fuller Gˢ clause — disclosed. Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14. Charles's hmt note: "Thou seest. Lost in Gᵍ through hmt." — recorded.
- **"(preserved)" → "kept" (v. 6):** Charles's round-bracket supply absorbed per the ch. 1 standing rule ("the eternal secrets that were kept in heaven"); disclosed. The question whether "preserved" should stand was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"striving to learn" kept (v. 6):** the base's "which men were striving to learn" stands; no plainer floor found that doesn't lose the reaching sense. G3 item.
- **v. 7 — the unbracketed "And":** Charles's note reads "7. ⟨And.⟩ Supplied from Gˢ", but the printed main text carries NO visible angle brackets — a print oddity verified in both scans. The draft prints plain "And". Recorded; the discrepancy is print fact, not a transcription error. The question whether a note flags it for readers was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"to bear rule over his associates" → "to rule over his companions" (v. 7):** plain register; disclosed.
- **v. 8 plain moves:** "have gone to" → "went to"; "upon the earth" → "on the earth"; "revealed to them all kinds of sins" → "showed them every kind of sin". Disclosed. Charles's idiom note (sighted): "With the women. Here E = μετ᾽ αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν θηλειῶν — the literal rendering of an Aramaic idiom = עמהין עם נשיא = 'with the women'. Gˢ not understanding this idiom divided the phrase into two parts, and connected them with different verbs συνεκοιμήθησαν μετ᾽ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐν ταῖς θηλείαις ἐμάνθησαν. Gˢ omitted the latter half of the phrase and read αὐταῖς after συνεκοιμήθησαν." Recorded as apparatus.
- **v. 8 — the Gˢ addition:** "All kinds of sins. + 'and have taught them to make hate-producing charms' (Gˢ). But as Martin suggests μίσητρα is possibly corrupt for μισητίαν. Hence 'taught them to practise lewdness'." Recorded as apparatus, not imported. The question of a reader-facing note was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **v. 9 plain moves:** "have borne" → "bore"; "has thereby been filled" → "was filled"; "thereby" → "because of them". Disclosed. Charles's giant-name note (sighted): "Giants. Gᵍ reads τιτᾶνας, Gˢ γίγαντας." Recorded; the draft keeps "giants" with Charles.
- **"And now, behold" → "And now, look" (v. 10):** plain register, matching ch. 1's "Look!" for "And behold!". "their lamentations have ascended" → "their cries of grief have gone up" — plain; disclosed.
- **"cease" in thick type (v. 10):** Charles's own emendation — marked in the base per the standing rule. His note (sighted): "read ἐξελθεῖν = למנפק corrupt for למפסק = 'cease'. The lamentations must keep ascending to heaven without ceasing because of the deeds of violence on earth." The print ends the verse with no terminal period after "cease" — kept as print fact. Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14. Charles's intercession note (sighted; cross-references are kept in the apparatus only, as built): "10–11. The intercession of the angels on man's behalf, which appears in this chapter and is found also in 15² 40⁶ 47² 99³,¹⁶ 104¹, is an O.T. doctrine; cf. Job 5¹ 33²³ Zech. 1¹²."
- **v. 11 plain moves:** "knowest all things before they come to pass" → "know all things before they happen"; "Thou dost suffer them" → "You let them go on" ("suffer" = permit; disclosed); "Thou dost not say to us what we are to do to them in regard to these" → "You do not tell us what we are to do with them". Disclosed. The print follows E's "knowest" against Gˢˢ "seest" ("11. Seest (Gˢˢ). E 'knowest'") and follows Gˢˢ for "dost suffer them" against a corrupt E ("Dost suffer them (Gˢˢ). E = τὰ εἰς αὐτούς corrupt for ἕας αὐτούς") — recorded as apparatus; the draft follows Charles's main line. The question of "let them go on" vs "allow them" was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"unrighteousness" (vv. 6, 9):** kept, not flattened to "wrongdoing" — G3 term item (against ch. 8's "godlessness", a different word).
- **"lawlessness" (v. 1):** kept; G3 item.
- **"the Most High" (vv. 3, 10):** kept as a standing title; G3 item.
- **"Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings" (v. 4):** kept verbatim — a liturgical formula (Charles cites Deut. 10:17); flattening it would lose the parallelism. G3 item.
- **"holy ones of heaven" (v. 3):** kept; G3 item ("holy ones" title across the book).
- **"revealed" (vv. 6, 8):** ch. 8 used "showed" for "made known"; here "revealed" is Charles's own word in both verses (v. 8's "revealed to them all kinds of sins" → "showed them every kind of sin"). The v. 6/v. 8 "revealed" pair is recorded for the G3 sweep — do not harmonize now.
- **"defiled themselves" (v. 8):** kept — matches ch. 7's G4 item on "defile / unclean"; the G3 sweep will settle one form.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with Greek/Aramaic controls present in principle for the section and consulted here only through Charles's printed footnotes as verified on the scans. Any future claim of Greek-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed.

# WORKSHEET — 1 Enoch, Chapter 10

> DRAFT — clear-English rendering prepared with AI assistance; a translation of a translation (Ge'ez from lost Hebrew/Aramaic and Greek stages); not reviewed by a Ge'ez scholar; not finished.
