## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 10

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 10" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_10), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 22–26 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below. Material transcription-vs-print corrections (the print is the authority): the transcription's "〈'Go to Noah and〉" carries a spurious leading curly quote — the print reads "⟨Go to Noah and⟩"; the transcription's v. 16 "a blessing; the works" uses a semicolon — the print reads "a blessing: the works". Five thick-type emendations invisible in the transcription were settled on the scans and are marked in the base below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter X = vv. 1–22 exactly, spanning printed pp. 22–26; "XI. 1." begins on p. 26 immediately after v. 22. The chapter heading is inline bold "X. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER X." is a normalization). Running heads: "The Book of Enoch" center, "[Sect. I" top right (pp. 22–26); p. 23 carries the page-level running head "Chapters IX. 11—X. 9"; p. 25 carries "Chapter X. 10–18". **Thick type (Charles's emendations, invisible in the transcription):** "**Uriel**" (v. 1); "**approaching**" (v. 2 — extra-heavy against the bold quoted-speech face in both scans; no footnote explanation on the visible pages, recorded as print fact); "**deluge**" (v. 2 — extra-heavy against the bold quoted-speech face in both scans); "**disclosed**" (v. 7); "**bind**" (v. 11 — δῆσον Gˢ, against Gᵍ E δήλωσον, a corruption native to Gᵍ; extra-heavy in both scans); "**valleys**" (v. 12); "**condemned**" (v. 14); "**old age**" (v. 17 — extra-heavy in regular-type narration in both scans; the footnote presents the τὰ σάββατα αὐτῶν = שַׁבְּתֹתָם misvocalization for שַׂבְתָּם = τὸ γῆρας αὐτῶν). The last three ("approaching", "bind", "old age") were settled on an independent coordinator re-verification of the scans after Worker A's G1, which had recorded only five. **Single thin corner brackets ⌜ ⌝ (witness-divergence flag; the footnote gives the direction):** "⌜and it shall prove a blessing: the works of righteousness and truth⌝" (v. 16 — single-stroked opening and closing, verified at 3× on both scans); "⌜And all the children of men shall become righteous⌝" (v. 21 — single). **Angle brackets ⟨ ⟩ (Charles's supply, usually from Gˢ):** "⟨Go to Noah and⟩" (v. 2); "⟨and⟩" (v. 13). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial/dittograph):** "[the children of fornication and]" (v. 9 — a dittograph); "[and cause them to go forth]" (v. 9). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(i. e. their fathers)" (v. 10); "(them)" (v. 22). No daggers †, no double corners in vv. 1–22. Quoted speech is set in bold type throughout — typography, not emendation.

1. Then said the Most High, the Holy and Great One spake, and sent **Uriel** to the son of Lamech, and said to him:
2. '⟨Go to Noah and⟩ tell him in my name "Hide thyself!", and reveal to him the end that is **approaching**: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a **deluge** is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.
3. And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.'
4. And again the Lord said to Raphael: 'Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness: and make an opening in the desert, which is in Dûdâêl, and cast him therein.
5. And place upon him rough and jagged rocks, and cover him with darkness, and let him abide there for ever, and cover his face that he may not see light.
6. And on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire.
7. And heal the earth which the angels have corrupted, and proclaim the healing of the earth, that they may heal the plague, and that all the children of men may not perish through all the secret things that the Watchers have **disclosed** and have taught their sons.
8. And the whole earth has been corrupted through the works that were taught by Azâzêl: to him ascribe all sin.'
9. And to Gabriel said the Lord: 'Proceed against the bastards and the reprobates, and against the children of fornication: and destroy [the children of fornication and] the children of the Watchers from amongst men: [and cause them to go forth]: send them one against the other that they may destroy each other in battle: for length of days shall they not have.
10. And no request that they (i. e. their fathers) make of thee shall be granted unto their fathers on their behalf; for they hope to live an eternal life, and that each one of them will live five hundred years.'
11. And the Lord said unto Michael: 'Go, **bind** Semjâzâ and his associates who have united themselves with women so as to have defiled themselves with them in all their uncleanness.
12. And, when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the **valleys** of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated.
13. In those days they shall be led off to the abyss of fire: ⟨and⟩ to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever.
14. And whosoever shall be **condemned** and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations.
15. And destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.
16. Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: ⌜and it shall prove a blessing: the works of righteousness and truth⌝ shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.
17. And then shall all the righteous escape,
And shall live till they beget thousands of children,
And all the days of their youth and their **old age** shall they complete in peace.
18. And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.
19. And all desirable trees shall be planted on it, and they shall plant vines on it: and the vine which they plant thereon shall yield wine in abundance, and as for all the seed which is sown thereon each measure (of it) shall bear a thousand, and each measure of olives shall yield ten presses of oil.
20. And cleanse thou the earth from all oppression, and from all unrighteousness, and from all sin, and from all godlessness: and all the uncleanness that is wrought upon the earth destroy from off the earth.
21. ⌜And all the children of men shall become righteous⌝, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me.
22. And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment, and from all torment, and I will never again send (them) upon it from generation to generation and for ever.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 1 "Uriel" is thick type — Charles's note (sighted): "Uriel (Gˢ). Gᵍ 'Ἰστραήλ'. E is corrupt." v. 2 "deluge" is thick type; the note (sighted) discusses the flood-wording. The angle-bracketed "⟨Go to Noah and⟩" is Charles's restoration from Gˢ ("πορεύου πρὸς τὸν Νῶε καί"), "already lost in the archetype of E" — and the print's French-spacing „ " quotation marks (" Hide thyself! ") are a print normalization, recorded. The v. 2 main text prints plain "And" though the note reads "⟨And.⟩" as supplied — the same print oddity as ch. 9 v. 7, recorded, not acted on. v. 7 "disclosed" is thick type — Charles's note (sighted) walks the corruption: "E Gˢˢ have here ἐπάταξαν = אכדן corrupt for אמרו = εἶπον which we find in Gˢ." v. 9's square brackets mark a dittograph ("[the children of fornication and]") and a duplicate rendering ("[and cause them to go forth]") — the note (sighted) explains the πέμψον duplicate. v. 12 "valleys" is thick type — the note (sighted): "Valleys (νάπαι Gˢˢ). E reads 'hills'." v. 13 "⟨and⟩" is Charles's supply. v. 14 "condemned" is thick type — the note (sighted): "Condemned (Gˢ). Gᵍ E read κατακαυσθῇ corrupt for κατακριθῇ." v. 16's corner brackets are single-stroked (both strokes, 3×, both scans) — the transcription carries them identically; the note (sighted) reads "After these words Gˢ omits through hmt. καὶ ἔσται εὐλογία· τὰ ἔργα τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας, which are preserved by E." v. 17 "old age" prints in thick type (extra-heavy in regular-type narration in both scans — corrected at coordinator re-verification) — the note (sighted) discusses the vocalization (τὰ σάββατα αὐτῶν = שַׁבְּתֹתָם, wrongly vocalized for שַׂבְתָּם = τὸ γῆρας αὐτῶν). v. 21's corners are single — the note (sighted): "And all the children of men shall become righteous (E). > Gˢ." The single corners in this chapter (vv. 16, 21) mark clauses where the witnesses diverge and the footnote gives the direction — here E-attested, Gˢ-omitted; see the "Corner-bracket finding" in the Notes. The v. 22 "(them)" is Charles's round-bracket supply.

No Greek wording independently transcribed in this lane; Greek-related notes are taken from Charles's own printed footnotes — here the v. 1 Uriel/Israel fork, the v. 2 "Go to Noah" restoration, the v. 3 Gˢ fullness, the v. 4 Azazel/Dudael note, the v. 7 "disclosed" corruption, the v. 11 "bind" (δῆσον) corruption, the v. 12 "valleys"/"hills" fork, the v. 14 "condemned"/"burnt" fork, and the v. 16 hmt-omission (see Notes). ## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Then the Most High spoke — the Holy and Great One — and sent **Uriel** to the son of Lamech, and said to him:
2. "⟨Go to Noah and⟩ tell him in my name, 'Hide yourself!' Show him the end that is coming: the whole earth will be destroyed, and a **flood** is about to come on the whole earth and destroy everything on it.
3. Teach him now, so he can escape and his line can be kept alive through all the generations of the world."
4. And again the Lord said to Raphael: "Tie up Azâzêl hand and foot and throw him into the darkness. Open up a pit in the desert — in Dûdâêl — and throw him into it.
5. Pile rough, jagged rocks on him, cover him with darkness, and let him stay there for ever. Cover his face so he cannot see light.
6. On the day of the great judgement he will be thrown into the fire.
7. Heal the earth that the angels have ruined, and proclaim the healing of the earth, so they can heal the plague and none of the children of men perish because of all the secret things the Watchers have **disclosed** and taught their sons.
8. The whole earth has been ruined by the works Azâzêl taught. Lay all sin on him."
9. And to Gabriel the Lord said: "Move against the bastards and the outcasts, and against the children of fornication. Destroy [the children of fornication and] the children of the Watchers from among men [and cause them to go forth]: send them against each other so they kill each other in battle, for they will not live long.
10. No plea they make to you — their fathers — will be granted to their fathers for them, for they hope to live for ever, and each of them to live five hundred years."
11. And the Lord said to Michael: "Go, tie up Semjâzâ and his companions, who joined themselves to women and defiled themselves with them in all their uncleanness.
12. When their sons have killed each other and they have seen their loved ones destroyed, tie them fast for seventy generations in the **valleys** of the earth, till the day of their judgement and their end, till the judgement that lasts for ever and ever is complete.
13. In those days they will be led away to the lake of fire — ⟨and⟩ to the torment and the prison where they will be shut up for ever.
14. And whoever is **condemned** and destroyed will from then on be tied up with them to the end of all generations.
15. Destroy all the spirits of the outcasts and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.
16. Wipe all wrong off the face of the earth and bring every evil work to an end. Let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: ⌜it will be a blessing — the works of righteousness and truth⌝ will be planted in truth and joy for evermore.
17. Then all who do right will escape,
and live till they have thousands of children,
and complete all the days of their youth and their old age in peace.
18. Then the whole earth will be farmed in righteousness, planted with trees everywhere, and full of blessing.
19. Every good tree will be planted on it, and they will plant vines on it. The vine they plant there will yield wine in plenty, and for every seed sown there each measure will bear a thousand, and each measure of olives will yield ten presses of oil.
20. Cleanse the earth of all oppression, all unrighteousness, all sin, all godlessness. Destroy from off the earth all the uncleanness worked on the earth.
21. ⌜And all the children of men will become righteous⌝ — all nations will bow down and praise Me, and all will worship Me.
22. The earth will be cleansed of all defilement, all sin, all punishment, all torment, and I will never again send (them) on it, from generation to generation, for ever."

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 10:** the four commissions — Uriel warns Noah (vv. 1–3), Raphael binds Azâzêl (vv. 4–8), Gabriel destroys the giants (vv. 9–10), Michael binds Semjâzâ (vv. 11–15) — then the purged-earth/Messianic aftermath (vv. 16–22). The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none. The v. 17 verse-lines are kept as lines.
- **Corner-bracket finding (G1, both scans):** the single thin corners ⌜ ⌝ in this chapter (v. 16 "and it shall prove a blessing: the works of righteousness and truth"; v. 21 "And all the children of men shall become righteous") are verified single-stroked on the print (v. 16 at 3×, both strokes, both scans). Charles's footnotes attribute both clauses to E with Gˢ omitting (v. 16: "preserved by E", Gˢ omits through hmt; v. 21: "(E). > Gˢ"). This does not fit the ch. 2 standing gloss ("single = Greek-not-Ethiopic") on its face; across ch. 10–36 the single corners prove to be a bidirectional witness-divergence flag, with the footnote giving the direction (see the block-level finding recorded at ch. 14). Recorded as print fact + verbatim footnote; flagged for G2/Robert. The draft keeps the cornered words visible per the lane rule. Whether reader-facing corners (or a note) are wanted stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"spake" → "spoke" (v. 1):** plain register. "Then said the Most High, the Holy and Great One spake" → "Then the Most High spoke — the Holy and Great One —". Disclosed;
- **"Uriel" in thick type (v. 1):** Charles's own emendation — marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. His note (sighted): "Uriel (Gˢ). Gᵍ 'Ἰστραήλ'. E is corrupt." Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"⟨Go to Noah and⟩" (v. 2):** Charles's restoration from Gˢ, kept visible; his note (sighted) explains it was "already lost in the archetype of E" and that each command begins with "go". The transcription's spurious leading curly quote is corrected to the print. Whether reader-facing brackets are wanted stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"Hide thyself!" → "Hide yourself!" (v. 2):** Thou→You per the ch. 9 decision; disclosed;
- **"deluge" in thick type → "flood" (v. 2):** Charles's emendation marked in the base; the draft renders it "flood" for plain register — disclosed; the G3 sweep may settle "deluge" vs "flood".
- **"therein" → "into it" (v. 4); "abide" → "stay" (v. 5); "ascribe" → "lay on him" (v. 8):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"approaching" in thick type (v. 2):** settled on enlarged crops in both scans (extra-heavy against the bold quoted-speech face), added at coordinator re-verification; no footnote explanation on the visible pages — recorded as print fact. The draft renders it plainly ("the end that is coming"). Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"disclosed" in thick type (v. 7):** Charles's emendation — marked in the base. His note (sighted) walks the corruption (ἐπάταξαν corrupt for εἶπον, found in Gˢ). Whether the reading text signals it stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"bind" in thick type (v. 11):** settled on enlarged crops in both scans (extra-heavy against the bold quoted-speech face), added at coordinator re-verification. Charles's note (sighted): "Bind (i.e. δῆσον Gˢ). Gᵍ E read δήλωσον, a corruption native to Gᵍ." Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"old age" in thick type (v. 17):** settled on enlarged crops in both scans (extra-heavy in regular-type narration — v. 17 is not quoted speech), added at coordinator re-verification; Worker A's G1 had recorded it as regular type. Charles's note (sighted) presents the emendation: "Here Gᵍ E have τὰ σάββατα αὐτῶν = שַׁבְּתֹתָם in which the word is wrongly vocalized for שַׂבְתָּם = τὸ γῆρας αὐτῶν. The error could also be explained in Hebrew." Whether the reading text signals it stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"the bastards and the reprobates" (v. 9):** kept — Charles's words; flattening would lose the charge. G3 items.
- **The v. 9 square brackets:** "[the children of fornication and]" (dittograph) and "[and cause them to go forth]" (duplicate rendering) are kept visible in the draft per the lane rule; Charles's note (sighted) explains the dittograph and the πέμψον duplicate. Whether reader-facing brackets are wanted stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"(i. e. their fathers)" → "their fathers" (v. 10):** Charles's gloss absorbed per the ch. 1 standing rule; disclosed. "make of thee" → "make to you"; "thee" → "you" (Thou→You).
- **"Go, bind" → "Go, tie up" (v. 11); "united themselves" kept; "defiled themselves" kept (matches ch. 7–9 G4 item):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"beloved ones" → "loved ones" (v. 12); "valleys" in thick type (v. 12):** Charles's emendation marked in the base (E reads "hills"). Whether the reading text signals it stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14. "consummation" → "end"/"complete" (vv. 12, 14) — plain; the G3 sweep may settle "consummation".
- **"the abyss of fire" → "the lake of fire" (v. 13):** plain register — "abyss" is kept at 12:5–6 but here the fire-context favors "lake"; disclosed. The G3 sweep may settle one form. Referred to the editor's read-through and closed there on 2026-10-14. "⟨and⟩" kept visible. "confined" → "shut up".
- **"whosoever" → "whoever" (v. 14); "thenceforth" → "from then on" (v. 14); "condemned" in thick type (v. 14):** Charles's emendation marked in the base. Whether signalled stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"the spirits of the reprobate" (v. 15):** kept; G3 item. "wronged mankind" kept — plain enough.
- **"prove a blessing" → "be a blessing" (v. 16):** plain register; disclosed. The cornered clause is kept visible.
- **"plant of righteousness" (v. 16):** kept — a standing image (cf. 93:2, 5, 10); G3 item.
- **"tilled" (v. 18):** kept — "farmed" would lose the Messianic-agriculture echo; disclosed. G3 item.
- **"thereon" → "there"/"on it" (v. 19); "wrought" → "worked" (v. 20):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"cleanse thou" → "cleanse" (v. 20):** imperative flattened; disclosed. "oppression", "unrighteousness", "godlessness" kept — G3 items.
- **"offer adoration" → "bow down" (v. 21):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"(them)" (v. 22):** Charles's round-bracket supply kept visible; disclosed.
- **"the Most High", "the Holy and Great One", "the Lord" (titles):** kept throughout; G3 items.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with Greek/Aramaic controls present in principle for the section and consulted here only through Charles's printed footnotes as verified on the scans. Any future claim of Greek-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed.

## G1 Audit Record — Chapter 10 (performed 2026-10-11, this slice)

**Scope of audit (per checkpoint):** fidelity to Charles 1912; verse-by-verse comparison of the draft against the base; scan verification of the base on printed pp. 22–26 in two independent scans of the 1912 edition (IA `bookofenochor1en00char`, BookReader leaves n137–n141 = printed pp. 22–26, page images via the `/page/nNNN.jpg` endpoint; IA `cu31924067146773` Cornell copy, same leaves, same endpoint); heading form; bracket, dagger, and thick-type check per the standing rules; Charles footnotes sighted (v. 1 Uriel; v. 2 Go-to-Noah restoration; v. 3 Gˢ fullness; v. 4 Dudael; v. 5 seventy-generations; v. 6 judgement-day; v. 7 disclosed-corruption; v. 8 Azazel-works; vv. 9–10 Jubilees/dittograph; v. 11 bind-corruption; v. 12 valleys/hills + Jude 6; v. 13 fire-lake; v. 14 condemned-corruption; v. 15 commission-note; v. 16 hmt-omission + plant-catena; v. 17 old-age vocalization; vv. 18–19 chiliastic; v. 20 oppression; v. 21 Gentile-conversion; v. 22 earth/upon-it).

**Findings:**

1. **Completeness and fidelity (text level):** 22 of 22 verses drafted; nothing omitted, added, or reordered. Plain-register moves, all recorded in the Notes. No sense added beyond the disclosed moves.
2. **Chapter span, heading — SETTLED on both scans:** Chapter X = vv. 1–22 exactly, spanning printed pp. 22–26; "XI. 1." begins on p. 26 immediately after v. 22. Inline bold "X. 1." heading run into the text — the transcription's display "CHAPTER X." is a normalization, corrected. P. 23's page-level running head is "Chapters IX. 11—X. 9"; p. 25's is "Chapter X. 10–18"; other running heads "The Book of Enoch" center, "[Sect. I" top right. PASS.
3. **Brackets, daggers, thick type — SETTLED:** thick type (Charles's emendations) on "**Uriel**" (v. 1), "**approaching**" (v. 2), "**deluge**" (v. 2), "**disclosed**" (v. 7), "**bind**" (v. 11), "**valleys**" (v. 12), "**condemned**" (v. 14), "**old age**" (v. 17) — all eight confirmed on both scans (the transcription marks none of them); the last three were settled on the coordinator's independent re-verification of the enlarged scan crops after Worker A's G1 (which had recorded five and "old age" as regular) — "approaching" and "old age" have no footnote explanation on the visible pages, "bind" rests on the note "Bind (i.e. δῆσον Gˢ). Gᵍ E read δήλωσον, a corruption native to Gᵍ", and "old age" rests on the τὰ σάββατα/שַׁבְּתֹתָם misvocalization note; all recorded as print fact. Single thin corner brackets ⌜ ⌝ (single-stroked, both strokes verified at 3× on both scans) on the v. 16 clause and the v. 21 clause; angle brackets ⟨ ⟩ on "⟨Go to Noah and⟩" (v. 2) and "⟨and⟩" (v. 13), both scans; square brackets [ ] on the v. 9 dittograph and duplicate rendering, both scans; round parentheses on "(i. e. their fathers)" (v. 10) and "(them)" (v. 22), both scans; no daggers, no double corners in vv. 1–22; quoted speech in bold type throughout (typography, not emendation). PASS.
4. **Transcription vs print — SETTLED, two material corrections:** (a) the transcription's "〈'Go to Noah and〉" (spurious leading curly quote) corrected to the print's "⟨Go to Noah and⟩"; (b) the transcription's v. 16 "a blessing; the works" (semicolon) corrected to the print's "a blessing: the works" (colon). Otherwise the transcription matched both scans word-for-word (wording, punctuation, diacritics). The print's French-spacing „ " quotation marks and spaced colons are print normalizations, recorded. PASS.

1. And Enoch went and said: 'Azâzêl, thou shalt have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against thee to put thee in bonds:
2. And thou shalt not have toleration nor †request† granted to thee, because of the unrighteousness which thou hast taught, and because of all the works of godlessness and unrighteousness and sin which thou hast shown to men.'
3. Then I went and spoke to them all together, and they were all afraid, and fear and trembling seized them.
4. And they besought me to draw up a petition for them that they might find forgiveness, and to read their petition in the presence of the Lord of heaven.
5. For from thenceforward they could not speak (with Him) nor lift up their eyes to heaven for shame of their sins for which they had been condemned.
6. Then I wrote out their petition, and the prayer †in regard to their spirits ⌜and their deeds individually⌝ and in regard to their requests (περὶ ὧν ἡμάρτησαν καὶ κατεκρίθησαν) that they should have forgiveness and length†.

8. And behold a dream came to me, and visions fell down upon me, and I saw visions of chastisement, ⌜and a voice came bidding (me)⌉ to tell it to the sons of heaven, and reprimand them.
9. And when I awaked, I came unto them, and they were all sitting gathered together, weeping in 'Abelsjâil, which is between Lebanon and Sênêsêr, with their faces covered.
10. And I recounted before them all the visions which I had seen in sleep, and I began to speak the words of righteousness, and to reprimand the heavenly Watchers.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And Enoch went and said: "Azâzêl, you will have no peace. A harsh sentence has gone out against you, to put you in chains.
2. You will get no mercy and no †hearing† for what you taught — all the wrong, the godlessness, the unrighteousness, the sin you showed to men."
3. Then I went and spoke to them all together. They were terrified — fear and trembling gripped them.
4. They begged me to write a plea for them, so they might find forgiveness, and to read their plea before the Lord of heaven.
5. For from then on they could not speak (with Him) or lift their eyes to heaven, ashamed of the sins they were condemned for.
6. So I wrote out their plea — the prayer †for their spirits ⌜and what each of them did⌝, asking for forgiveness and long life†.
7. Then I went off and sat by the waters of Dan, in the land of Dan, south-west of Hermon. I read their plea till I fell asleep.
8. And a dream came to me — visions fell on me. I saw visions of punishment, ⌜and a voice told (me)⌉ to take it to the sons of heaven and rebuke them.
9. When I woke, I went to them. They were all sitting together, weeping at 'Abelsjâil, between Lebanon and Sênêsêr, their faces covered.
10. I told them all the visions I had seen in my sleep, and began to speak words of righteousness and rebuke the heavenly Watchers.

1. The book of the words of righteousness, and of the reprimand of the eternal Watchers in accordance with the command of the Holy Great One in that vision.
2. I saw in my sleep what I will now say with a tongue of flesh and with the breath of my mouth: which the Great One has given to men to converse therewith and understand with the heart.
3. As He has created and given ⌜to man the power of understanding the word of wisdom, so hath He created me also and given⌝ me the power of reprimanding the Watchers, the children of heaven.
4. I wrote out your petition, and in my vision it appeared thus, that your petition will not be granted unto you ⌜throughout all the days of eternity, and that judgement has been finally passed upon you: yea (your petition) will not be granted unto you⌝.
5. And from henceforth you shall not ascend into heaven unto all eternity, and ⌜in bonds⌝ of the earth the decree has gone forth to bind you for all the days of the world.
6. And (that) previously you shall have seen the destruction of your beloved sons and ye shall have no pleasure in them, but they shall fall before you by the sword.
7. And your petition on their behalf shall not be granted, nor yet on your own: even though you weep and pray and speak all the words contained in the writing which I have written.
8. And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven.
9. And I went in till I drew nigh to a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire: and it began to affright me.
10. And I went into the tongues of fire and drew nigh to a large house which was built of crystals: and the walls of the house were like a tesselated floor (made) of crystals, and its groundwork was of crystal.
11. Its ceiling was like the path of the stars and the lightnings, and between them were fiery cherubim, and their heaven was (clear as) water.
12. A flaming fire surrounded the walls, and its portals blazed with fire.
13. And I entered into that house, and it was hot as fire and cold as ice: there were no delights of life therein: fear covered me, and trembling gat hold upon me.
14. And as I quaked and trembled, I fell upon my face. And I beheld a vision,
15. And lo! there was a second house, greater than the former, and the entire portal stood open before me, and it was built of flames of fire.
16. And in every respect it so excelled in splendour and magnificence and extent that I cannot describe to you its splendour and its extent.
17. And its floor was of fire, and above it were lightnings and the path of the stars, and its ceiling also was flaming fire.
18. And I looked and saw ⌜therein⌝ a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim.
19. And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon.
20. And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow.
21. None of the angels could enter and could behold His face by reason of the magnificence and glory, and no flesh could behold Him.
22. The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.
23. And the most holy ones who were nigh to Him did not leave by night nor depart from Him.
24. And until then I had been prostrate on my face, trembling: and the Lord called me with His own mouth, and said to me: 'Come hither, Enoch, and hear my word.'
25. ⌜And one of the holy ones came to me and waked me⌝, and He made me rise up and approach the door: and I bowed my face downwards.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. The book of the words of righteousness, and of the rebuke to the eternal Watchers, commanded by the Holy Great One in that vision.
2. In my sleep I saw what I will now say with a tongue of flesh, with the breath of my mouth — which the Great One gave to men, to talk with and understand with the heart.
3. As He made man and gave ⌜him the power to understand the word of wisdom, so He made me too and gave⌝ me the power to rebuke the Watchers, the children of heaven.
4. I wrote out your plea. In my vision it appeared like this: your plea will not be granted ⌜for all eternity — judgement has been passed on you for good, and (your plea) will not be granted⌝.
5. From now on you will never go up into heaven again, and ⌜in chains⌝ on earth the order has gone out to tie you up for all the days of the world.
6. Before that, you will have watched your loved sons destroyed — you will take no joy in them; they will fall before you by the sword.
7. Your plea for them will not be granted, nor your own — not though you weep and pray and speak every word written in the document I have written.
8. The vision came to me like this: Look — in the vision, clouds called me, mist summoned me. The stars and lightnings sped me on their course and hurried me along; the winds in the vision made me fly, lifted me up, and carried me into heaven.
9. I went in till I came near a wall built of crystal, ringed with tongues of fire — and it frightened me.
10. I went into the tongues of fire and came near a great house built of crystal. Its walls were like a crystal mosaic floor, and its foundation was crystal.
11. Its ceiling was like the path of the stars and the lightnings; fiery cherubim stood between them, and their heaven was (clear as) water.
12. Flaming fire ringed the walls, and its gates blazed with fire.
13. I entered that house — hot as fire and cold as ice. No joy of life was in it. Fear covered me; trembling gripped me.
14. Shaking and trembling, I fell on my face. And I saw a vision —
15. and look! There was a second house, greater than the first. Its whole doorway stood open before me, built of flames of fire.
16. In every way it outshone the first in splendour and grandeur and size — I cannot describe its splendour and its size to you.
17. Its floor was fire; above it were lightnings and the path of the stars; its ceiling too was flaming fire.
18. I looked and saw ⌜there⌝ a high throne. It looked like crystal; its wheels like the shining sun; and there was the vision of cherubim.
19. From under the throne streamed rivers of flaming fire, so I could not look at it.
20. The Great Glory sat on it. His clothing shone brighter than the sun, whiter than any snow.
21. No angel could enter or see His face, for His magnificence and glory — no flesh could look on Him.
22. Flaming fire circled Him; a great fire stood before Him. None around could come near Him. Ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him — yet He needed no counsellor.
23. The most holy ones near Him never left by night, never went from Him.
24. Till then I had lain face down, trembling. And the Lord called me with His own mouth: "Come here, Enoch, and hear my word."
25. ⌜And one of the holy ones came to me and woke me⌝ — He made me stand and come to the door, and I bowed my face down.

7. And therefore I have not appointed wives for you; for as for the spiritual ones of the heaven, in heaven is their dwelling.
8. And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling.
9. Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men, ⌜and⌝ from the holy watchers is their beginning and primal origin; ⌜they shall be evil spirits on earth, and⌝ evil spirits shall they be called.

11. And the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction upon the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, ⌜but nevertheless hunger⌉ and thirst, and cause offences.
12. And these spirits shall rise up against the children of men and against the women, because they have proceeded ⌜from them⌝.

1. I saw the storehouses of all the winds — I saw how He had stocked with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth.

9. I saw a flaming fire. And beyond these mountains
10. is a region, the end of the great earth — there the heavens were finished.
11. I saw a deep abyss, with columns ⌜of heavenly fire — and among them I saw columns⌝ of fire falling, beyond measure, up to the height and down to the depth.

16. He was angry with them and tied them up till the time their guilt is complete — (even) ⌜for ten thousand years⌝."

4. Then I said: "For what sin are they bound? Why were they thrown in here?"
5. Then Uriel — one of the holy angels, who was with me and was chief over them — said: "Enoch, why do you ask? Why are you so eager for the truth?
6. These are some of the stars ⌜of heaven⌝. They broke the Lord's command and are tied here till their time is complete — the ten thousand years, the time their sins have earned."
7. From there I went to another place, even more horrible than the first. I saw a horrible thing: a great fire burning and blazing there. The place was split open down to the abyss, full of great columns of fire coming down. I could not see how far or how big it was — I could not even guess.
8. Then I said: "How fearful this place is — how terrible to look at!"
9. Then Uriel — one of the holy angels with me — answered and said to me: "Enoch, why are you so afraid and frightened?" And I answered: "Because of this fearful place, and the sight of the pain."
10. And he said ⌜to me⌝: "This place is the prison of the angels. Here they will be locked up for ever."

Sheol or the Underworld.

1. [And.] thence I went to another place, and he showed me in the west ⌜another⌝ great and high mountain [and] of hard rock.
2. And there was in it †four† hollow places, deep and wide and very smooth. †How† smooth are the hollow places and deep and dark to look at.
3. Then Raphael answered, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said unto me: 'These hollow places have been created for this very purpose, that the spirits of the souls of the dead should assemble therein, yea that all the souls of the children of men should assemble here.
4. And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.'
5. I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead, and their voice went forth to heaven and made suit.
6. Then I asked Raphael the angel who was with me, and I said unto him: 'This spirit—whose is it whose voice goeth forth and maketh suit?'
7. And he answered me saying: 'This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.'
8. Then I asked regarding it, and regarding all the hollow places: 'Why is one separated from the other?'
9. And he answered me and said unto me: 'These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made ⟨for⟩ the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.
10. And such has been made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgement has not been executed on them in their lifetime.
11. Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement and punishment and torment of those who †curse† for ever, and retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever.
12. And such a division has been made for the spirits of those who make their suit, who make disclosures concerning their destruction, when they were slain in the days of the sinners.
13. Such has been made for the spirits of men who were not righteous but sinners, who were complete in transgression, and of the transgressors they shall be companions: but their spirits shall not be slain in the day of judgement nor shall they be raised from thence.'
14. Then I blessed the Lord of glory and said: 'Blessed be my Lord, the Lord of righteousness, who ruleth for ever.'

**Print-level findings (both scans):** the parallel E/Gˢ layout is as described (v. 2 and vv. 5–14 parallel; vv. 1, 3–4 single-column E). The E column is Charles's primary line. Charles's notes (sighted): v. 1 "[And.] Bracketed as an intrusion in E. Not in Gˢ."; v. 2 "†Four†. There are four divisions, according to the text of this verse, in" (with dittograph note); "†Four† ... †three†. Read 'Three ... two'. See preceding note."; "†How†. Since the angel, in reply, gives the object of Sheol, 'how' cannot be right: we expect 'why', 'wherefore', or 'for what purpose'. Hence ... read 'for what purpose are these hollow places smooth and deep and dark to view?'"; v. 4 "[Till the period appointed.] A dittograph."; v. 5 "Spirits of the children of men who were dead (E). Gˢ defective and corrupt"; v. 11 "†curse†" (corrupt); v. 9 "⟨for⟩" (Charles's supply). The Gˢ column's "⟨the spirit of⟩" (v. 5) and "†three†" (v. 2) are control-only, not imported. No thick type anywhere in vv. 1–14 on either scan.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 E-column base above)

1. [And.] From there I went to another place. He showed me in the west ⌜another⌝ great high mountain [and] of hard rock.
2. In it were †four† hollow places — deep, wide, very smooth. †How† smooth the hollow places are — deep and dark to look at.
3. Then Raphael — one of the holy angels with me — answered and said to me: "These hollow places were made for this very purpose: that the spirits of the souls of the dead should gather there — yes, that all the souls of the children of men should gather here.
4. These places were made to receive them till the day of their judgement, till their appointed time [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) on them."
5. I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead. Their voice went up to heaven, pleading.
6. Then I asked Raphael, the angel with me: "This spirit — whose is it, whose voice goes up pleading?"
7. He answered: "This is the spirit that left Abel, whom his brother Cain killed. He pleads against him till his seed is wiped from the face of the earth, his seed destroyed from among the seed of men."
8. Then I asked about it, and about all the hollow places: "Why is one separated from the other?"
9. He answered me: "These three were made so the spirits of the dead could be separated. Such a division was made ⟨for⟩ the spirits of the righteous — where the bright spring of water is.
10. Such was made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth, and judgement was not carried out on them in their lifetime.
11. Here their spirits will be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement — punishment and torment of those who †curse† for ever, retribution for their spirits. There He will tie them for ever.
12. Such a division was made for the spirits of those who plead — who tell of their destruction, when they were killed in the days of the sinners.
13. Such was made for the spirits of men who were not righteous but sinners — complete in wrongdoing; they will keep company with wrongdoers. But their spirits will not be killed on the day of judgement, nor raised from there."
14. Then I blessed the Lord of glory: "Blessed be my Lord, the Lord of righteousness, who rules for ever."

The Purpose of the Accursed Valley.

1. Then said I: 'For what object is this blessed land, which is entirely filled with trees, and this accursed valley ⌜between ?⌝'
2. ⌜Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: 'This⌝ accursed valley is for those who are accursed for ever: here shall all ⌜the accursed⌝ be gathered together who utter with their lips against the Lord unseemly words and of His glory speak hard things. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be their place of judgement.
3. In the last days there shall be upon them the spectacle of righteous judgement in the presence of the righteous for ever: here shall the merciful bless the Lord of Glory, the Eternal King.
4. In the days of judgement over the former, they shall bless Him for the mercy in accordance with which He has assigned them (their lot).'
5. Then I blessed the Lord of Glory and set forth His ⌜glory⌝ and lauded Him gloriously.

**Print-level findings (both scans):** the v. 2/v. 3 parallel E/Gˢ layout on p. 56 is a print fact; the E column is Charles's primary line. All four cornered clauses are single-bracketed on the print. Charles's notes (sighted): v. 1 (the "between ?" corner — direction not fully sighted); v. 2 "'This (E). > Gˢ."; "The accursed (Gˢ). > E."; v. 3 "In the days (Gˢ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις). Here E reads ἔσται αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν ὅρασιν"; v. 5 "His ⌜glory⌝ (Gˢ). E om. 'glory' perhaps owing to its occurrence just before." No thick type anywhere in vv. 1–5 on either scan.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 37

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 37" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_37), carrying the Charles text (public domain). 1. The second vision which he saw, the vision of wisdom—which Enoch the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan, the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, saw.
2. And this is the beginning of the words of wisdom which I lifted up my voice to speak and say to those which dwell on earth: Hear, ye men of old time, and see, ye that come after, the words of the Holy One which I will speak before the Lord of Spirits.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. The second vision he saw — the vision of wisdom — which Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Cainan, son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, saw.
2. And this is the beginning of the words of wisdom, which I lifted up my voice to speak and say to those who live on earth: "Hear, you men of old time, and see, you who come after — the words of the Holy One, which I will speak before the Lord of Spirits."
3. It would have been better to declare them only to the men of old time, but even from those who come after, we will not hold back the beginning of wisdom.

5. Now three parables were given to me, and I lifted up my voice and told them to those who live on the earth.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 37:** the prologue to the entire Parables block (37–71) — "the second vision" (the first being the Watchers block, ch. 1–36), Enoch's full genealogy, and the announcement of the three Parables. The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none. Section II opens here ("Section II. Chapters XXXVII–LXXI / The Parables" in the transcription's section heads).
- **"the second vision" (v. 1):** kept — it counts the Watchers visions as the first; no explicitation added. G3-adjacent; disclosed.
- **Genealogy "the son of Jared…" → "son of Jared…" (v. 1):** the repeated "the" dropped for plain English; disclosed.
- **"those which dwell on earth" → "those who live on earth" (vv. 2, 5):** "which" → "who" for people; "dwell" → "live" for plain register. Disclosed;
- **"ye" → "you" (v. 2):** "Hear, ye men of old time, and see, ye that come after" → "Hear, you men of old time, and see, you who come after" — extension of the ch. 9 Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your decision to "ye". Disclosed;
- **Quoted address (v. 2):** SETTLED at G1 Part B — the print sets the direct address ("Hear, ye men of old time...") in regular type after a colon, with no bold and no quote marks. The draft's double quotes are a disclosed normalization; the print's no-bold setting is now recorded fact, not assumption.
- **"(them only)" → "them only" (v. 3):** Charles's round-bracket supply absorbed into plain English per the ch. 1 standing rule; disclosed.
- **"It were better" → "It would have been better" (v. 3):** subjunctive modernized; disclosed.
- **"we will not withhold" → "we will not hold back" (v. 3):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"Till the present day" → "To this day" (v. 4):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"imparted to me" → "given to me"; "recounted" → "told" (v. 5):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"Lord of Spirits" (vv. 2, 4):** kept verbatim — the standing divine title of the Parables, first occurring in this verse; never flattened or harmonized. **G3-CRITICAL.**
- **"the Holy One" (v. 2):** kept; G3 item.
- **"the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits" (v. 4):** kept verbatim — liturgical formula; G3 item.
- **"the lot of eternal life" (v. 4):** kept; G3 item ("lot"/portion language).
- **"according to my insight" (v. 4):** kept; G3 item.
- **"three parables" lowercase (v. 5):** the print reads "three parables" in ordinary lower case — the transcription's capital "Parables" was a normalization, corrected at G1 Part B. "Parable(s)" remains a technical term for the block's three divisions (38–44, 45–57, 58–71); G3 item.

- **"has caused His light to appear" in thick type (v. 4):** Charles's own emendation — marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. His note (sighted): "I have emended tar'ĕja = 'is seen' into 'ar'aja = 'has caused to appear'. This emendation is required by the fact that 'the Lord of Spirits' is in the nom. in α, d, and 'His light' in the acc. in q. β-d reads 'the light of the Lord of Spirits is seen'." Whether the reading text signals the emendation is
- **"shall" futures → plain futures (vv. 1–6):** "shall appear" → "appears"/"will perish" etc. — the prophetic future kept, the archaic "shall" dropped. No tense change intended; disclosed.
- **"the Righteous One" (v. 2):** kept verbatim — a title distinct from "the Elect One" and "Son of Man"; never harmonized. **G3-CRITICAL.**
- **"Whose elect works hang upon the Lord of Spirits" (v. 2):** kept nearly verbatim ("hang upon" = depend on); the oddness is Charles's, not smoothed. G3 item ("elect works").
- **"It had been good for them if they had not been born" → "It would have been better for them if they had not been born" (v. 2):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"the godless" (v. 3):** kept as Charles's word (ch. 8's "godlessness" is the related noun); not flattened to "the wicked". G3 item.
- **"behold the face of the holy" → "look on the face of the holy" (v. 4):** "behold" → "look" per the ch. 9 standing move; disclosed.
- **"thenceforward" → "from then on" (v. 6):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"none shall seek for themselves mercy" → "none will seek mercy for themselves" (v. 6):** plain word order; disclosed.
- **"the kings and the mighty" (v. 5):** kept — the recurring judged pair of the Parables; G3 item.
- **"the congregation of the righteous" (v. 1):** kept; G3 item.
- **"denied the Lord of Spirits" (v. 2):** kept; G3 item.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 39

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 39" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_39), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 74–77 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 Part B — see the G1 Audit Record; one minor transcription-vs-print correction was made (v. 1 bracket opens before the verse number in print: "[1. And it...", not "1. [And it...").

[1. And it †shall come to pass in those days that elect and holy children †will descend from the high heaven, and their seed† will become one with the children of men. 2. And in those days Enoch received books of zeal and wrath, and books of disquiet and expulsion.]

And mercy shall not be accorded to them, saith the Lord of Spirits.

3. And in those days a whirlwind carried me off from the earth,

And set me down at the end of the heavens.

4. And there I saw another vision, the dwelling-places of the holy,

And the resting-places of the righteous.

5. Here mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels,

And their resting-places with the holy.

And they petitioned and interceded and prayed for the children of men,

And righteousness flowed before them as water,

And mercy like dew upon the earth:

Thus it is amongst them for ever and ever.

6a. And in that place mine eyes saw the Elect One of righteousness and of faith,

7a. And I saw his dwelling-place under the wings of the Lord of Spirits.

6b. And righteousness shall prevail in his days,

And the righteous and elect shall be without number before Him for ever and ever.

7b. And all the righteous and elect before Him shall be †strong† as fiery lights,

And their mouth shall be full of blessing,

And their lips extol the name of the Lord of Spirits,

And righteousness before Him shall never fail,

[And uprightness shall never fail before Him.]

8. There I wished to dwell,

And my spirit longed for that dwelling-place:

And there heretofore hath been my portion,

For so has it been established concerning me before the Lord of Spirits.

9. In those days I praised and extolled the name of the Lord of Spirits with blessings and praises, because He hath destined me for blessing and glory according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits. 10. For a long time my eyes regarded that place, and I blessed Him and praised Him, saying: 'Blessed is He, and may He be blessed from the beginning and for evermore. 11. And before Him there is no ceasing. He knows before the world was created what is for ever and what will be from generation unto generation. 12. Those who sleep not bless Thee: they stand before Thy glory and bless, praise, and extol, saying: "Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of Spirits: He filleth the earth with spirits."' 13. And here my eyes saw all those who sleep not: they stand before Him and bless and say: 'Blessed be Thou, and blessed be the name of the Lord for ever and ever.' 14. And my face was changed; for I could no longer behold.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 40

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 40" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_40), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 77–79 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 Part B — see the G1 Audit Record; two material transcription-vs-print corrections were made (v. 2 "the angel that went with me" → "the angel who went with me"; v. 6 "pray and intercede" and "supplicate" settled in thick type and marked in the base).

1. And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before the Lord of Spirits. 2. And on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those that sleep not, and I learnt their names: for the angel who went with me made known to me their names, and showed me all the hidden things.

3. And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before the Lord of glory. 4. The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever. 5. And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who hang upon the Lord of Spirits. 6. And the third voice I heard **pray and intercede** for those who dwell on the earth and **supplicate** in the name of the Lord of Spirits. 7. And I heard the fourth voice fending off the Satans and forbidding them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse them who dwell on the earth. 8. After that I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden: 'Who are these four presences which I have seen and whose words I have heard and written down?' 9. And he said to me: 'This first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.' 10. And these are the four angels of the Lord of Spirits and the four voices I heard in those days.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand — I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning — who stood before the Lord of Spirits. 2. And on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those who do not sleep, and I learned their names: for the angel who went with me made known to me their names, and showed me all the hidden things.

3. And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before the Lord of glory. 4. The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever. 5. And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who hang upon the Lord of Spirits. 6. And the third voice I heard pray and intercede for those who live on the earth and plead in the name of the Lord of Spirits. 7. And I heard the fourth voice fending off the Satans and forbidding them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse those who live on the earth. 8. After that I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden: "Who are these four presences which I have seen, and whose words I have heard and written down?" 9. And he said to me: "This first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering; and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael; and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel; and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel." 10. And these are the four angels of the Lord of Spirits, and the four voices I heard in those days.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **"thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand" (v. 1):** the number formula kept verbatim; G3 item.
- **"the angel who went with me" (v. 2):** the print reads "who", not "that" — corrected from the transcription at G1 Part B (both scans). The draft already had "who".
- **"pray and intercede" and "supplicate" in thick type (v. 6):** Charles's own marking — settled on enlarged crops in both scans and marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. His note (sighted) discusses the verbs without an explicit emendation statement: "Pray and intercede... supplicate. These verbs are in the plural in all MSS. but *d*." The thick type is nonetheless unmistakable in both scans. Whether the reading text signals the marking is
- **"four presences" (vv. 2, 3, 8):** Charles's word for the archangels as throne-presences; kept, not replaced with "angels" (v. 10 itself says "these are the four angels"). G3 item.
- **"those that sleep not" → "those who do not sleep" (v. 2):** consistent with ch. 39; disclosed.
- **"learnt" → "learned" (v. 2):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"supplicate" → "plead" (v. 6):** plain register ("pray and intercede … and plead"); disclosed.
- **"them who dwell on the earth" → "those who live on the earth" (v. 7):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"fending off the Satans" (v. 7):** kept — "the Satans" in the plural, accusers barred from the throne; G3 item.
- **"the angel of peace" (v. 8):** Enoch's guiding angel in the Parables; kept as a title; G3 item.
- **v. 9 colons → semicolons:** the base separates the four identifications with colons; the draft uses semicolons for plain readability. Disclosed;
- **"the merciful and long-suffering" (Michael, v. 9):** epithets kept; G3 items.
- **"the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life" (v. 9, Phanuel's charge):** "unto" kept — the phrase is deliberately odd; paraphrasing it ("repentance that leads to hope") would be interpretation. Disclosed as kept; **G3 item.** The question whether a plainer form is wanted was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"Lord of glory" (v. 3):** kept — a distinct title from "Lord of Spirits"; never harmonized. G3 item.
- **"the Elect One and the elect ones" (v. 5):** the singular/plural pair kept exactly; **G3-CRITICAL.**
- **"hang upon the Lord of Spirits" (v. 5):** same phrase as ch. 38 v. 2; kept; G3 item — do not harmonize now.
- **Quote marks flattened** (vv. 8, 9): transcription's '…' → double quotes in the draft, per the ch. 9 disclosure; the print's bold-speech setting is typography, pending scan confirmation.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 41

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 41" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_41), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 78–81 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 Part B — see the G1 Audit Record; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse and line faithfully).

1. And after that I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the actions of men are weighed in the balance. 2. And there I saw the mansions of the elect and the mansions of the holy, and mine eyes saw there all the sinners being driven from thence which deny the name of the Lord of Spirits, and being dragged off: and they could not abide because of the punishment which proceeds from the Lord of Spirits.

3. And there mine eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and of the thunder, and the secrets of the winds, how they are divided to blow over the earth, and the secrets of the clouds and dew, and there I saw from whence they proceed in that place and from whence they saturate the dusty earth. 4. And there I saw closed chambers out of which the winds are divided, the chamber of the hail and winds, the chamber of the mist, and of the clouds, and the cloud thereof hovers over the earth from the beginning of the world. 5. And I saw the chambers of the sun and moon, whence they proceed and whither they come again, and their glorious return, and how one is superior to the other, and their stately orbit, and how they do not leave their orbit, and they add nothing to their orbit and they take nothing from it, and they keep faith with each other, in accordance with the oath by which they are bound together. 6. And first the sun goes forth and traverses his path according to the commandment of the Lord of Spirits, and mighty is His name for ever and ever. 7. And after that I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon, and she accomplishes the course of her path in that place by day and by night—the one holding a position opposite to the other before the Lord of Spirits.

And they give thanks and praise and rest not;

For unto them is their thanksgiving rest.

8. For the sun changes oft for a blessing or a curse,

And the course of the path of the moon is light to the righteous

And darkness to the sinners in the name of the Lord,

Who made a separation between the light and the darkness,

And divided the spirits of men,

And strengthened the spirits of the righteous,

In the name of His righteousness.

9. For no angel hinders and no power is able to hinder; for He appoints a judge for them all and He judges them all before Him.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And after that I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the actions of men are weighed in the balance. 2. And there I saw the mansions of the elect and the mansions of the holy, and my eyes saw there all the sinners being driven from there — those who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits — being dragged off; and they could not stand because of the punishment which comes from the Lord of Spirits.

3. And there my eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and of the thunder, and the secrets of the winds — how they are divided to blow over the earth — and the secrets of the clouds and dew; and there I saw where they come from in that place, and where they soak the dusty earth. 4. And there I saw closed chambers out of which the winds are divided — the chamber of the hail and winds, the chamber of the mist and of the clouds — and its cloud hovers over the earth from the beginning of the world. 5. And I saw the chambers of the sun and moon — where they come from and where they return, and their glorious return — and how one is greater than the other, and their stately orbit, and how they do not leave their orbit: they add nothing to their orbit and take nothing from it, and they keep faith with each other, according to the oath by which they are bound together. 6. And first the sun goes out and travels his path according to the command of the Lord of Spirits, and mighty is His name for ever and ever. 7. And after that I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon, and she completes the course of her path in that place by day and by night — the one holding a position opposite to the other before the Lord of Spirits.

And they give thanks and praise and do not rest;

for their thanksgiving is their rest.

8. For the sun often changes, for blessing or for curse,

and the course of the moon's path is light to the righteous

and darkness to the sinners, in the name of the Lord,

who made a separation between the light and the darkness,

and divided the spirits of men,

and strengthened the spirits of the righteous,

in the name of His righteousness.

9. For no angel hinders and no power can hinder; for He appoints a judge for them all, and He judges them all before Him.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **"hearkened unto Him" → "listened to Him" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"(I saw)" ×2 and "(how)" (v. 2):** Charles's round-bracket supplies, absorbed into plain English per the ch. 1 standing rule ("I saw the width…", "I saw their circling…", "and how they keep faith"); disclosed.
- **"proportions of light" → "portions of light" (v. 2):** "proportions" = measured shares; "portions" is the plainer floor. Disclosed;
- **"revolution" → "circling" (v. 2):** plain register for the stars' turning; disclosed.
- **"they keep faith with each other" (v. 2):** same phrase as ch. 41 v. 5 (the luminaries); kept; G3 item — do not harmonize now.
- **"thee" → "you"; "hath showed" → "has shown" (v. 4):** per the ch. 9 Thou-decision; disclosed.
- **"their parabolic meaning (lit. 'their parable')" (v. 4):** "parabolic" is jargon; rendered "what they mean as a parable" with Charles's literal gloss kept visible ("literally 'their parable'"). Disclosed; the question whether the gloss stays for readers was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"the names of the holy who dwell on the earth and believe in the name of the Lord of Spirits" (v. 4):** the stars ARE the names of the holy — the parable's own decoding; kept verbatim; G3 item.
- **"weighed in a righteous balance" (v. 2):** kept; G3 item (against ch. 41's "weighed in the balance").
- **Quote marks flattened** (vv. 3, 4): transcription's '…' → double quotes in the draft, per the ch. 9 disclosure; the print's bold-speech setting is typography, pending scan confirmation.

1. And this is the second Parable, concerning those who deny the name of the dwelling of the holy ones and the Lord of Spirits.

2. And into heaven they will not go up,

and on the earth they will not come:

such will be the lot of the sinners

who have denied the name of the Lord of Spirits,

who are kept like this for the day of suffering and anguish.

3. On that day My Elect One will sit on the throne of glory

and will test their works,

and their resting-places will be beyond counting.

And their souls will grow strong within them when they see My elect ones,

and those who have called upon My glorious name.

4. Then I will cause My Elect One to live among them.

And I will transform the heaven and make it an eternal blessing and light.

5. And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing,

and I will cause My elect ones to live upon it —

but the sinners and evildoers will not set foot on it.

6. For I have cared for My righteous ones and filled them with peace,

and have caused them to live before Me.

But for the sinners, judgment is waiting with Me,

and I will destroy them from the face of the earth.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **"shall **try** their works" (v. 3):** "try" is in Charles's thick type in the print (settled on both scans) — his emendation, marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. His note (sighted): "Try. Text reads jahari (= choose) = יבחר corrupt for יבחן..." — apparatus only. Whether the reading text signals the marking is
- **"the second Parable" (v. 1):** Charles's rubric for the second division (ch. 45–57), carried as v. 1; kept as a heading-line. Disclosed.
- **"those who deny the name of the dwelling of the holy ones and the Lord of Spirits" (v. 1):** the phrasing is strained (deny the name *of the dwelling*?); kept exactly as Charles prints it — smoothing it would be interpretation without a control. Disclosed; G3 item.
- **"Mine" → "My" (vv. 3, 4, 5):** "Mine Elect One", "Mine elect ones" — Charles's archaic "mine" before vowels; modernized to "My". Disclosed;
- **"shall not ascend … shall not come" → "will not go up … will not come" (v. 2):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"preserved for the day of suffering and tribulation" → "kept like this for the day of suffering and anguish" (v. 2):** "preserved" = kept in store; "tribulation" → "anguish" (plain). Disclosed;
- **"shall try their works" → "will test their works" (v. 3):** "try" = judicially test; plain form disclosed.
- **"places of rest" (v. 3):** kept; G3 item (against ch. 39's "resting-places" — do not harmonize now).
- **"evil-doers" → "evildoers"; "thereon" → "on it" (v. 5):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"I have provided and satisfied with peace My righteous ones" → "I have cared for My righteous ones and filled them with peace" (v. 6):** the base's compressed syntax unpacked into plain English; disclosed.
- **"judgement impending" → "judgment is waiting" (v. 6):** "impending" modernized; disclosed.
- **"dwell" → "live" (vv. 4, 5, 6):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"transform the heaven … transform the earth" (vv. 4, 5):** kept; G3 item (the renewal).
- **"My Elect One … My elect ones" (vv. 3–5):** the singular title and the plural kept distinct; **G3-CRITICAL.**
- **"throne of glory" (v. 3):** kept; G3 item.
- **"the lot of the sinners" (v. 2):** kept; G3 item (lot/portion language, cf. ch. 37 "the lot of eternal life").
- **Poetic lineation:** the draft keeps the transcription's line breaks; disclosed as a structural choice.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 46

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 46" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_46), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 85–90 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 Part B — see the G1 Audit Record; one material transcription-vs-print correction was made (v. 7 "gods" carries the print's daggers: "†gods†", dropped by the transcription — restored in base and draft).

1. And there I saw One who had a head of days,

And His head was white like wool,

And with Him was another being whose countenance had the appearance of a man,

And his face was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels.

2. And I asked the angel who went with me and showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Man, who he was, and whence he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days? 3. And he answered and said unto me:

This is the Son of Man who hath righteousness,

With whom dwelleth righteousness,

And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden,

Because the Lord of Spirits hath chosen him,

And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before the Lord of Spirits in uprightness for ever.

4. And this Son of Man whom thou hast seen

Shall †raise up† the kings and the mighty from their seats,

[And the strong from their thrones]

And shall loosen the reins of the strong,

And break the teeth of the sinners.

5. [And he shall put down the kings from their thrones and kingdoms]

Because they do not extol and praise Him,

Nor humbly acknowledge whence the kingdom was bestowed upon them.

6. And he shall put down the countenance of the strong,

And shall fill them with shame.

And darkness shall be their dwelling,

And worms shall be their bed,

And they shall have no hope of rising from their beds,

Because they do not extol the name of the Lord of Spirits.

7. And these are they who †judge† the stars of heaven,

[And raise their hands against the Most High],

†And tread upon the earth and dwell upon it†.

And all their deeds manifest unrighteousness,

And their power rests upon their riches,

And their faith is in the †gods† which they have made with their hands,

And they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits,

8. And they persecute the houses of His congregations,

And the faithful who hang upon the name of the Lord of Spirits.

because they do not extol and praise Him,

and will fill them with shame.

And darkness will be their dwelling,

and worms will be their bed,

and they will have no hope of rising from their beds,

because they do not extol the name of the Lord of Spirits.

†And tread upon the earth and live upon it†.

and their power rests upon their riches,

and they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits,

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 47

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 47" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_47), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 90–93 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 Part B — see the G1 Audit Record; one material transcription-vs-print correction was made (v. 4 "had been offered" settled in thick type and marked in the base).

1. And in those days shall have ascended the prayer of the righteous,

And the blood of the righteous from the earth before the Lord of Spirits.

2. In those days the holy ones who dwell above in the heavens

Shall unite with one voice

And supplicate and pray [and praise,

And give thanks and bless the name of the Lord of Spirits]

On behalf of the blood of the righteous which has been shed,

And that the prayer of the righteous may not be in vain before the Lord of Spirits,

That judgement may be done unto them,

And that they may not have to suffer for ever.

3. In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory,

And the books of the living were opened before Him:

And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,

4. And the hearts of the holy were filled with joy;

Because the number of the righteous **had been offered**,

And the prayer of the righteous had been heard,

And the blood of the righteous been required before the Lord of Spirits.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And in those days the prayer of the righteous will have gone up,

and the blood of the righteous from the earth, before the Lord of Spirits.

2. In those days the holy ones who live above in the heavens

will join together with one voice

and plead and pray [and praise,

and give thanks and bless the name of the Lord of Spirits]

for the blood of the righteous which has been shed,

and so that the prayer of the righteous may not be in vain before the Lord of Spirits,

so that judgment may be done for them,

and they may not have to suffer for ever.

3. In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated Himself on the throne of His glory,

and the books of the living were opened before Him;

and all His host in heaven above, and His counsellors, stood before Him.

4. And the hearts of the holy were filled with joy,

because the number of the righteous had been offered,

and the prayer of the righteous had been heard,

and the blood of the righteous had been required before the Lord of Spirits.

Been offered. α reads qarĕba = ἤγγικε = קרב, which in Mishnaic and late Hebrew = 'had been offered' as well as 'had drawn nigh'. The latter meaning is inappropriate; for the judgement is already begun. The text means that the number of the righteous, i. e. the martyrs, is complete. The martyrs were regarded as offerings to God. Cf. Rev. 6¹⁰, ¹¹, and my note in loc. For qarĕba β reads baṣeḥa = 'has come'." PASS.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 48

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 48" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_48), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 93–96 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 Part B — see the G1 Audit Record; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse faithfully, including Charles's round-bracket supply).

1. And in that place I saw the fountain of righteousness

Which was inexhaustible:

And around it were many fountains of wisdom:

And all the thirsty drank of them,

And were filled with wisdom,

And their dwellings were with the righteous and holy and elect.

2. And at that hour that Son of Man was named

In the presence of the Lord of Spirits,

And his name before the Head of Days.

3. Yea, before the sun and the signs were created,

Before the stars of the heaven were made,

His name was named before the Lord of Spirits.

4. He shall be a staff to the righteous whereon to stay themselves and not fall,

And he shall be the light of the Gentiles,

And the hope of those who are troubled of heart.

5. All who dwell on earth shall fall down and worship before him,

And will praise and bless and celebrate with song the Lord of Spirits.

6. And for this reason hath he been chosen and hidden before Him,

Before the creation of the world and for evermore.

7. And the wisdom of the Lord of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous;

For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous,

Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness,

And have hated all its works and ways in the name of the Lord of Spirits:

For in his name they are saved,

And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.

8. In these days downcast in countenance shall the kings of the earth have become,

And the strong who possess the land because of the works of their hands,

For on the day of their anguish and affliction they shall not (be able to) save themselves.

9. And I will give them over into the hands of Mine elect:

As straw in the fire so shall they burn before the face of the holy:

As lead in the water shall they sink before the face of the righteous,

And no trace of them shall any more be found.

10. And on the day of their affliction there shall be rest on the earth,

And before them they shall fall and not rise again:

And there shall be no one to take them with his hands and raise them:

For they have denied the Lord of Spirits and His Anointed.

The name of the Lord of Spirits be blessed.
