## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 72

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 72" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_72), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 151–156 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below. One material transcription-vs-print correction was needed (72.1 "The Book", capital B in print); no thick-type emendations occur in the main text of this chapter.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter LXXII = vv. 1–37 exactly, spanning printed pp. 151–156; "LXXIII. 1." begins on p. 156 immediately after v. 37, under the italic sub-heading "The Moon and its Phases." The chapter opens on p. 151 under Charles's own italic centered sub-heading "The Sun.", followed by the inline bold "LXXII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER LXXII." is a normalization; the transcription's "### Section III. Chapters LXXII-LXXXII." and "### The Book of the Heavenly Luminaries." headers are Wikisource navigation, not print). Running heads: "Sect. III]" top left, "Chapter LXXII. 1-3" / "Chapter LXXII. 4-12" / "Chapter LXXII. 13-33" center (pp. 151, 153, 155), "The Book of Enoch" center with "[Sect. III" top right (pp. 152, 154, 156). **No thick type** in the main text of vv. 1–37 (both scans). **Daggers † (corrupt):** "†two†" (v. 12), "†two†" (v. 18), "†ninth†" (v. 28). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial):** "[those six portals in the east]" (v. 6), "[and becomes of equal length]" (v. 20). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(lit. 'that')" (v. 5), "(therewith)" (v. 27), "(lit. 'they are separated')" (v. 33). No single or double corner brackets, no angle brackets in vv. 1–37. Bold word numerals are typography only.

1. The Book of the courses of the luminaries of the heaven, the relations of each, according to their classes, their dominion and their seasons, according to their names and places of origin, and according to their months, which Uriel, the holy angel, who was with me, who is their guide, showed me; and he showed me all their laws exactly as they are, and how it is with regard to all the years of the world and unto eternity, till the new creation is accomplished which dureth till eternity.
2. And this is the first law of the luminaries: the luminary the Sun has its rising in the eastern portals of the heaven, and its setting in the western portals of the heaven.
3. And I saw six portals in which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets: and the moon rises and sets in these portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, and all following each other in accurately corresponding order: also many windows to the right and left of these portals.
4. And first there goes forth the great luminary, named the Sun, and his circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and he is quite filled with illuminating and heating fire.
5. The chariot on which he ascends, the wind drives, and the sun goes down from the heaven and returns through the north in order to reach the east, and is so guided that he comes to the appropriate (lit. 'that') portal and shines in the face of the heaven.
6. In this way he rises in the first month in the great portal, which is the fourth [those six portals in the east].
7. And in that fourth portal from which the sun rises in the first month are twelve window-openings, from which proceed a flame when they are opened in their season.
8. When the sun rises in the heaven, he comes forth through that fourth portal thirty mornings in succession, and sets accurately in the fourth portal in the west of the heaven.
9. And during this period the day becomes daily longer and the night nightly shorter to the thirtieth morning.
10. On that day the day is longer than the night by a ninth part, and the day amounts exactly to ten parts and the night to eight parts.
11. And the sun rises from that fourth portal, and sets in the fourth and returns to the fifth portal of the east thirty mornings, and rises from it and sets in the fifth portal.
12. And then the day becomes longer by †two† parts and amounts to eleven parts, and the night becomes shorter and amounts to seven parts.
13. And it returns to the east and enters into the sixth portal, and rises and sets in the sixth portal one-and-thirty mornings on account of its sign.
14. On that day the day becomes longer than the night, and the day becomes double the night, and the day becomes twelve parts, and the night is shortened and becomes six parts.
15. And the sun mounts up to make the day shorter and the night longer, and the sun returns to the east and enters into the sixth portal, and rises from it and sets thirty mornings.
16. And when thirty mornings are accomplished, the day decreases by exactly one part, and becomes eleven parts, and the night seven.
17. And the sun goes forth from that sixth portal in the west, and goes to the east and rises in the fifth portal for thirty mornings, and sets in the west again in the fifth western portal.
18. On that day the day decreases by †two† parts, and amounts to ten parts and the night to eight parts.
19. And the sun goes forth from that fifth portal and sets in the fifth portal of the west, and rises in the fourth portal for one-and-thirty mornings on account of its sign, and sets in the west.
20. On that day the day is equalized with the night, [and becomes of equal length], and the night amounts to nine parts and the day to nine parts.
21. And the sun rises from that portal and sets in the west, and returns to the east and rises thirty mornings in the third portal and sets in the west in the third portal.
22. And on that day the night becomes longer than the day, and night becomes longer than night, and day shorter than day till the thirtieth morning, and the night amounts exactly to ten parts and the day to eight parts.
23. And the sun rises from that third portal and sets in the third portal in the west and returns to the east, and for thirty mornings rises in the second portal in the east, and in like manner sets in the second portal in the west of the heaven.
24. And on that day the night amounts to eleven parts and the day to seven parts.
25. And the sun rises on that day from that second portal and sets in the west in the second portal, and returns to the east into the first portal for one-and-thirty mornings, and sets in the first portal in the west of the heaven.
26. And on that day the night becomes longer and amounts to the double of the day: and the night amounts exactly to twelve parts and the day to six.
27. And the sun has (therewith) traversed the divisions of his orbit and turns again on those divisions of his orbit, and enters that portal thirty mornings and sets also in the west opposite to it.
28. And on that night has the night decreased in length by a †ninth† part, and the night has become eleven parts and the day seven parts.
29. And the sun has returned and entered into the second portal in the east, and returns on those his divisions of his orbit for thirty mornings, rising and setting.
30. And on that day the night decreases in length, and the night amounts to ten parts and the day to eight.
31. And on that day the sun rises from that portal, and sets in the west, and returns to the east, and rises in the third portal for one-and-thirty mornings, and sets in the west of the heaven.
32. On that day the night decreases and amounts to nine parts, and the day to nine parts, and the night is equal to the day and the year is exactly as to its days three hundred and sixty-four.
33. And the length of the day and of the night, and the shortness of the day and of the night arise—through the course of the sun these distinctions are made (lit. 'they are separated').
34. So it comes that its course becomes daily longer, and its course nightly shorter.
35. And this is the law and the course of the sun, and his return as often as he returns sixty times and rises, i.e. the great luminary which is named the sun, for ever and ever.
36. And that which (thus) rises is the great luminary, and is so named according to its appearance, according as the Lord commanded.
37. As he rises, so he sets and decreases not, and rests not, but runs day and night, and his light is sevenfold brighter than that of the moon; but as regards size they are both equal.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 1 "The Book" — print carries capital B ("The Book of the courses"); the transcription's "The book" is a normalization, corrected in the base above as a material correction. Running head p. 155 reads "Chapter LXXII. 13-33" (hyphen); p. 157 "Chapters LXXII. 34—LXXIII. 5" (em dash) — print fact, not normalized.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. The book of the courses of the luminaries of the sky — the dealings of each, by its kind, its rule and its seasons, by its names and where they come from, and by their months — which Uriel, the holy angel who was with me, who is their guide, showed me. He showed me all their laws exactly as they are, and how it stands with all the years of the world, on to eternity, till the new creation is finished, which lasts forever.
2. This is the first law of the luminaries: the luminary, the Sun, rises in the eastern portals of the sky and sets in the western portals of the sky.
3. I saw six portals where the sun rises and six portals where the sun sets. The moon rises and sets in these same portals, and so do the leaders of the stars and those they lead — six in the east and six in the west, each following the other in exactly matching order. There are also many windows to the right and left of these portals.
4. First goes out the great luminary, named the Sun. Its circle is like the circle of the sky, and it is full of light-giving and heat-giving fire.
5. The wind drives the chariot on which he climbs. The sun goes down from the sky and comes back through the north to reach the east, and is guided so that he comes to the right (that is, "that") portal and shines in the face of the sky.
6. In this way he rises in the first month in the great portal, which is the fourth [of those six portals in the east].
7. In that fourth portal, from which the sun rises in the first month, are twelve window-openings, and a flame comes out of them when they are opened in their season.
8. When the sun rises in the sky, he comes out through that fourth portal thirty mornings in a row, and sets exactly in the fourth portal in the west of the sky.
9. During this time the day gets longer every day and the night shorter every night, till the thirtieth morning.
10. On that day the day is longer than the night by a ninth part: the day comes to exactly ten parts and the night to eight parts.
11. The sun rises from that fourth portal and sets in the fourth, then goes back to the fifth portal of the east for thirty mornings, rising from it and setting in the fifth portal.
12. Then the day gets longer by †two† parts and comes to eleven parts, and the night gets shorter and comes to seven parts.
13. It goes back to the east and enters the sixth portal, rising and setting in the sixth portal for one-and-thirty mornings, because of its sign.
14. On that day the day gets longer than the night — the day becomes double the night: the day becomes twelve parts and the night is shortened and becomes six parts.
15. Then the sun climbs back to make the day shorter and the night longer: the sun goes back to the east, enters the sixth portal, and rises from it and sets for thirty mornings.
16. When the thirty mornings are done, the day shrinks by exactly one part and becomes eleven parts, and the night seven.
17. The sun goes out from that sixth portal in the west, travels to the east, and rises in the fifth portal for thirty mornings, and sets in the west again in the fifth western portal.
18. On that day the day shrinks by †two† parts and comes to ten parts, and the night to eight parts.
19. The sun goes out from that fifth portal and sets in the fifth portal of the west, then rises in the fourth portal for one-and-thirty mornings, because of its sign, and sets in the west.
20. On that day the day is made equal with the night, [and becomes of equal length]: the night comes to nine parts and the day to nine parts.
21. The sun rises from that portal and sets in the west, goes back to the east, and rises thirty mornings in the third portal, and sets in the west in the third portal.
22. On that day the night gets longer than the day — night gets longer than night and day shorter than day, till the thirtieth morning — and the night comes to exactly ten parts and the day to eight parts.
23. The sun rises from that third portal and sets in the third portal in the west, goes back to the east, and for thirty mornings rises in the second portal in the east, and likewise sets in the second portal in the west of the sky.
24. On that day the night comes to eleven parts and the day to seven parts.
25. On that day the sun rises from that second portal and sets in the west in the second portal, then goes back to the east into the first portal for one-and-thirty mornings, and sets in the first portal in the west of the sky.
26. On that day the night gets longer, twice the day: the night comes to exactly twelve parts and the day to six.
27. (And with that) the sun has crossed the divisions of his orbit and turns back on those divisions of his orbit, entering that portal for thirty mornings and setting in the west across from it.
28. On that night the night has grown shorter by a †ninth† part: the night has become eleven parts and the day seven parts.
29. The sun has gone back and entered the second portal in the east, and travels those divisions of his orbit for thirty mornings, rising and setting.
30. On that day the night grows shorter: the night comes to ten parts and the day to eight.
31. On that day the sun rises from that portal and sets in the west, goes back to the east, and rises in the third portal for one-and-thirty mornings, and sets in the west of the sky.
32. On that day the night shrinks and comes to nine parts, and the day to nine parts; night is equal to day, and the year is exactly three hundred and sixty-four days.
33. The length of the day and of the night, and the shortness of the day and of the night, come about — through the course of the sun these differences are made (that is, "they are separated").
34. So it comes about that his course gets longer by day and shorter by night.
35. This is the law and the course of the sun, and his turning back, as often as he turns back — sixty risings — that is, the great luminary named the sun, forever and ever.
36. What rises (in this way) is the great luminary, named for how it looks, as the Lord commanded.
37. As he rises, so he sets: he does not shrink and does not rest, but runs day and night. His light is seven times brighter than the moon's, but in size the two are equal.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 72:** the sun chapter — the whole 364-day portal scheme (six east, six west; 30/30/31-day months; the day-parts from 12:6 to 6:12 and back). The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none. No summary tables are rendered — full text only, disclosed.
- **"luminaries"/"luminary" kept (vv. 1–2, 4, 35–36):** technical term, literal per the standing rule; G3 will sweep it. "the luminary, the Sun" (v. 2) kept close to Charles's phrasing.
- **"heaven" → "sky" throughout this block:** plain register — in the Astronomical Book "heaven" almost always means the sky; disclosed as a block-wide plain move.
- **"portals" kept throughout:** Charles's word for the gates; not flattened to "gates" — G3 item. "windows" / "window-openings" kept as Charles prints them (v. 7 "window-openings" vs v. 3 "windows" — recorded, not harmonized).
- **"mornings" kept (vv. 8, 11, 13, ...):** Charles's "thirty mornings" for days of the month — kept literal; G3 item.
- **"his" for the sun (vv. 4–5, 15, 27, 29, 34–37):** Charles genders the sun masculine; the draft keeps "he/his" for the sun and "she/her" for the moon, as Charles does. Whether to keep the gendering stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"dureth till eternity" → "lasts forever" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"(therewith)" → "(And with that)" (v. 27):** plain register; disclosed.
- **Number forms:** Charles's forms are kept exactly — word numerals ("thirty", "twelve", "ten parts", "one-and-thirty", "three hundred and sixty-four") and his hyphenated "one-and-thirty" (vv. 13, 19, 25, 31). No digits occur in this chapter. The astronomy is not modernized or "corrected" — disclosed.
- **Daggers kept in the reading text (vv. 12, 18, 28):** as ch. 9 kept the v. 2 daggers. Charles's notes (sighted): v. 12 "†Two†. We should read 'one'"; v. 18 "For '†two†' read 'one'"; v. 28 "'ninth' ... The 'ninth', if original, must be of half the sun; for night and day cannot decrease or increase by more than 1/18th... Perhaps we might emend... and translate 'has the night grown shorter than the day by a ninth part'." The draft does not adopt the emendations — disclosed. The question of keeping the daggers was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **Square brackets kept visible (vv. 6, 20):** "[those six portals in the east]" (v. 6); "[and becomes of equal length]" (v. 20, bracketed as a duplicate rendering per the note). Whether reader-facing brackets stay stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **Round-bracket supplies absorbed or kept:** "(lit. 'that')" → "(that is, "that")" (v. 5); "(therewith)" → "(And with that)" (v. 27); "(lit. 'they are separated')" → "(that is, "they are separated")" (v. 33) — plain register, disclosed.
- **"the day becomes double the night" (v. 14) / "amounts to the double of the day" (v. 26):** kept close to Charles; "double" not flattened to "twice as long" — G3 item.
- **"mounts up" (v. 15):** kept — the sun's turn at the solstice; disclosed.
- **"on account of its sign" (vv. 13, 19):** kept literal; G3 item ("sign" across the section).
- **"sevenfold brighter" (v. 37):** kept; "as regards size they are both equal" → "in size the two are equal" — plain; disclosed.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with Aramaic control existing in principle for the section (4Q208–211) but consulted here only through Charles's printed footnotes as verified on the scans. Any future claim of Aramaic-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 73

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 73" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_73), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 156–158 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed, and no thick-type emendations occur in the main text of this chapter.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter LXXIII = vv. 1–8 exactly, spanning printed pp. 156–158; "LXXIV. 1." begins on p. 158 immediately after v. 8, under the italic sub-heading "The Lunar Year." The chapter opens on p. 156 under Charles's own italic centered sub-heading "The Moon and its Phases.", followed by the inline bold "LXXIII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER LXXIII." is a normalization; its "### LXXIII. The Moon and its Phases." line matches the print sub-heading). Running heads: "The Book of Enoch" center with "[Sect. III" top right (pp. 156, 158); "Sect. III]" top left with "Chapters LXXII. 34—LXXIII. 5" / "Chapters LXXIII. 6—LXXIV. 10" center (pp. 157, 159). **No thick type** in the main text of vv. 1–8 (both scans). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial):** "[in the commencement of the lunar day]" (v. 7). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(definite)" (v. 2), "(i.e. full)" (v. 3), "(and)" (v. 5), "(remaining)" (v. 8). No daggers, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in vv. 1–8. Bold word numerals are typography only.

1. And after this law I saw another law dealing with the smaller luminary, which is named the Moon.
2. And her circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and her chariot in which she rides is driven by the wind, and light is given to her in (definite) measure.
3. And her rising and setting change every month: and her days are like the days of the sun, and when her light is uniform (i.e. full) it amounts to the seventh part of the light of the sun.
4. And thus she rises. And her first phase in the east comes forth on the thirtieth morning: and on that day she becomes visible, and constitutes for you the first phase of the moon on the thirtieth day together with the sun in the portal where the sun rises.
5. And the one half of her goes forth by a seventh part, and her whole circumference is empty, without light, with the exception of one-seventh part of it, (and) the fourteenth part of her light.
6. And when she receives one-seventh part of the half of her light, her light amounts to one-seventh part and the half thereof.
7. And she sets with the sun, and when the sun rises the moon rises with him and receives the half of one part of light, and in that night in the beginning of her morning [in the commencement of the lunar day] the moon sets with the sun, and is invisible that night with the fourteen parts and the half of one of them.
8. And she rises on that day with exactly a seventh part, and comes forth and recedes from the rising of the sun, and in her remaining days she becomes bright in the (remaining) thirteen parts.

No wording corrections needed. The italic sub-heading "The Moon and its Phases." stands above "LXXIII. 1." on p. 156 in both scans.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. After this law I saw another law, about the smaller light, named the Moon.
2. Her circle is like the circle of the sky. The chariot she rides in is driven by the wind, and light is given to her in fixed measure.
3. Her rising and setting change every month. Her days are like the days of the sun, and when her light is even (that is, full) it comes to a seventh part of the light of the sun.
4. This is how she rises: her first phase in the east comes out on the thirtieth morning. On that day she becomes visible, and she marks for you the first phase of the moon on the thirtieth day, together with the sun, in the portal where the sun rises.
5. Half of her comes out by a seventh part. Her whole circle is empty, without light, except for one-seventh part of it, (and) the fourteenth part of her light.
6. When she takes in one-seventh part of half her light, her light comes to one-seventh part and half of that.
7. She sets with the sun. When the sun rises, the moon rises with him and takes in half of one part of light. In that night, at the start of her morning [at the start of the lunar day], the moon sets with the sun and cannot be seen that night, holding the fourteen parts and half of one of them.
8. She rises on that day with exactly a seventh part, comes out and pulls away from where the sun rises, and in her remaining days she grows bright in the remaining thirteen parts.

1. And I saw another course, a law for her, (and) how according to that law she performs her monthly revolution.
2. And all these Uriel, the holy angel who is the leader of them all, showed to me, and their positions, and I wrote down their positions as he showed them to me, and I wrote down their months as they were, and the appearance of their lights till fifteen days were accomplished.
3. In single seventh parts she accomplishes all her light in the east, and in single seventh parts accomplishes all her darkness in the west.
4. And in certain months she alters her settings, and in certain months she pursues her own peculiar course.
5. In two months the moon sets with the sun: in those two middle portals the third and the fourth.
6. She goes forth for seven days, and turns about and returns again through the portal where the sun rises, and accomplishes all her light: and she recedes from the sun, and in eight days enters the sixth portal from which the sun goes forth.
7. And when the sun goes forth from the fourth portal she goes forth seven days, until she goes forth from the fifth and turns back again in seven days into the fourth portal and accomplishes all her light: and she recedes and enters into the first portal in eight days.
8. And she returns again in seven days into the fourth portal from which the sun goes forth.
9. Thus I saw their position—how the moons rose and the sun set in those days.
10. And if five years are added together the sun has an overplus of thirty days, and all the days which accrue to it for one of those five years, when they are full, amount to 364 days.
11. And the overplus of the sun and of the stars amounts to six days: in 5 years 6 days every year come to 30 days: and the moon falls behind the sun and stars to the number of 30 days.
12. And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but **complete** the years with perfect justice in 364 days.
13. In 3 years there are 1,092 days, and in 5 years 1,820 days, so that in 8 years there are 2,912 days.
14. For the moon alone the days amount in 3 years to 1,062 days, and in 5 years she falls 50 days behind: [i.e. to the sum (of 1,770) there is to be added (1,000 and) 62 days.]
15. And in 5 years there are 1,770 days, so that for the moon the days in 8 years amount to 2,832 days.
16. [For in 8 years she falls behind to the amount of 80 days], all the days she falls behind in 8 years are 80.
17. And the year is accurately completed in conformity with their world-stations and the stations of the sun, which rise from the portals through which it (the sun) rises and sets 30 days.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. I saw another course, a law for her, (and) how by that law she makes her monthly round.
2. All these things Uriel, the holy angel who leads them all, showed me — their positions — and I wrote down their positions as he showed them to me, and I wrote down their months as they were, and how their lights looked, till fifteen days were done.
3. In single seventh parts she finishes all her light in the east, and in single seventh parts finishes all her darkness in the west.
4. In some months she changes her settings, and in some months she follows her own special course.
5. In two months the moon sets with the sun: in those two middle portals, the third and the fourth.
6. She goes out for seven days, turns around, and comes back again through the portal where the sun rises, and finishes all her light. She pulls away from the sun, and in eight days enters the sixth portal from which the sun goes out.
7. When the sun goes out from the fourth portal, she goes out for seven days, till she goes out from the fifth, then turns back again in seven days into the fourth portal and finishes all her light. She pulls away and enters the first portal in eight days.
8. She comes back again in seven days into the fourth portal from which the sun goes out.
9. This is how I saw their positions — how the moons rose and the sun set in those days.
10. If five years are put together, the sun has thirty days left over, and all the days that build up for one of those five years, when they are full, come to 364 days.
11. The sun's and the stars' leftover comes to six days: in 5 years, 6 days every year come to 30 days — and the moon falls behind the sun and stars by 30 days.
12. The sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly: they never move their position forward or back by a single day, forever — but complete the years with perfect fairness in 364 days.
13. In 3 years there are 1,092 days; in 5 years, 1,820 days; so in 8 years there are 2,912 days.
14. For the moon alone, the days come to 1,062 in 3 years, and in 5 years she falls 50 days behind: [that is, to the sum (of 1,770) there is to be added (1,000 and) 62 days.]
15. In 5 years there are 1,770 days, so for the moon the days in 8 years come to 2,832 days.
16. [For in 8 years she falls behind by 80 days] — all the days she falls behind in 8 years are 80.
17. The year is finished exactly, matching their world-stations and the stations of the sun, which rise from the portals through which it (the sun) rises and sets 30 days.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. The leaders of the heads of the thousands, who are set over the whole creation and over all the stars, also have to do with the four extra days — they cannot be separated from their post, by the year's reckoning — and they do service on the four days that are not counted in the year's reckoning.

4. In the same way Uriel showed me twelve doors, open in the circle of the sun's chariot in the sky, through which the sun's rays burst out. From them warmth spreads over the earth when they are opened at their set seasons.
5. [And for the winds and the spirit of the dew† when they are opened, standing open in the sky at the ends.]
6. As for the twelve portals in the sky at the ends of the earth, out of which go the sun, moon, and stars, and all the works of the sky in the east and in the west —
7. there are many windows open to the left and right of them, and one window at its set season gives warmth, matching (as these do) those doors from which the stars come out as He has commanded them, and in which they set according to their number.
8. I saw chariots in the sky, running in the world, above those portals in which turn the stars that never set.
9. One is bigger than all the rest, and it is the one that makes its course through the whole world.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 76

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 76" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_76), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 163–165 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed. One thick-type emendation invisible in the transcription was settled on the scans and is marked in the base below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter LXXVI = vv. 1–14 exactly, spanning printed pp. 163–165; "LXXVII. 1." begins on p. 165 immediately after v. 14, under the italic sub-heading "The Four Quarters of the World: the Seven Mountains, the Seven Rivers, &c." The chapter opens on p. 163 under Charles's own italic centered sub-heading "The Twelve Winds and their Portals.", followed by the inline bold "LXXVI. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER LXXVI." is a normalization; its "### LXXVI. The Twelve Winds and their Portals." line matches the print sub-heading). Running heads: "Sect. III]" top left with "Chapters LXXV. 3—LXXVI. 4" / "Chapters LXXVI. 5—LXXVII. 3" center (pp. 163, 165); "The Book of Enoch" center with "[Sect. III" top right (p. 164). **Thick type (Charles's emendation, invisible in the transcription):** "**quarters**" (v. 14, both scans, confirmed on zoomed crops — the v. 1 "quarters (of the heaven)" is regular type). **Daggers † (corrupt):** "†the north, and three [after those on the left] of the south†" (v. 3). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial):** "[after those on the left]" (v. 3, inside the daggers), "[four]" (v. 12). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(of the heaven)" (v. 1), "(i.e. the east)" / "(i.e. the south)" / "(i.e. the north)" (v. 2). No corner brackets, no angle brackets in vv. 1–14. Bold word numerals are typography only.

1. And at the ends of the earth I saw twelve portals open to all the quarters (of the heaven), from which the winds go forth and blow over the earth.
2. Three of them are open on the face (i.e. the east) of the heavens, and three in the west, and three on the right (i.e. the south) of the heaven, and three on the left (i.e. the north).
3. And the three first are those of the east, and three are of †the north, and three [after those on the left] of the south†, and three of the west.
4. Through four of these come winds of blessing and prosperity, and from those eight come hurtful winds: when they are sent, they bring destruction on all the earth and on the water upon it, and on all who dwell thereon, and on everything which is in the water and on the land.
5. And the first wind from those portals, called the east wind, comes forth through the first portal which is in the east, inclining towards the south: from it come forth desolation, drought, heat, and destruction.
6. And through the second portal in the middle comes what is fitting, and from it there come rain and fruitfulness and prosperity and dew; and through the third portal which lies toward the north come cold and drought.
7. And after these come forth the south winds through three portals: through the first portal of them inclining to the east comes forth a hot wind.
8. And through the middle portal next to it there come forth fragrant smells, and dew and rain, and prosperity and health.
9. And through the third portal lying to the west come forth dew and rain, locusts and desolation.
10. And after these the north winds: from the seventh portal in the east come dew and rain, locusts and desolation.
11. And from the middle portal come in a direct direction health and rain and dew and prosperity; and through the third portal in the west come cloud and hoar-frost, and snow and rain, and dew and locusts.
12. And after these [four] are the west winds: through the first portal adjoining the north come forth dew and hoar-frost, and cold and snow and frost.
13. And from the middle portal come forth dew and rain, and prosperity and blessing; and through the last portal which adjoins the south come forth drought and desolation, and burning and destruction.
14. And the twelve portals of the four **quarters** of the heaven are therewith completed, and all their laws and all their plagues and all their benefactions have I shown to thee, my son Methuselah.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 14 "**quarters**" stands in unmistakable thick type in both scans (zoomed crops compared against the regular-type "quarters (of the heaven)" in v. 1 on the same opening); Charles's footnote (sighted): "14. **Quarters.** MSS. read 'portals', i.e. θυρῶν corrupt for μερῶν, a rendering of רוחות." — marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. The v. 3 dagger pair encloses "the north, and three [after those on the left] of the south" with the square-bracketed clause inside the daggers — both scans. The v. 12 "[four]" is square-bracketed in both scans. Otherwise the transcription matched both scans word-for-word for vv. 1–14, including the parenthetical glosses in vv. 1–2 ("(of the heaven)", "(i.e. the east)", "(i.e. the south)", "(i.e. the north)"). ## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. At the ends of the earth I saw twelve portals open to all the quarters (of the sky), and the winds go out from them and blow over the earth.
2. Three of them are open on the face (that is, the east) of the skies, three in the west, three on the right (that is, the south) of the sky, and three on the left (that is, the north).
3. The first three are those of the east; three are of †the north, and three [after those on the left] of the south†; and three of the west.
4. Through four of these come winds of blessing and good fortune. From the other eight come harmful winds: when they are sent, they bring ruin on all the earth, on the water on it, on all who live on it, and on everything in the water and on the land.
5. The first wind from those portals, called the east wind, comes out through the first portal in the east, leaning toward the south. From it come ruin, drought, heat, and destruction.
6. Through the second portal in the middle comes what is fitting. From it come rain and fruitfulness, good fortune, and dew. Through the third portal, toward the north, come cold and drought.
7. After these come the south winds through three portals: through the first of them, leaning to the east, comes a hot wind.
8. Through the middle portal next to it come sweet smells, dew and rain, good fortune and health.
9. Through the third portal, toward the west, come dew and rain, locusts and ruin.
10. After these, the north winds: from the seventh portal in the east come dew and rain, locusts and ruin.
11. From the middle portal come — straight on — health and rain and dew and good fortune. Through the third portal in the west come cloud and frost, snow and rain, dew and locusts.
12. After these [four] come the west winds: through the first portal, next to the north, come dew and frost, cold and snow and ice.
13. From the middle portal come dew and rain, good fortune and blessing. Through the last portal, next to the south, come drought and ruin, burning and destruction.
14. With that, the twelve portals of the four quarters of the sky are finished, and I have shown you all their laws, all their plagues, and all their good gifts, my son Methuselah.

1. And the first **quarter** is called the east, because it is the first: and the second, the south, because the Most High **will descend** there, yea, there in quite a special sense will He who is blessed for ever **descend**.
2. And the west **quarter** is named the diminished, because there all the luminaries of the heaven wane and go down.
3. And the fourth **quarter**, named the north, is divided into three parts: the first of them is for the dwelling of men: and the second contains seas of water, and the abysses and forests and rivers, and darkness and clouds; and the third part contains the garden of righteousness.
4. I saw seven high mountains, higher than all the mountains which are on the earth: and thence comes forth hoar-frost, and days, seasons, and years pass away.
5. I saw seven rivers on the earth larger than all the rivers: one of them coming from the †west† pours its waters into the Great Sea.
6. And these two come from the north to the sea and pour their waters into the Erythraean Sea in the east.
7. And the remaining four come forth on the side of the north to their own sea, 〈two of them to〉 the Erythraean Sea, and two into the Great Sea and discharge themselves there [and some say: into the desert].
8. Seven great islands I saw in the sea and in the mainland: two in the mainland and five in the Great Sea.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** the five thick-type words in vv. 1–3 ("**quarter**" ×3, "**will descend**", "**descend**") stand in unmistakable heavy face in both scans — the Cornell grayscale copy shows the weight contrast most clearly; Charles's footnote (sighted): "1. ## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. The first quarter is called the east, because it is first. The second is the south, because the Most High will come down there — yes, there in a very special way He who is blessed forever will come down.
2. The west quarter is named "the diminished," because there all the lights of the sky fade and go down.
3. The fourth quarter, named the north, is split into three parts: the first is where men live; the second holds seas of water, the deep places, forests and rivers, darkness and clouds; and the third part holds the garden of righteousness.
4. I saw seven high mountains, higher than all the mountains on the earth. From there comes frost, and days, seasons, and years pass by.
5. I saw seven rivers on the earth, larger than all rivers. One of them, coming from the †west†, pours its waters into the Great Sea.
6. Two of them come from the north to the sea and pour their waters into the Erythraean Sea in the east.
7. The other four come out on the north side to their own sea — 〈two of them to〉 the Erythraean Sea, and two into the Great Sea — and empty themselves there [and some say: into the desert].
8. I saw seven great islands in the sea and on the mainland: two on the mainland and five in the Great Sea.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 77:** the quarters chapter — east/south/west/north, then the seven mountains, seven rivers, seven islands. The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none. No summary tables (full text only).
- **"heaven" → "sky" throughout this block:** plain register — in the Astronomical Book "heaven" almost always means the sky; disclosed as a block-wide plain move.
- **Thick-type emendations (vv. 1–3):** "**quarter**" (vv. 1–3), "**will descend**" / "**descend**" (v. 1) — Charles's own emendations, marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. - **"the garden of righteousness" kept (v. 3):** title-like phrase; G3 item.
- **"hoar-frost" → "frost" (v. 4):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"†west†" dagger kept (v. 5):** Charles's note (sighted): "One of them coming from the †west†. This must be the Nile, as Dillmann takes it, but the description 'from the west' cannot be right... ## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 78

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 78" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_78), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 166–169 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed, and no thick-type emendations occur in the main text of this chapter.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter LXXVIII = vv. 1–17 exactly, spanning printed pp. 166–169; "LXXIX. 1." begins on p. 169 immediately after v. 17, under the italic sub-heading "Recapitulation of several of the Laws." The chapter opens on p. 166 under Charles's own italic centered sub-heading "The Sun and Moon: the Waxing and Waning of the Moon.", followed by the inline bold "LXXVIII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER LXXVIII." is a normalization; its "### LXXVIII. The Sun and Moon: the Waxing and Waning of the Moon." line matches the print sub-heading). Running heads: "The Book of Enoch" center with "[Sect. III" top right (pp. 166, 168); "Sect. III]" top left with "Chapters LXXVII. 4—LXXVIII. 6" / "Chapters LXXVIII. 7—LXXIX. 2" center (pp. 167, 169). **No thick type** in the main text of vv. 1–17 (both scans). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial):** "[the light becomes full in her]" (v. 6), "[her light is accomplished in the heaven]" (v. 11). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(of)" (v. 15), "(of)" (v. 16). No daggers, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in vv. 1–17. Bold word numerals are typography only.

1. And the names of the sun are the following: the first Orjârês, and the second Tômâs.
2. And the moon has four names: the first name is Asônjâ, the second Eblâ, the third Benâsê, and the fourth Erâe.
3. These are the two great luminaries: their circumference is like the circumference of the heaven, and the size of the circumference of both is alike.
4. In the circumference of the sun there are seven portions of light which are added to it more than to the moon, and in definite measures it is transferred till the seventh portion of the sun is exhausted.
5. And they set and enter the portals of the west, and make their revolution by the north, and come forth through the eastern portals on the face of the heaven.
6. And when the moon rises one-fourteenth part appears in the heaven: [the light becomes full in her]: on the fourteenth day she accomplishes her light.
7. And fifteen parts of light are transferred to her till the fifteenth day (when) her light is accomplished, according to the sign of the year, and she becomes fifteen parts, and the moon grows by (the addition of) fourteenth parts.
8. And in her waning (the moon) decreases on the first day to fourteen parts of her light, on the second to thirteen parts of light, on the third to twelve, on the fourth to eleven, on the fifth to ten, on the sixth to nine, on the seventh to eight, on the eighth to seven, on the ninth to six, on the tenth to five, on the eleventh to four, on the twelfth to three, on the thirteenth to two, on the fourteenth to the half of a seventh, and all her remaining light disappears wholly on the fifteenth.
9. And in certain months the month has twenty-nine days and once twenty-eight.
10. And Uriel showed me another law: when light is transferred to the moon, and on which side it is transferred to her by the sun.
11. During all the period during which the moon is growing in her light, she is transferring it to herself when opposite to the sun during fourteen days [her light is accomplished in the heaven], and when she is illumined throughout, her light is accomplished full in the heaven.
12. And on the first day she is called the new moon, for on that day the light rises upon her.
13. She becomes full moon exactly on the day when the sun sets in the west, and from the east she rises at night, and the moon shines the whole night through till the sun rises over against her and the moon is seen over against the sun.
14. On the side whence the light of the moon comes forth, there again she wanes till all the light vanishes and all the days of the month are at an end, and her circumference is empty, void of light.
15. And three months she makes of thirty days, and at her time she makes three months of twenty-nine days each, in which she accomplishes her waning in the first period of time, and in the first portal for one hundred and seventy-seven days.
16. And in the time of her going out she appears for three months (of) thirty days each, and for three months she appears (of) twenty-nine each.
17. At night she appears like a man for twenty days each time, and by day she appears like the heaven, and there is nothing else in her save her light.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** the transcription matched both scans word-for-word for vv. 1–17 — wording, punctuation (the v. 6 colon before the bracketed clause, the v. 8 serial commas through the fourteen-to-two countdown), the two bracketed duplicate-rendering clauses (vv. 6, 11), and the v. 15 "(when)"/"(the addition of)" and v. 16 "(of)" supplies. Charles's notes (sighted): v. 6 "['The light becomes full in her'] (a-u). I have bracketed this clause as a duplicate rendering of τὸ φῶς πληροῖ (or τελεῖ)"; v. 11 "[Her light is accomplished in the heaven] ¹° ... Bracketed as a dittograph from the next clause." No wording corrections needed. The diacritic name-forms (Orjârês, Tômâs, Asônjâ, Eblâ, Benâsê, Erâe) match the transcription exactly in both scans.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. The names of the sun are these: the first is Orjârês, and the second Tômâs.
2. The moon has four names: the first is Asônjâ, the second Eblâ, the third Benâsê, and the fourth Erâe.
3. These are the two great lights: their circle is like the circle of the sky, and the size of the circle is the same for both.
4. In the circle of the sun there are seven portions of light added to it beyond the moon, and in fixed measures it is passed over till the seventh portion of the sun is used up.
5. They set and enter the portals of the west, circle around by the north, and come out through the eastern portals on the face of the sky.
6. When the moon rises, one-fourteenth part shows in the sky: [the light becomes full in her]. On the fourteenth day she finishes her light.
7. Fifteen parts of light are passed to her till the fifteenth day, when her light is finished, by the sign of the year. She becomes fifteen parts, and the moon grows by the adding of fourteenth parts.
8. As she wanes, the moon shrinks: on the first day to fourteen parts of her light, on the second to thirteen, on the third to twelve, on the fourth to eleven, on the fifth to ten, on the sixth to nine, on the seventh to eight, on the eighth to seven, on the ninth to six, on the tenth to five, on the eleventh to four, on the twelfth to three, on the thirteenth to two, on the fourteenth to half of a seventh — and all her remaining light is gone entirely on the fifteenth.
9. In some months the month has twenty-nine days, and once twenty-eight.
10. Uriel showed me another law: when light is passed to the moon, and on which side the sun passes it to her.
11. All the time the moon is growing in her light, she is drawing it to herself while facing the sun, for fourteen days [her light is finished in the sky]. When she is lit all through, her light is finished, full in the sky.
12. On the first day she is called the new moon, because on that day the light rises on her.
13. She becomes full moon exactly on the day the sun sets in the west. From the east she rises at night, and the moon shines all night long, till the sun rises facing her and the moon is seen facing the sun.
14. On the side where the moon's light comes out, she wanes again till all the light is gone and all the days of the month are ended, and her circle is empty, void of light.
15. She makes three months of thirty days, and in her season she makes three months of twenty-nine days each. In these she finishes her waning in the first stretch of time, and in the first portal, for one hundred and seventy-seven days.
16. When she goes out, she shows for three months of thirty days each, and for three months she shows twenty-nine each.
17. At night she looks like a man for twenty days at a time; by day she looks like the sky, and there is nothing else in her but her light.

1. And now, my son, I have shown you everything, and the law of all the stars of the sky is finished.
2. He showed me all the laws of these for every day, for every season of rule, for every year, for its going out, and for the order laid down for it every month and every week:

1. In those days the angel Uriel answered and said to me: "Look, I have shown you everything, Enoch. I have told you everything, so that you should see this sun and this moon, the leaders of the stars of the sky, and all those who turn them — their tasks, their times, and their departures.

They will change their orbits and tasks
and not appear at the seasons laid down for them.
7. The whole order of the stars will be hidden from the sinners.
The thoughts of those on the earth will go wrong about them —
[they will be changed from all their ways] —
yes, they will go wrong and take them for gods.
8. Evil will pile up on them,
and punishment will come on them
to wipe them all out."

1. And he said unto me:
'Observe, Enoch, these heavenly tablets,
And read what is written thereon,
And mark every individual fact.'
2. And I observed the heavenly tablets, and read everything which was written (thereon) and understood everything, and read the book of all the deeds of mankind, and of all the children of flesh that shall be upon the earth to the remotest generations.
3. And forthwith I blessed the great Lord the King of glory for ever, in that He has made all the works of the world,
And I extolled the Lord because of His patience,
And blessed Him because of the children of men.
4. And after that I said:
'Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness,
Concerning whom there is no book of unrighteousness written,
And against whom no day of judgement shall be found.'
5. And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: 'Declare everything to thy son Methuselah, and show to all thy children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of the Lord, for He is their Creator.
6. One year we will leave thee with thy son, till thou givest thy (last) commands, that thou mayst teach thy children and record (it) for them, and testify to all thy children; and in the second year they shall take thee from their midst.
7. Let thy heart be strong,
For the good shall announce righteousness to the good;
The righteous with the righteous shall rejoice,
And shall offer congratulation to one another.
8. But the sinners shall die with the sinners,
And the apostate go down with the apostate.
9. And those who practise righteousness shall die on account of the deeds of men,
And be taken away on account of the doings of the godless.'
10. And in those days they ceased to speak to me, and I came to my people, blessing the Lord of the world.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. He said to me: "Watch, Enoch — these heavenly tablets. Read what is written on them, and mark every single fact."
2. I looked at the heavenly tablets, read everything written on them, and understood everything. I read the book of all the deeds of mankind, and of all the children of flesh who will be on the earth, down to the farthest generations.
3. Right away I blessed the great Lord, the King of glory, forever, because He has made all the works of the world.
I praised the Lord for His patience,
and blessed Him for the children of men.
4. After that I said: "Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness — about whom no book of unrighteousness is written, and against whom no day of judgment will be found."
5. Those seven holy ones brought me and set me on the earth in front of the door of my house, and said to me: "Tell everything to your son Methuselah, and show all your children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of the Lord, for He is their Maker.
6. We will leave you with your son for one year, till you give your last commands, so you may teach your children, write it down for them, and bear witness to all your children. In the second year they will take you from among them.
7. Let your heart be strong:
the good will tell righteousness to the good;
the righteous will rejoice with the righteous
and congratulate one another.
8. But sinners will die with sinners,
and the turncoat will go down with the turncoat.
9. Those who practice righteousness will die because of what men do,
and be taken away because of what the godless do."
10. In those days they stopped speaking to me, and I came to my people, blessing the Lord of the world.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 82

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 82" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_82), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 174–178 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed. Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter LXXXII = vv. 1–20 exactly, spanning printed pp. 174–178; the Section IV introduction ("SECTION IV (CHAPTERS LXXXIII—XC) THE DREAM-VISIONS. INTRODUCTION") begins on p. 179 immediately after v. 20. The chapter opens on p. 174 under Charles's own italic centered sub-heading "Charge given to Enoch: the four Intercalary Days: the Stars which lead the Seasons and the Months.", followed by the inline bold "LXXXII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER LXXXII." is a normalization; its "### LXXXII. 1. And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to thee and writing down for thee, and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father's hand, and (see) that thou deliver them to the generations of the world.
2. I have given wisdom to thee and to thy children,
[And thy children that shall be to thee],
That they may give it to their children for generations,
This wisdom (namely) that passeth their thought.
3. And those who understand it shall not sleep,
But shall listen with the ear that they may learn this wisdom,
And it shall please those that eat thereof better than good food.
4. Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.
5. Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the **whole reckoning of the year**: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.
6. For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.
7. And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to **whom** the Lord of the whole creation of the world hath **subjected** the host of heaven.
8. And he has power over night and day in the heaven to cause the light to give light to men—sun, moon, and stars, and all the powers of the heaven which revolve in their circular chariots.
9. And these are the orders of the stars, which set in their places, and in their seasons and festivals and months.
10. And these are the names of those who lead them, who watch **that they** enter at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their periods of dominion, and in their positions.
11. Their four leaders who divide the four parts of the year enter first; and after them the twelve leaders of the orders who divide the months; and for the three hundred and sixty (days) there are heads over thousands who divide the days; and for the four intercalary days there are the leaders which sunder the four parts of the year.
12. And these heads over thousands are intercalated between leader and leader, each behind a station, but their leaders make the division.
13. And these are the names of the leaders who divide the four parts of the year which are ordained: Mîlkî'êl, Hel'emmêlêk, and Mêl'êjal, and Nârêl.
14. And the names of those who lead them: Adnâr'êl, and Îjâsûsa'êl, and 'Elômê'êl—these three follow the leaders of the orders, and there is one that follows the three leaders of the orders which follow those leaders of stations that divide the four parts of the year.
15. In the beginning of the year Melkejâl rises first and rules, who is named †Tam'âinî and sun,† and all the days of his dominion whilst he bears rule are ninety-one days.
16. And these are the signs of the days which are to be seen on earth in the days of his dominion: sweat, and heat, and calms; and all the trees bear fruit, and leaves are produced on all the trees, and the harvest of wheat, and the rose-flowers, and all the flowers which come forth in the field, but the trees of the winter season become withered.
17. And these are the names of the leaders which are under them: Berka'êl, Zêlebs'êl, and another who is added a head of a thousand, called Hîlujâseph: and the days of the dominion of this (leader) are at an end.
18. The next leader after him is Hel'emmêlêk, whom one names the shining sun, and all the days of his light are ninety-one days.
19. And these are the signs of (his) days on the earth: glowing heat and dryness, and the trees ripen their fruits and produce all their fruits ripe and ready, and the sheep pair and become pregnant, and all the fruits of the earth are gathered in, and everything that is in the fields, and the winepress: these things take place in the days of his dominion.
20. These are the names, and the orders, and the leaders of those heads of thousands: Gîdâ'ijal, Kê'êl, and Hê'êl, and the name of the head of a thousand which is added to them, Asfâ'êl: and the days of his dominion are at an end.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** the four thick-type emendations stand in unmistakable heavy face in both scans: "**whole reckoning of the year**" (v. 5; Charles's note, sighted: "So with Beer I correct baḥasāba kwellu 'ālam (= 'in the reckoning of the whole world') into bakwellu ḥasāba 'āmat"); "**whom**" and "**subjected**" (v. 7; note: "The text a-q, β reads za'azaza ... lita (= 'whom He hath commanded for me') which I have emended into za'azaza lotô = ὃ ἐτέταξε. But ἐτέταξε is corrupt for ὑπέταξε"); "**that they**" (v. 10; note: "Here the Ethiopic is literally 'who watch and enter'. But the context requires the rendering I have given"). All marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule. The v. 11 "three hundred and sixty (days)" is regular type in the main text in both scans (zoom-confirmed) — the footnote's own thick type there is footnote apparatus, not main text. The v. 15 "†Tam'âinî and sun,†" daggers, v. 2 bracketed interpolation line, and the four round-bracket supplies are all present in both scans exactly as transcribed. No wording corrections needed. The diacritic leader-names (vv. 13–14, 17, 20) match the transcription exactly in both scans.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And now, my son Methuselah, I am telling you all these things and writing them down for you. I have shown you everything and given you books about all of it. So keep safe, my son Methuselah, the books from your father's hand, and see to it that you hand them down to the generations of the world.
2. I have given wisdom to you and your children —
[and to your children who will come after you] —
so they may give it to their children for generations:
this wisdom that goes beyond what they can think.
3. Those who understand it will not sleep.
They will listen with their ears to learn this wisdom,
and it will please those who feed on it more than good food.
4. Blessed are all the righteous; blessed are all who walk in the way of righteousness and do not sin like the sinners, in the counting of all their days, in which the sun crosses the sky, going into and out of the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four added ones that split the four parts of the year, which lead them and go in with them for four days.
5. Because of them men go wrong and leave them out of the whole counting of the year — yes, men go wrong and do not mark them rightly.
6. For they belong to the year's counting and are truly written down forever: one in the first portal, one in the third, one in the fourth, and one in the sixth — and the year is finished in three hundred and sixty-four days.
7. The account of it is true, and the written counting of it exact. For Uriel has shown and told me the lights, the months and festivals, the years and days — Uriel, to whom the Lord of the whole creation of the world has put the host of heaven under.
8. He has power over night and day in the sky, to make the light give light to men — sun, moon, and stars, and all the powers of the sky that turn in their circling chariots.
9. These are the orders of the stars, which take their places in their seasons, festivals, and months.
10. These are the names of those who lead them, who watch that they come in at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their seasons of rule, and in their places.
11. Their four leaders who split the four parts of the year go in first. After them come the twelve leaders of the orders who split the months. For the three hundred and sixty days there are heads over thousands who split the days, and for the four extra days there are the leaders that cut apart the four parts of the year.
12. These heads over thousands are set in between leader and leader, each behind a station, but their leaders make the split.
13. These are the names of the leaders who split the four parts of the year, as ordained: Mîlkî'êl, Hel'emmêlêk, Mêl'êjal, and Nârêl.
14. And the names of those who lead them: Adnâr'êl, Îjâsûsa'êl, and 'Elômê'êl. These three follow the leaders of the orders, and there is one who follows the three leaders of the orders that follow those leaders of stations that split the four parts of the year.
15. At the start of the year Melkejâl rises first and rules — he is named †Tam'âinî and sun† — and all the days of his rule, while he rules, are ninety-one days.
16. These are the signs of the days to be seen on earth in the days of his rule: sweat, heat, and calm weather. All the trees bear fruit, leaves come out on all the trees — the wheat harvest, the rose-flowers, and all the flowers that come out in the field — but the trees of the winter season wither.
17. These are the names of the leaders under them: Berka'êl, Zêlebs'êl, and another, added as a head of a thousand, called Hîlujâseph. The days of this leader's rule are over.
18. The next leader after him is Hel'emmêlêk, whom people call the shining sun, and all the days of his light are ninety-one days.
19. These are the signs of his days on the earth: burning heat and dryness. The trees ripen their fruits and bring all their fruits ripe and ready; the sheep mate and become pregnant; all the fruits of the earth are gathered in, everything in the fields, and the winepress. These things happen in the days of his rule.
20. These are the names, the orders, and the leaders of those heads of thousands: Gîdâ'ijal, Kê'êl, and Hê'êl, and the name of the head of a thousand added to them, Asfâ'êl. The days of his rule are over.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 82:** the charge chapter — Enoch hands Methuselah the books and the wisdom, then the calendar's leadership roster: four year-dividers, twelve month-leaders, heads of thousands, the four intercalary leaders, and the named leaders of the first two ninety-one-day seasons (the roster breaks off after two). The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none. No summary tables (full text only).
- **"heaven" → "sky" throughout this block:** plain register — in the Astronomical Book "heaven" almost always means the sky; disclosed as a block-wide plain move.
- **Thick-type emendations:** "**whole reckoning of the year**" (v. 5), "**whom**" / "**subjected**" (v. 7), "**that they**" (v. 10) — Charles's own emendations, marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule (notes sighted, see Print-level findings). Whether the reading text signals the emendations stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"my son Methuselah" kept (v. 1):** the addressee formula; G3 item.
- **"thee/thy/thou" → "you/your" (vv. 1–2):** Thou-forms modernized per the ch. 9 standing decision —
- **"(see)" absorbed (v. 1):** "see to it that you hand them down" — plain; disclosed.
- **"that passeth their thought" → "that goes beyond what they can think" (v. 2):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"[And thy children that shall be to thee]," kept visible (v. 2):** Charles's bracket ("Bracketed as an interpolation" per the note). Rendered "[and to your children who will come after you]" — disclosed.
- **"it shall please those that eat thereof" → "it will please those who feed on it" (v. 3):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"in the reckoning of all their days" → "in the counting of all their days" (v. 4):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"which are intercalated" → "the four added ones" (v. 4); "intercalary days" → "extra days" (v. 11):** plain register — flagged for G3 against ch. 75's kept "intercalary".
- **"shall be at fault" → "go wrong" (v. 5):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"(thereon)" absorbed (v. 6):** "truly written down forever" — plain; disclosed.
- **"hath subjected" → "has put ... under" (v. 7):** plain register — "has put the host of heaven under [him]" (the "him" supplied for sense; disclosed).
- **"luminaries" → "lights" (v. 7):** plain register — flagged for G3 against ch. 72's kept "luminaries".
- **"men—sun, moon, and stars" em-dash kept (v. 8):** Charles's apposition; disclosed.
- **"which set in their places" → "which take their places" (v. 9):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"periods of dominion" → "seasons of rule" (v. 10); "dominion" → "rule" (vv. 15–20):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"sunder" → "cut apart" (v. 11); "divide" → "split" (vv. 11–14):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"a station" kept (v. 12):** Charles's note: "A station. q, a read 'his station'"; the draft keeps "a station" with Charles — disclosed.
- **The fourteen leader-names kept with Charles's diacritics (vv. 13–14, 17–18, 20):** copied exactly from the print; Charles's notes (sighted) discuss Semitic etymologies (recorded as apparatus, not imported). The question whether the diacritic forms stand for readers was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"†Tam'âinî and sun,†" dagger kept (v. 15):** Charles's note (sighted): "The leader of this period is named 'Tam'âinî' and 'sun'." The draft does not resolve the corruption — disclosed.
- **"calms" → "calm weather" (v. 16):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"the sheep pair" → "the sheep mate" (v. 19):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"(leader)" / "(his)" absorbed (vv. 17, 19):** "this leader's rule"; "his days" — plain; disclosed.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with Aramaic control existing in principle for the section (4Q208–211) but consulted here only through Charles's printed footnotes as verified on the scans.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 83

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 83" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_83), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Scan verification of the base against both IA 1912 copies at G1 — see "Print-level findings" below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts: pp. 182–183 in both scans; inline bold 'LXXXIII. 1.'; section head 'LXXXIII—LXXXIV. First Dream-Vision on the Deluge.'; running head 'Chapter LXXXIII. 1—11'. Full details in the G1 Audit Record below.

1. And now, my son Methuselah, I will show thee all my visions which I have seen, recounting them before thee.
2. Two visions I saw before I took a wife, and the one was quite unlike the other: the first when I was learning to write: the second before I took thy mother, (when) I saw a terrible vision.
3. And regarding them I prayed to the Lord. I had laid me down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, (when) I saw in a vision how the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth.
4. And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and high trees were rent from their stems, and hurled down and sunk in the abyss.
5. And thereupon a word fell into my mouth, and I lifted up (my voice) to cry aloud, and said: 'The earth is destroyed.'
6. And my grandfather Mahalalel waked me as I lay near him, and said unto me: 'Why dost thou cry so, my son, and why dost thou make such lamentation?'
7. And I recounted to him the whole vision which I had seen, and he said unto me: 'A terrible thing hast thou seen, my son, and of grave moment is thy dream-vision as to the secrets of all the sin of the earth: it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction.
8. And now, my son, arise and make petition to the Lord of glory, since thou art a believer, that a remnant may remain on the earth, and that He may not destroy the whole earth.
9. My son, from heaven all this will come upon the earth, and upon the earth there will be great destruction.
10. After that I arose and prayed and implored and besought, and wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world, and I will show everything to thee, my son Methuselah.
11. And when I had gone forth below and seen the heaven, and the sun rising in the east, and the moon setting in the west, and a few stars, and the whole earth, and everything as †He had known† it in the beginning, then I blessed the Lord of judgement and extolled Him because He had made the sun to go forth from the windows of the east, †and he ascended and rose on the face of the heaven, and set out and kept traversing the path shown unto him.

**Print-level findings (both scans):** V. 11's two daggered clauses ('†He had known†', '†and he ascended and rose on the face of the heaven†') confirmed on both scans; no square brackets, no thick type, no corner-marks in this chapter; no material transcription-vs-print wording differences (see G1 items 3–4).

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And now, my son Methuselah, I will show you all the visions I have seen, telling them over before you.
2. I saw two visions before I took a wife, and the one was quite unlike the other: the first when I was learning to write; the second, before I took your mother, when I saw a terrible vision.
3. And about them I prayed to the Lord. I had lain down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, when I saw in a vision how the sky collapsed and was carried off and fell to the earth.
4. And when it fell to the earth, I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss: mountains piled on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and tall trees were torn from their roots, thrown down, and sunk in the abyss.
5. Then a word fell into my mouth, and I lifted up my voice to cry aloud, and said: "The earth is destroyed."
6. And my grandfather Mahalalel woke me as I lay near him, and said to me: "Why are you crying so, my son, and why are you wailing?"
7. And I told him the whole vision I had seen, and he said to me: "A terrible thing you have seen, my son, and your dream-vision carries grave weight — it holds the secrets of all the sin of the earth: it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction.
8. And now, my son, get up and make your plea to the Lord of glory — since you are a believer — that a remnant may be left on the earth, and that He may not destroy the whole earth.
9. My son, all this will come upon the earth from heaven, and on the earth there will be great destruction.
10. After that I got up and prayed and pleaded and begged, and wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world, and I will show everything to you, my son Methuselah.
11. And when I had gone out below and seen the sky, and the sun rising in the east, and the moon setting in the west, and a few stars, and the whole earth, and everything as †He had known† it in the beginning, then I blessed the Lord of judgement and praised Him, because He had made the sun go out from the windows of the east, †and he rose and climbed across the face of the sky, and set out and kept travelling the path shown to him.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 83:** the first dream-vision — Enoch recounts to Methuselah the terrible vision seen before his marriage (the Deluge vision), Mahalalel's interpretation, and Enoch's written prayer. The draft keeps Charles's structure and adds none.
- **Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your (vv. 1–2, 6–8, 10):** plain register, per the ch. 9 decision. "thee" → "you" (vv. 1, 10); "thy mother" → "your mother" (v. 2); "dost thou cry" → "are you crying" (v. 6); "thou art" → "you are", "thou hast seen" → "you have seen" (vv. 7–8). Disclosed;
- **"(when)" ×3 (vv. 2, 3) and "(my voice)" (v. 5):** Charles's round-bracket supplies, absorbed into plain English per the ch. 1 standing rule; disclosed. The question whether "when" should stand bracketed for readers was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"recounting them before thee" → "telling them over before you" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"the heaven ... was borne off" → "the sky ... was carried off" (v. 3):** "borne off" is archaic; "heaven" → "sky" here is the visible sky (contrast ch. 9's "gates of heaven", kept). Recorded for the G3 sweep — do not harmonize now.
- **"mountains were suspended on mountains" → "mountains piled on mountains" (v. 4):** plain register; disclosed. "high trees were rent from their stems" → "tall trees were torn from their roots" — "rent" is archaic; disclosed.
- **"thereupon" → "Then" (v. 5):** plain register; disclosed.

and nothing is too hard for You.
Wisdom does not leave the place of Your throne,
nor turn away from Your presence.
You know and see and hear everything,
and nothing is hidden from You [for You see everything].
4. And now the angels of Your heavens stand guilty of trespass,
and on the flesh of men Your anger rests until the great day of judgement.
5. And now, O God and Lord and Great King,
I plead with You and beg You to answer my prayer:
leave me descendants on earth,
and do not destroy all human flesh,
and do not make the earth without inhabitants,
so that destruction would never end.
6. And now, my Lord, destroy from the earth the flesh that has stirred up Your anger,
but set up the flesh of righteousness and uprightness as a plant of the everlasting seed,
and do not hide Your face from the prayer of Your servant, O Lord."

1. And after this I saw another dream, and I will show you the whole dream, my son.
2. And Enoch raised his voice and spoke to his son Methuselah: "To you, my son, I will speak: hear my words — turn your ear to your father's dream-vision.

4. And that black bull gored the red one and chased him across the earth, and then I could no longer see that red bull.
5. But that black bull grew, and that heifer went with him, and I saw that many oxen came from him, which looked like him and followed him."
6. And that cow, that first one, left the presence of that first bull to look for that red one, but did not find him; and she mourned for him with loud mourning, and kept searching for him.
7. And I watched until that first bull came to her and calmed her, and from that time on she cried no more.
8. And after that she bore another white bull, and after him she bore many bulls and black cows.
9. And I saw in my sleep that that white bull also grew and became a great white bull, and from him came many white bulls, and they looked like him.
10. And they began to father many white bulls, which looked like them, one after another — a great many.

3. And those three who had come out last took me by the hand and lifted me up, away from the generations of the earth, and set me on a high place, and showed me a tower raised high above the earth, while all the hills lay lower.
4. And one said to me: "Stay here until you see everything that happens to those elephants, camels, and donkeys, and the stars and the oxen — all of them."
