# WORKSHEET — 1 Enoch, Chapter 89

> DRAFT — clear-English rendering prepared with AI assistance; a translation of a translation (Ge'ez from lost Hebrew/Aramaic and Greek stages); not reviewed by a Ge'ez scholar; not finished. State: AUDITED — G1 worker self-audit passed (see G1 Audit Record); G2 and G3 passed on 2026-10-12; G4 read-through ruled read by Robert on 2026-10-14. Never claim finished, first, or definitive.

- **Chapter:** 89 (Section IV, Book of Dream Visions, ch. 83–90; the Animal Apocalypse's long middle — the Deluge and Noah (1–9); Noah to the Exodus (10–27); desert, Law, and entry into the land (28–40); Judges to the Temple (41–50); the two kingdoms to the destruction of Jerusalem (51–67); the seventy shepherds, first period (68–71); second period, Cyrus to Alexander (72–77). Charles's subsection heads divide the chapter into seven blocks, listed in the base below.)
- **Witness status:** Ge'ez complete + partial Greek control (**Vat. ## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 89

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 89" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_89), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Scan verification of the base against both IA 1912 copies at G1 — see "Print-level findings" below. Charles's seven subsection heads are carried in the base as printed (see print findings for their exact form).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts: pp. 190–204 in both scans; inline bold 'LXXXIX. 1.'; Charles's seven subsection heads (centered small caps); the Vatican Greek fragment (Gr. 1809) printed as a parallel smaller-type column beside the English at vv. 42–49. Full details in the G1 Audit Record below.

*LXXXIX. 1-9. The Deluge and the Deliverance of Noah.*

1. And one of those four went to that white bull and instructed him in a secret, without his being terrified: he was born a bull and became a man, and built for himself a great vessel and dwelt thereon; and three bulls dwelt with him in that vessel and they were covered in.
2. And again I raised mine eyes towards heaven and saw a lofty roof, with seven water torrents thereon, and those torrents flowed with much water into an enclosure.
3. And I saw again, and behold fountains were opened on the surface of that great enclosure, and that water began to swell and rise upon the surface, and I saw that enclosure till all its surface was covered with water.
4. And the water, the darkness, and mist increased upon it; and as I looked at the height of that water, that water had risen above the height of that enclosure, and was streaming over that enclosure, and it stood upon the earth.
5. And all the cattle of that enclosure were gathered together until I saw how they sank and were swallowed up and perished in that water.
6. But that vessel floated on the water, while all the oxen and elephants and camels and asses sank to the bottom with all the animals, so that I could no longer see them, and they were not able to escape, (but) perished and sank into the depths.
7. And again I saw in the vision till those water torrents were removed from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were levelled up and other abysses were opened.
8. Then the water began to run down into these, till the earth became visible; but that vessel settled on the earth, and the darkness retired and light appeared.
9. But that white bull which had become a man came out of that vessel, and the three bulls with him, and one of those three was white like that bull, and one of them was red as blood, and one black: and that white bull departed from them.

*LXXXIX. 10-27. From the Death of Noah to the Exodus.*

10. And they began to bring forth beasts of the field and birds, so that there arose different genera: lions, tigers, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, squirrels, swine, falcons, vultures, kites, eagles, and ravens; and among them was born a white bull.
11. And they began to bite one another; but that white bull which was born amongst them begat a wild ass and a white bull with it, and the wild asses multiplied.
12. But that bull which was born from him begat a black wild boar and a white sheep; and the former begat many boars, but that sheep begat twelve sheep.
13. And when those twelve sheep had grown, they gave up one of them to the asses, and those asses again gave up that sheep to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves.
14. And the Lord brought the eleven sheep to live with it and to pasture with it among the wolves: and they multiplied and became many flocks of sheep.
15. And the wolves began to fear them, and they oppressed them until they destroyed their little ones, and they cast their young into a river of much water: but those sheep began to cry aloud on account of their little ones, and to complain unto their Lord.
16. And a sheep which had been saved from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild asses; and I saw the sheep how they lamented and cried, and besought their Lord with all their might, till that Lord of the sheep descended at the voice of the sheep from a lofty abode, and came to them and pastured them.
17. And He called that sheep which had escaped the wolves, and spake with it concerning the wolves that it should admonish them not to touch the sheep.
18. And the sheep went to the wolves according to the word of the Lord, and another sheep met it and went with it, and the two went and entered together into the assembly of those wolves, and spake with them and admonished them not to touch the sheep from henceforth.
19. And thereupon I saw the wolves, and how they oppressed the sheep exceedingly with all their power; and the sheep cried aloud.
20. And the Lord came to the sheep and they began to smite those wolves: and the wolves began to make lamentation; but the sheep became quiet and forthwith ceased to cry out.
21. And I saw the sheep till they departed from amongst the wolves; but the eyes of the wolves were blinded, and those wolves departed in pursuit of the sheep with all their power.
22. And the Lord of the sheep went with them, as their leader, and all His sheep followed Him: and His face was dazzling and glorious and terrible to behold.
23. But the wolves began to pursue those sheep till they reached a sea of water.
24. And that sea was divided, and the water stood on this side and on that before their face, and their Lord led them and placed Himself between them and the wolves.
25. And as those wolves did not yet see the sheep, they proceeded into the midst of that sea, and the wolves followed the sheep, and [those wolves] ran after them into that sea.
26. And when they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to flee before His face, but that sea gathered itself together, and became as it had been created, and the water swelled and rose till it covered those wolves.
27. And I saw till all the wolves who pursued those sheep perished and were drowned.

*LXXXIX. 28-40. Israel in the Desert, the Giving of the Law, the Entrance into Palestine.*

28. But the sheep escaped from that water and went forth into a wilderness, where there was no water and no grass; and they began to open their eyes and to see; and I saw the Lord of the sheep pasturing them and giving them water and grass, and that sheep going and leading them.
29. And that sheep ascended to the summit of that lofty rock, and the Lord of the sheep sent it to them.
30. And after that I saw the Lord of the sheep who stood before them, and His appearance was great and terrible and majestic, and all those sheep saw Him and were afraid before His face.
31. And they all feared and trembled because of Him, and they cried to that sheep with them [which was amongst them]: 'We are not able to stand before our Lord or to behold Him.'
32. And that sheep which led them again ascended to the summit of that rock, but the sheep began to be blinded and to wander from the way which he had showed them, but that sheep wot not thereof.
33. And the Lord of the sheep was wrathful exceedingly against them, and that sheep discovered it, and went down from the summit of the rock, and came to the sheep, and found the greatest part of them blinded and fallen away.
34. And when they saw it they feared and trembled at its presence, and desired to return to their folds.
35. And that sheep took other sheep with it, and came to those sheep which had fallen away, and began to slay them; and the sheep feared its presence, and thus that sheep brought back those sheep that had fallen away, and they returned to their folds.
36. And I saw in this vision till that sheep became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep, and placed all the sheep in that house.
37. And I saw till this sheep which had met that sheep which led them fell asleep: and I saw till all the great sheep perished and little ones arose in their place, and they came to a pasture, and approached a stream of water.
38. Then that sheep, their leader which had become a man, withdrew from them and fell asleep, and all the sheep sought it and cried over it with a great crying.
39. And I saw till they left off crying for that sheep and crossed that stream of water, and there arose the two sheep as leaders in the place of those which had led them and fallen asleep (lit. 'had fallen asleep and led them').
40. And I saw till the sheep came to a goodly place, and a pleasant and glorious land, and I saw till those sheep were satisfied; and that house stood amongst them in the pleasant land.

*LXXXIX. 41-50. From the Time of the Judges till the Building of the Temple.*

41. And sometimes their eyes were opened, and sometimes blinded, till another sheep arose and led them and brought them all back, and their eyes were opened.
42. And the dogs and the foxes and the wild boars began to devour those sheep till the Lord of the sheep raised up [another sheep] a ram from their midst, which led them.
43. And that ram began to butt on either side those dogs, foxes, and wild boars till he had destroyed them †all†.
44. And that sheep whose eyes were opened saw that ram, which was amongst the sheep, till it †forsook its glory† and began to butt those sheep, and trampled upon them, and behaved itself unseemly.
45. And the Lord of the sheep sent the lamb to another lamb and raised it to being a ram and leader of the sheep instead of that ram which had †forsaken its glory†.
46. And it went to it and spake to it alone, and raised it to being a ram, and made it the prince and leader of the sheep; but during all these things those dogs oppressed the sheep.
47. And the first ram pursued that second ram, and that second ram arose and fled before it; and I saw till those dogs pulled down the first ram.
48. And that second ram arose and led the [little] sheep.
49. And those sheep grew and multiplied; but all the dogs, and foxes, and wild boars feared and fled before it, and that ram butted and killed the wild beasts, and those wild beasts had no longer any power among the sheep and robbed them no more of ought.
48b. And that ram begat many sheep and fell asleep; and a little sheep became ram in its stead, and became prince and leader of those sheep.

[At vv. 42–49 Charles prints the Vatican Greek fragment (Gr. 1809) as a parallel smaller-type column beside the English, with his headnote — layout verified on both scans; see Notes.]

50. And that house became great and broad, and it was built for those sheep: (and) a tower lofty and great was built on the house for the Lord of the sheep, and that house was low, but the tower was elevated and lofty, and the Lord of the sheep stood on that tower and they offered a full table before Him.

*LXXXIX. 51-67. The Two Kingdoms of Israel and Judah to the Destruction of Jerusalem.*

51. And again I saw those sheep that they again erred and went many ways, and forsook that their house, and the Lord of the sheep called some from amongst the sheep and sent them to the sheep, but the sheep began to slay them.
52. And one of them was saved and was not slain, and it sped away and cried aloud over the sheep; and they sought to slay it, but the Lord of the sheep saved it from the sheep, and brought it up to me, and caused it to dwell there.
53. And many other sheep He sent to those sheep to testify unto them and lament over them.
54. And after that I saw that when they forsook the house of the Lord and His tower they fell away entirely, and their eyes were blinded; and I saw the Lord of the sheep how He wrought much slaughter amongst them in their herds until those sheep invited that slaughter and betrayed His place.
55. And He gave them over into the hands of the lions and tigers, and wolves and hyenas, and into the hand of the foxes, and to all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear in pieces those sheep.
56. And I saw that He forsook that their house and their tower and gave them all into the hand of the lions, to tear and devour them, into the hand of all the wild beasts.
57. And I began to cry aloud with all my power, and to appeal to the Lord of the sheep, and to represent to Him in regard to the sheep that they were devoured by all the wild beasts.
58. But He remained unmoved, though He saw it, and rejoiced that they were devoured and swallowed and robbed, and left them to be devoured in the hand of all the beasts.
59. And He called seventy shepherds, and cast those sheep to them that they might pasture them, and He spake to the shepherds and their companions: 'Let each individual of you pasture the sheep henceforward, and everything that I shall command you that do ye.
60. And I will deliver them over unto you duly numbered, and tell you which of them are to be destroyed—and them destroy ye.' And He gave over unto them those sheep.
61. And He called another and spake unto him: 'Observe and mark everything that the shepherds will do to those sheep; for they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them.
62. And every excess and the destruction which will be wrought through the shepherds, record (namely) how many they destroy according to my command, and how many according to their own caprice: record against every individual shepherd all the destruction he effects.
63. And read out before me by number how many they destroy, and how many they deliver over for destruction, that I may have this as a testimony against them, and know every deed of the shepherds, that I may **comprehend** and see what they do, whether or not they abide by my command which I have commanded them.
64. But they shall not know it, and thou shalt not declare it to them, nor admonish them, but only record against each individual all the destruction which the shepherds effect each in his time and lay it all before me.'
65. And I saw till those shepherds pastured in their season, and they began to slay and to destroy more than they were bidden, and they delivered those sheep into the hand of the lions.
66. And the lions and tigers eat and devoured the greater part of those sheep, and the wild boars eat along with them; and they burnt that tower and demolished that house.
67. And I became exceedingly sorrowful over that tower because that house of the sheep was demolished, and afterwards I was unable to see if those sheep entered that house.

*LXXXIX. 68-71. First Period of the Angelic Rulers—from the Destruction of Jerusalem to the Return from the Captivity.*

68. And the shepherds and their associates delivered over those sheep to all the wild beasts, to devour them, and each one of them received in his time a definite number: it was written by the other in a book how many each one of them destroyed of them.
69. And each one slew and destroyed many more than was prescribed; and I began to weep and lament on account of those sheep.
70. And thus in the vision I saw that one who wrote, how he wrote down every one that was destroyed by those shepherds, day by day, and carried up and laid down and showed actually the whole book to the Lord of the sheep—(even) everything that they had done, and all that each one of them had made away with, and all that they had given over to destruction.
71. And the book was read before the Lord of the sheep, and He took the book from his hand and read it and sealed it and laid it down.

*LXXXIX. 72-77. Second Period—from the Time of Cyrus to that of Alexander the Great.*

72. And forthwith I saw how the shepherds pastured for twelve hours, and behold three of those sheep turned back and came and entered and began to build up all that had fallen down of that house; but the wild boars tried to hinder them, but they were not able.
73. And they began again to build as before, and they reared up that tower, and it was named the high tower; and they began again to place a table before the tower, but all the bread on it was polluted and not pure.
74. And as touching all this the eyes of those sheep were blinded so that they saw not, and (the eyes of) their shepherds likewise; and they delivered them in large numbers to their shepherds for destruction, and they trampled the sheep with their feet and devoured them.
75. And the Lord of the sheep remained unmoved till all the sheep were dispersed over the field and mingled with them (i.e. the beasts), and they (i.e. the shepherds) did not save them out of the hand of the beasts.
76. And this one who wrote the book carried it up, and showed it and read it before the Lord of the sheep, and implored Him on their account, and besought Him on their account as he showed Him all the doings of the shepherds, and gave testimony before Him against all the shepherds.
77. And he took the actual book and laid it down beside Him and departed.

**Print-level findings (both scans):** THREE material transcription-vs-print corrections, all confirmed on both scans: (a) 48b prints AFTER v. 49 ('48ᵇ'); (b) v. 50's supply is round brackets '(and)', not '〈and〉'; (c) v. 77 carries NO closing quote (the v. 61–64 speech closes at v. 64). '**comprehend**' (v. 63) confirmed as Charles's thick-type emendation on both scans at high resolution. All dagger, bracket, and supply markings confirmed (see G1 items 3–4).

## Control column (labelled, not independently transcribed in this lane)

- **Ge'ez (Charles 1906, 23 MSS):** the ultimate source of Charles 1912. Not opened as an independent control column here — Route A only.
- **Greek (Vat. Gr. 1809, at 89:42–49):** Charles prints the Vatican Greek fragment at vv. 42–49 — the one Greek control in this block. Its layout in the 1912 print, and its verse-level forks against the English main text, are settled on the scans and recorded in the Notes; no Greek wording is independently transcribed in this lane.
- **Aramaic (Qumran):** 4Q204–207 preserve Dream Visions scraps (the section generally, notably around the Animal Apocalypse). No Aramaic wording is claimed for ch. 89 here.
- **Laurence (1821, PD, check-only):** not consulted as a skeleton in this slice; Laurence's 105-chapter numbering is never mapped onto the 108.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And one of those four went to that white bull and taught him a secret, without frightening him. He was born a bull and became a man, and built himself a great vessel and lived in it; and three bulls lived with him in that vessel, and they were shut inside.
2. And again I raised my eyes toward heaven and saw a high roof, with seven torrents of water on it, and those torrents poured much water into an enclosure.
3. And I looked again — and look — springs were opened on the surface of that great enclosure, and the water began to swell and rise over the surface, and I watched that enclosure until its whole surface was covered with water.
4. And the water, the darkness, and the mist grew over it; and as I watched the rising of that water, it had risen above the top of that enclosure, and was pouring over that enclosure, and it stood upon the earth.
5. And all the cattle of that enclosure were herded together, until I saw how they sank and were swallowed up and died in that water.
6. But that vessel floated on the water, while all the oxen and elephants and camels and donkeys sank to the bottom with all the animals, so that I could no longer see them; they could not escape — they died and sank into the depths.
7. And again I saw in the vision, until those torrents of water were taken away from that high roof, and the cracks in the earth were filled in and other depths were opened.
8. Then the water began to run down into them, until the earth could be seen; but that vessel came to rest on the earth, and the darkness drew back and light appeared.
9. But that white bull which had become a man came out of that vessel, with the three bulls with him; and one of those three was white like that bull, and one of them was red as blood, and one black — and that white bull left them.
10. And they began to bring forth wild animals and birds, so that different kinds arose: lions, tigers, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, squirrels, pigs, falcons, vultures, kites, eagles, and ravens; and among them a white bull was born.
11. And they began to bite one another; but that white bull which was born among them fathered a wild donkey and a white bull along with it, and the wild donkeys multiplied.
12. But that bull which was born from him fathered a black wild boar and a white sheep; and the boar fathered many boars, but that sheep fathered twelve sheep.
13. And when those twelve sheep had grown, they handed one of them over to the donkeys, and those donkeys in turn handed that sheep over to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves.
14. And the Lord brought the eleven sheep to live with it and to graze with it among the wolves; and they multiplied and became many flocks of sheep.
15. And the wolves began to fear them, and they crushed them until they destroyed their little ones, and threw their young into a river of deep water; but those sheep began to cry out loud over their little ones, and to plead with their Lord.
16. And a sheep that had been saved from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild donkeys; and I saw how the sheep grieved and cried, and begged their Lord with all their strength, until that Lord of the sheep came down at the voice of the sheep from His high dwelling, and came to them and fed them.
17. And He called that sheep which had escaped the wolves, and spoke with it about the wolves — that it should warn them not to touch the sheep.
18. And the sheep went to the wolves as the Lord had said, and another sheep met it and went with it, and the two went and entered together into the gathering of those wolves, and spoke with them and warned them not to touch the sheep from then on.
19. And then I saw the wolves, and how they crushed the sheep fiercely with all their power; and the sheep cried out loud.
20. And the Lord came to the sheep, and they began to strike those wolves; and the wolves began to wail — but the sheep grew quiet and at once stopped crying out.
21. And I watched the sheep until they got away from among the wolves; but the eyes of the wolves were blinded, and those wolves set out after the sheep with all their power.
22. And the Lord of the sheep went with them as their leader, and all His sheep followed Him; and His face was dazzling and glorious and fearsome to look at.
23. But the wolves kept chasing those sheep until they reached a sea of water.
24. And that sea was split, and the water stood on this side and on that before them, and their Lord led them and put Himself between them and the wolves.
25. And since those wolves still could not see the sheep, they went on into the middle of that sea — and the wolves followed the sheep, and [those wolves] ran after them into that sea.
26. And when they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to run from before His face; but that sea closed back together and became as it had been made, and the water swelled and rose until it covered those wolves.
27. And I watched until all the wolves that had chased those sheep died and were drowned.
28. But the sheep escaped from that water and went out into a wilderness, where there was no water and no grass; and they began to open their eyes and see. And I saw the Lord of the sheep feeding them and giving them water and grass, and that sheep going ahead and leading them.
29. And that sheep climbed to the top of that high rock, and the Lord of the sheep sent it down to them.
30. And after that I saw the Lord of the sheep standing before them, and He looked great and fearsome and majestic, and all those sheep saw Him and were afraid before His face.
31. And they all feared and shook because of Him, and they cried to that sheep with them [which was among them]: "We cannot stand before our Lord or look at Him."
32. And that sheep which led them climbed back to the top of that rock, but the sheep began to go blind and to wander from the path he had shown them — and that sheep did not know it.
33. And the Lord of the sheep was fiercely angry with them, and that sheep found out, and came down from the top of the rock, and went to the sheep, and found most of them blind and fallen away.
34. And when they saw it they feared and shook at its coming, and wanted to go back to their folds.
35. And that sheep took other sheep with it, and went to those sheep that had fallen away, and began to kill them; and the sheep feared its coming — and so that sheep brought back those sheep that had fallen away, and they returned to their folds.
36. And I saw in this vision until that sheep became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep, and put all the sheep in that house.
37. And I watched until this sheep — the one that had met that sheep which led them — fell asleep; and I watched until all the great sheep died and little ones rose up in their place, and they came to a pasture and drew near a stream of water.
38. Then that sheep, their leader which had become a man, left them and fell asleep, and all the sheep looked for it and wept over it with loud weeping.
39. And I watched until they stopped weeping for that sheep and crossed that stream of water, and two sheep rose up as leaders in place of those which had led them and fallen asleep (lit. "had fallen asleep and led them").
40. And I watched until the sheep came to a fine place, a pleasant and glorious land, and I watched until those sheep were content; and that house stood among them in the pleasant land.
41. And sometimes their eyes were opened, and sometimes blinded, until another sheep rose up and led them and brought them all back, and their eyes were opened.
42. And the dogs and the foxes and the wild boars began to devour those sheep, until the Lord of the sheep raised up [another sheep] a ram from among them, which led them.
43. And that ram began to butt those dogs, foxes, and wild boars on both sides until he had destroyed them †all†.
44. And that sheep whose eyes were opened watched that ram, which was among the sheep, until it †gave up its glory† and began to butt those sheep, and trampled on them, and acted shamefully.
45. And the Lord of the sheep sent the lamb to another lamb, and raised it to be a ram and leader of the sheep in place of that ram which had †given up its glory†.
46. And it went to it and spoke to it privately, and raised it to be a ram, and made it the prince and leader of the sheep; but all this while those dogs crushed the sheep.
47. And the first ram chased that second ram, and that second ram got up and ran from it; and I watched until those dogs pulled down the first ram.
48. And that second ram rose up and led the [little] sheep.
49. And those sheep grew and multiplied; but all the dogs and foxes and wild boars feared it and ran from it, and that ram butted and killed the wild beasts, and those wild beasts no longer had any power over the sheep, and robbed them of nothing any more.
48b. And that ram fathered many sheep and fell asleep; and a little sheep became ram in its place, and became prince and leader of those sheep.
50. And that house became great and wide, and it was built for those sheep; (and) a tall, great tower was built on the house for the Lord of the sheep — and that house was low, but the tower was high and lofty, and the Lord of the sheep stood on that tower, and they set a full table before Him.
51. And again I saw those sheep go astray again and wander many ways, and leave that house of theirs; and the Lord of the sheep called some from among the sheep and sent them to the sheep, but the sheep began to kill them.
52. And one of them escaped and was not killed; it hurried away and cried out loud over the sheep. They tried to kill it, but the Lord of the sheep saved it from the sheep, and brought it up to me, and made it live there.
53. And He sent many other sheep to those sheep to warn them and grieve over them.
54. And after that I saw that when they left the house of the Lord and His tower, they fell away completely, and their eyes were blinded; and I saw how the Lord of the sheep worked great slaughter among them in their herds, until those sheep invited that slaughter and gave away His place.
55. And He handed them over to the lions and tigers, and wolves and hyenas, and to the foxes, and to all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear those sheep to pieces.
56. And I saw that He left that house of theirs and their tower, and gave them all to the lions, to tear and devour them — to all the wild beasts.
57. And I began to cry out loud with all my strength, and to plead with the Lord of the sheep, and to lay before Him the case of the sheep — that they were being devoured by all the wild beasts.
58. But He stayed unmoved, though He saw it, and rejoiced that they were devoured and swallowed and robbed, and left them to be devoured by all the beasts.
59. And He called seventy shepherds, and threw those sheep to them to feed, and He said to the shepherds and their helpers: "Each one of you is to feed the sheep from now on, and everything I command you — do it.
60. And I will hand them over to you, counted out one by one, and tell you which of them are to be destroyed — and those, destroy." And He handed those sheep over to them.
61. And He called another and said to him: "Watch and note everything the shepherds do to those sheep, for they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them.
62. And record every excess, and the destruction worked through the shepherds — how many they destroy by my command, and how many by their own whim: record against each shepherd, one by one, all the destruction he brings about.
63. And read out before me, by number, how many they destroy and how many they hand over for destruction, so that I may have this as a witness against them, and know every deed of the shepherds — so that I may comprehend and see what they do, whether or not they keep the command I have given them.
64. But they are not to know it, and you are not to tell them or warn them — only record against each one all the destruction the shepherds bring about, each in his own time, and lay it all before me."
65. And I watched until those shepherds fed their flocks in their season, and they began to kill and destroy more than they had been told, and they handed those sheep over to the lions.
66. And the lions and tigers ate and devoured most of those sheep, and the wild boars ate along with them; and they burned that tower and tore down that house.
67. And I grew deeply sad over that tower, because that house of the sheep had been torn down, and afterwards I could not see whether those sheep entered that house.
68. And the shepherds and their helpers handed those sheep over to all the wild beasts to devour them, and each one of them received in his own time a set number; and the other wrote in a book how many each one of them destroyed.
69. And each one killed and destroyed many more than had been ordered; and I began to weep and grieve over those sheep.
70. And so in the vision I saw that writer — how he wrote down, day by day, every one destroyed by those shepherds, and carried the book up and laid it down and showed the whole book to the Lord of the sheep — everything they had done, and all that each one of them had done away with, and all that they had handed over for destruction.
71. And the book was read before the Lord of the sheep, and He took the book from his hand and read it and sealed it and laid it down.
72. And at once I saw how the shepherds fed their flocks for twelve hours — and look, three of those sheep turned back and came and went in and began to rebuild everything of that house that had fallen down; but the wild boars tried to stop them, and could not.
73. And they began to build again as before, and they raised up that tower, and it was called the high tower; and they began again to set a table before the tower, but all the bread on it was defiled and not pure.
74. And in all this the eyes of those sheep were blinded so that they could not see — and (the eyes of) their shepherds too; and they handed them over in large numbers to their shepherds for destruction, and they trampled the sheep underfoot and devoured them.
75. And the Lord of the sheep stayed unmoved until all the sheep were scattered over the field and mixed in with them (that is, the beasts), and they (that is, the shepherds) did not rescue them from the beasts.
76. And this writer carried the book up, and showed it and read it before the Lord of the sheep, and pleaded with Him for them, and begged Him for them, as he showed Him all the doings of the shepherds, and bore witness before Him against all the shepherds.
77. And he took the book itself and laid it down beside Him and left.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 89:** the long middle of the Animal Apocalypse — Israel's history from the Flood to Alexander in sheep/shepherd allegory. The allegory is rendered PLAINLY and LITERALLY throughout: sheep, rams, shepherds, wild beasts stand exactly as Charles prints them. No decoding is imported into the reading text. Charles's identifications (his footnotes, sighted on the scans — Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Joshua, the Judges, David, Solomon, Elijah, the seventy shepherds, Zerubbabel, Ezra, etc.) are recorded as apparatus below, never in the text. The question of a reader-facing note pointing to the identifications was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **Charles's seven subsection heads:** carried in the base as printed (their exact typography — centered small caps per the ch. 83 print — to be settled on the scans). They are Charles's editorial divisions, not verse text. The question whether the reading text keeps them was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **Thou/Thy → You/Your (vv. 64 only):** the chapter's one direct address ("thou shalt not declare it to them") → "you are not to tell them". Per the ch. 9 decision; disclosed.
- **"instructed him in a secret" → "taught him a secret" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed. "without his being terrified" → "without frightening him" — plain; disclosed. "dwelt thereon" → "lived in it"; "covered in" → "shut inside" — plain; disclosed.
- **"a lofty roof" → "a high roof" (v. 2):** "lofty" → "high" (plain); disclosed. "mine eyes" → "my eyes" — modernized; disclosed. "flowed with much water" → "poured much water" — plain; disclosed.
- **"behold" → "look" (vv. 3, 72):** plain register, matching ch. 1's "Look!"; disclosed.
- **"fountains" → "springs" (v. 3):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"perished" → "died" (vv. 5, 6, 27, 37):** plain register; disclosed. "gathered together" → "herded together" (v. 5) — plain; disclosed.
- **"(but)" (v. 6):** Charles's round-bracket supply, absorbed per the ch. 1 standing rule ("they could not escape — they died"); disclosed.
- **"the chasms of the earth were levelled up" → "the cracks in the earth were filled in" (v. 7):** "chasm" → "crack", "levelled up" → "filled in" — plain; disclosed. "abysses" → "depths" — plain; disclosed.
- **"the darkness retired" → "the darkness drew back" (v. 8):** "retired" → "drew back" (plain); disclosed. "that vessel settled" → "that vessel came to rest" — plain; disclosed.
- **"departed from them" → "left them" (v. 9):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"beasts of the field" → "wild animals" (vv. 10, 19, 33):** plain register; disclosed — G3 item (kept consistent within this chapter; not harmonized across chapters now).
- **"genera" → "kinds" (v. 10):** "genera" is technical Latin; disclosed. "swine" → "pigs" — plain; disclosed.
- **"begat" → "fathered" (vv. 11, 12, 48b):** plain register; disclosed. "the former" → "the boar" (v. 12) — plain; disclosed.
- **"gave up ... to" → "handed over to" (v. 13):** plain register; disclosed. "asses" → "donkeys" (vv. 6, 11, 13, 16) — plain; disclosed (asses/donkeys is a G3 item for the slice).
- **"to pasture with it" → "to graze with it" (v. 14):** plain register; disclosed. "pasturing them" → "feeding them" (vv. 16, 28) — plain; disclosed.
- **"oppressed" → "crushed" (vv. 15, 19, 46):** plain register; disclosed — G3 item. "cast their young" → "threw their young" — plain; disclosed. "complain unto their Lord" → "plead with their Lord" — plain; disclosed.
- **"lamented" → "grieved" (vv. 16, 69):** plain register; disclosed. "besought" → "begged" (vv. 16, 76) — plain; disclosed. "a lofty abode" → "His high dwelling" — plain; disclosed.
- **"spake" → "spoke" (vv. 17, 18, 46, 59, 61):** modernized; disclosed. "admonish" → "warn" (vv. 17, 18, 64) — plain; disclosed.
- **"according to the word of the Lord" → "as the Lord had said" (v. 18):** plain register; disclosed. "the assembly of those wolves" → "the gathering of those wolves" — plain; disclosed. "henceforth" → "from then on" — plain; disclosed.
- **"thereupon" → "then" (v. 19):** plain register; disclosed. "exceedingly" → "fiercely" — plain; disclosed.
- **"smite" → "strike" (v. 20):** plain register; disclosed. "make lamentation" → "wail" — plain; disclosed. "forthwith" → "at once" — plain; disclosed.
- **"departed from amongst" → "got away from among" (v. 21):** plain register; disclosed. "departed in pursuit of" → "set out after" — plain; disclosed.
- **"terrible to behold" → "fearsome to look at" (vv. 22, 30):** "terrible" → "fearsome", "behold" → "look at" — plain; disclosed. (terrible/fearsome is a G3 item).
- **"pursue" → "chase" (vv. 23, 27, 47):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"that sea was divided" → "that sea was split" (v. 24):** plain register; disclosed. "before their face" → "before them" — plain; disclosed. "placed Himself" → "put Himself" — plain; disclosed.
- **"[those wolves]" (v. 25):** Charles's square brackets = editorial — kept visible; disclosed. Whether reader-facing brackets (or a note) are wanted stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"to flee before His face" → "to run from before His face" (v. 26):** plain register; disclosed. "gathered itself together" → "closed back together" — plain; disclosed. "as it had been created" → "as it had been made" — plain; disclosed.
- **"went forth" → "went out" (v. 28):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"ascended to the summit of that lofty rock" → "climbed to the top of that high rock" (vv. 29, 32, 33):** plain register; disclosed.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 90

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 90" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_90), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Scan verification of the base against both IA 1912 copies at G1 — see "Print-level findings" below. Charles's five subsection heads are carried in the base as printed (see print findings for their exact form).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts: pp. 204–224 in both scans; inline bold 'XC. 1.'; Charles's five subsection heads (the fifth prints as 'XC. 28–38.'); the vv. 13–18 doublet printed as parallel columns in the order 13|16, then v. 19, then 14|17, 15|18. Full details in the G1 Audit Record below.

*XC. 1-5. Third Period—from Alexander the Great to the Graeco-Syrian Domination.*

1. And I saw till that in this manner **thirty-five** shepherds undertook the pasturing (of the sheep), and they severally completed their periods as did the first; and others received them into their hands, to pasture them for their period, each shepherd in his own period.
2. And after that I saw in my vision all the birds of heaven coming, the eagles, the vultures, the kites, the ravens; but the eagles led all the birds; and they began to devour those sheep, and to pick out their eyes and to devour their flesh.
3. And the sheep cried out because their flesh was being devoured by the birds, and as for me I looked and lamented in my sleep over that shepherd who pastured the sheep.
4. And I saw until those sheep were devoured by the dogs and eagles and kites, and they left neither flesh nor skin nor sinew remaining on them till only their bones stood there: and their bones too fell to the earth and the sheep became few.
5. And I saw until that twenty-three had undertaken the pasturing and completed in their several periods fifty-eight times.

*XC. 6-12. Fourth Period—from the Graeco-Syrian Domination to the Maccabean Revolt.*

6. But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.
7. Yea, they cried to them, but they did not hearken to what they said to them, but were exceedingly deaf, and their eyes were very exceedingly blinded.
8. And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, and dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.
9. And I saw till horns grew upon those lambs, and the ravens cast down their horns; and I saw till there sprouted a great horn of one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened.
10. And it †looked at† them [and their eyes opened], and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.
11. And notwithstanding all this those eagles and vultures and ravens and kites still kept tearing the sheep and swooping down upon them and devouring them: still the sheep remained silent, but the rams lamented and cried out.
12. And those ravens fought and battled with it and sought to lay low its horn, but they had no power over it.

*XC. 13-19. The last Assault of the Gentiles on the Jews (where vv. 13-15 and 16-18 are doublets).*

[The print sets vv. 13–18 as parallel columns — Column A (vv. 13–15) | Column B (vv. 16–18) — with v. 19 placed between the 13|16 pair and the 14|17 pair, in Charles's reconstructed order. Both columns are kept here, unmerged, in the print's order. Column layout settled on the scans.]

Column A | Column B:

13. And I saw till the †shepherds and† eagles and those vultures and kites came, and †they cried to the ravens† that they should break the horn of that ram, and they battled and fought with it, and it battled with them and cried that its help might come. | 16. All the eagles and vultures and ravens and kites were gathered together, and there came with them all the sheep of the field, yea, they all came together, and helped each other to break that horn of the ram.

19. And I saw till a great sword was given to the sheep, and the sheep proceeded against all the beasts of the field to slay them, and all the beasts and the birds of the heaven fled before their face.

14. And I saw till that man, who wrote down the names of the shepherds [and] carried up into the presence of the Lord of the sheep [came and helped it and showed it everything: he had come down for the help of that ram]. | 17. And I saw that man, who wrote the book according to the command of the Lord, till he opened that book concerning the destruction which those twelve last shepherds had wrought, and showed that they had destroyed much more than their predecessors, before the Lord of the sheep.

15. And I saw till the Lord of the sheep came unto them in wrath, and all who saw Him fled, and they all fell †into His shadow† from before His face. | 18. And I saw till the Lord of the sheep came unto them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath, and smote the earth, and the earth clave asunder, and all the beasts and all the birds of the heaven fell from among those sheep, and were swallowed up in the earth and it covered them.

*XC. 20-27. Judgement of the Fallen Angels, the Shepherds, and the Apostates.*

20. And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and the Lord of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before the Lord of the sheep.
21. And the Lord called those men the seven first white ones, and commanded that they should bring before Him, beginning with the first star which led the way, all the stars whose privy members were like those of horses, and they brought them all before Him.
22. And He said to that man who wrote before Him, being one of those seven white ones, and said unto him: "Take those seventy shepherds to whom I delivered the sheep, and who taking them on their own authority slew more than I commanded them."
23. And behold they were all bound, I saw, and they all stood before Him.
24. And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire.
25. And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.
26. And I saw at that time how a like abyss was opened in the midst of the earth, full of fire, and they brought those blinded sheep, and they were all judged and found guilty and cast into this fiery abyss, and they burned; now this abyss was to the right of that house.
27. And I saw those sheep burning †and their bones burning†.

*XC. 28–38. The New Jerusalem, the Conversion of the surviving Gentiles, the Resurrection of the Righteous, the Messiah.*

28. And I stood up to see till they folded up that old house; and carried off all the pillars, and all the beams and ornaments of the house were at the same time folded up with it, and they carried it off and laid it in a place in the south of the land.
29. And I saw till the Lord of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.
30. And I saw all the sheep which had been left, and all the beasts on the earth, and all the birds of the heaven, falling down and doing homage to those sheep and making petition to and obeying them in every thing.
31. And thereafter those three who were clothed in white and had seized me by my hand [who had taken me up before], and the hand of that ram also seizing hold of me, they took me up and set me down in the midst of those sheep †before the judgement took place†.
32. And those sheep were all white, and their wool was abundant and clean.
33. And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.
34. And I saw till they laid down that sword, which had been given to the sheep, and they brought it back into the house, and it was sealed before the presence of the Lord, and all the sheep were invited into that house, but it held them not.
35. And the eyes of them all were opened, and they saw the good, and there was not one among them that did not see.
36. And I saw that that house was large and broad and very full.
37. And I saw that a white bull was born, with large horns, and all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the air feared him and made petition to him all the time.
38. And I saw till all their generations were transformed, and they all became white bulls; and the first among them became a lamb, and that lamb became a great animal and had great black horns on its head; and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over it and over all the oxen.
39. And I slept in their midst: and I awoke and saw everything.
40. This is the vision which I saw while I slept, and I awoke and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave Him glory.
41. Then I wept with a great weeping and my tears stayed not till I could no longer endure it: when I saw, they flowed on account of what I had seen; for everything shall come and be fulfilled, and all the deeds of men in their order were shown to me.
42. On that night I remembered the first dream, and because of it I wept and was troubled—because I had seen that vision.

**Print-level findings (both scans):** THREE material transcription-vs-print corrections, all confirmed on both scans: (a) the doublet's print order is 13|16, 19, 14|17, 15|18; (b) the fifth subsection head prints 'XC. 28–38.' (not '28-42', no 'Enoch awakes and weeps'); (c) v. 22's speech uses double quotes in print. '**thirty-five**' (v. 1) confirmed as Charles's thick-type emendation on both scans at high resolution. All dagger and bracket markings confirmed; 'other' (v. 20), v. 21's clause, and 'it' (v. 38) are regular weight despite footnote discussion (see G1 items 3–4).

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And I watched as, in this way, thirty-five shepherds took up the feeding of the sheep, and each completed his own term as the first ones had; and others took them in hand, to feed them for their term, each shepherd in his own term.
2. And after that I saw in my vision all the birds of the sky coming — the eagles, the vultures, the kites, the ravens; but the eagles led all the birds — and they began to devour those sheep, and to peck out their eyes and devour their flesh.
3. And the sheep cried out because their flesh was being devoured by the birds; and as for me, I watched and grieved in my sleep over that shepherd who fed the sheep.
4. And I watched until those sheep were devoured by the dogs and eagles and kites, and they left neither flesh nor skin nor sinew on them, until only their bones stood there; and their bones too fell to the earth, and the sheep grew few.
5. And I watched until twenty-three had taken up the feeding, and in their several terms completed fifty-eight times.
6. But look — lambs were born to those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and see, and to cry out to the sheep.
7. Yes, they cried to them, but they did not listen to what they said — they were stone-deaf, and their eyes were utterly blinded.
8. And I saw in the vision how the ravens swooped on those lambs and seized one of those lambs, and dashed the sheep to pieces and devoured them.
9. And I watched until horns grew on those lambs, and the ravens broke off their horns; and I watched until a great horn sprouted on one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened.
10. And it †looked at† them [and their eyes opened], and it cried out to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.
11. And for all this, those eagles and vultures and ravens and kites kept on tearing the sheep and swooping down on them and devouring them; still the sheep stayed silent, but the rams grieved and cried out.
12. And those ravens fought and battled with it and tried to bring down its horn, but they had no power over it.

[The vv. 13–18 doublet is rendered pair by pair, unmerged, in the print's order — 13|16, then 19, then 14|17, 15|18:]

13 | 16:
13. And I watched until the †shepherds and† eagles and those vultures and kites came, and †they called to the ravens† to break the horn of that ram; and they battled and fought with it, and it fought back and cried out for help to come. | 16. All the eagles and vultures and ravens and kites were gathered together, and with them came all the sheep of the field — yes, they all came together, and helped one another break that horn of the ram.

19. And I watched until a great sword was given to the sheep, and the sheep went out against all the beasts of the field to kill them, and all the beasts and the birds of the sky ran from before them.

14 | 17:
14. And I watched until that man — the one who wrote down the names of the shepherds [and] carried them up into the presence of the Lord of the sheep — [came and helped it and showed it everything: he had come down to help that ram]. | 17. And I saw that man — the one who wrote the book at the Lord's command — until he opened that book about the destruction those twelve last shepherds had worked, and showed that they had destroyed much more than those before them, before the Lord of the sheep.

15 | 18:
15. And I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them in anger, and all who saw Him ran, and they all fell †into His shadow† before His face. | 18. And I watched until the Lord of the sheep came to them and took the staff of His anger in His hand, and struck the earth, and the earth split apart, and all the beasts and all the birds of the sky fell away from those sheep and were swallowed up in the earth, and it covered them.
20. And I watched until a throne was set up in the pleasant land, and the Lord of the sheep seated Himself on it, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before the Lord of the sheep.
21. And the Lord called those men, the seven first white ones, and commanded them to bring before Him — beginning with the first star which led the way — all the stars whose private parts were like those of horses; and they brought them all before Him.
22. And He said to that man who wrote in His presence — one of those seven white ones — He said to him: "Take those seventy shepherds to whom I handed over the sheep, who on their own authority killed more than I commanded them."
23. And look — they were all bound, I saw, and they all stood before Him.
24. And judgement was held first over the stars: they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and were thrown into an abyss full of fire and flames, and full of pillars of fire.
25. And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and were thrown into that fiery abyss.
26. And I saw at that time how a like abyss was opened in the middle of the earth, full of fire; and they brought those blinded sheep, and they were all judged and found guilty and thrown into this fiery abyss, and they burned — and this abyss was to the right of that house.
27. And I saw those sheep burning †and their bones burning†.
28. And I stood up to watch as they folded up that old house; and they carried off all the pillars, and all the beams and ornaments of the house were folded up with it at the same time, and they carried it off and laid it in a place in the south of the land.
29. And I watched until the Lord of the sheep brought a new house, greater and higher than the first, and set it up where the first had been folded up; all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first — the old one He had taken away — and all the sheep were inside it.
30. And I saw all the sheep that were left, and all the beasts on the earth, and all the birds of the sky, bowing down and doing honour to those sheep, and making their plea to them and obeying them in everything.
31. And after that, those three who were dressed in white and had taken me by the hand [who had taken me up before] — and the hand of that ram also holding me — took me up and set me down in the middle of those sheep †before the judgement took place†.
32. And those sheep were all white, and their wool was thick and clean.
33. And all that had been destroyed and scattered, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the sky, gathered in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had come back to His house.
34. And I watched until they laid down that sword which had been given to the sheep, and they brought it back into the house, and it was sealed up before the Lord, and all the sheep were invited into that house — but it could not hold them.
35. And the eyes of them all were opened, and they saw the good, and there was not one among them who could not see.
36. And I saw that that house was large and wide and very full.
37. And I saw that a white bull was born, with great horns, and all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the air feared him and kept making their plea to him.
38. And I watched until all their generations were changed, and they all became white bulls; and the first among them became a lamb, and that lamb became a great animal with great black horns on its head; and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over it and over all the oxen.
39. And I slept among them; and I woke up and saw everything.
40. This is the vision I saw while I slept; and I woke up and blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave Him glory.
41. Then I wept with loud weeping, and my tears did not stop until I could bear it no longer; as I looked, they flowed because of what I had seen — for everything shall come and be fulfilled, and all the deeds of men were shown to me in their order.
42. That night I remembered the first dream, and because of it I wept and was troubled — because I had seen that vision.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Role of ch. 90:** the close of the Animal Apocalypse — the last shepherds, the Maccabean horn, the final assault, the threefold judgement (stars, shepherds, blinded sheep), the new house, the white bull. The allegory is rendered PLAINLY and LITERALLY throughout; no decoding imported. Charles's identifications (his footnotes, to be sighted on the scans) are apparatus only. The question of a reader-facing note was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **Charles's five subsection heads:** carried in the base as printed (centered small caps). **Material transcription-vs-print correction:** the fifth head prints as "XC. 28–38." — NOT "XC. 28-42." and WITHOUT the transcription's added "Enoch awakes and weeps" (the print's head ends at "the Messiah."). Vv. 39–42 carry no separate head in print; they fall under the 28–38 head. They are Charles's editorial divisions, not verse text. The question whether the reading text keeps them was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **The vv. 13–18 doublet:** the print sets these as PARALLEL COLUMNS — two forms of the same episode side by side — in Charles's reconstructed order: the 13|16 pair, then v. 19, then the 14|17 pair, then the 15|18 pair (his footnote: "ver. 19 should be read immediately after ver. 13 (= ver. 16)"). This worksheet keeps both columns whole, in the print's order, with v. 19 where the print puts it — NOT merged, NOT smoothed, NOT harmonized into one narrative, NOT reordered to 13–15/16–18 + 19 (per the task's standing rule). The draft renders each pair separately in the same order. **The base was corrected from the transcription's apparent 13–15/16–18 + 19 grouping to the print's 13|16, 19, 14|17, 15|18 — recorded as a material transcription-vs-print correction** (the transcription's table had v. 19 misplaced mid-table; the print is unambiguous). Charles's footnote on the doublet (text-critical reconstruction; the doublet existed already in Greek and Hebrew) is recorded as apparatus. Whether a reader-facing note flags the doublet stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"**thirty-five**" in thick type (v. 1):** Charles's own emendation — marked in the base per the ch. 2 standing rule (settled on both scans at high resolution: the word stands in clearly heavier type than the surrounding text). His note: "Thirty-five. All the MSS. are corrupt here. gt, β–kq read 'thirty-seven'..." — the figure is his reckoning (12 + 23). Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"undertook the pasturing (of the sheep)" → "took up the feeding of the sheep" (vv. 1, 5):** "(of the sheep)" is Charles's round-bracket supply — absorbed per the ch. 1 standing rule; "undertook the pasturing" → "took up the feeding" (plain); disclosed.
- **"severally" → "each" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed. "periods" → "terms" — plain; disclosed (periods/terms is a G3 item). "received them into their hands" → "took them in hand" — plain; disclosed.
- **"birds of heaven" → "birds of the sky" (vv. 2, 18, 19, 30, 33):** the visible sky (cf. 83:3 note); disclosed. (heaven/sky is a G3 item).
- **"pick out their eyes" → "peck out their eyes" (v. 2):** "pick out" → "peck out" is the plain bird-verb; disclosed.

- **"neither flesh nor skin nor sinew remaining on them" → "neither flesh nor skin nor sinew on them" (v. 4):** plain syntax; disclosed. "the sheep became few" → "the sheep grew few" — plain; disclosed.
- **"completed in their several periods fifty-eight times" (v. 5):** kept close to the base — "had taken up the feeding, and in their several terms completed fifty-eight times"; the arithmetic (35 + 23 = 58) is not spelled out in the text. Disclosed.

The allegory is rendered literally throughout — no identification imported into the text. Plain-register moves, all recorded in the Notes (see the verse-by-verse list above — 90+ disclosed moves, including "(of the sheep)" absorbed per the ch. 1 rule, "[and their eyes opened]"/"[and]"/"[came and helped it ...]"/"[who had taken me up before]" kept visible, "†looked at†"/"†shepherds and†"/"†they cried to the ravens†"/"†into His shadow†"/"†and their bones burning†"/"†before the judgement took place†" kept daggered, the v. 22 double "said" kept). **Material transcription-vs-print correction in the base:** the doublet's order (13|16, 19, 14|17, 15|18 per print). No sense added beyond the disclosed moves.
2. **Chapter span, heading — settled on both scans:** pp. 204–224 in both scans (scan 1: files _0320–_0340; scan 2: files _0319–_0339). Inline bold "XC. 1." as transcribed; Charles's five subsection heads carried in the base as printed — with the correction that the fifth head prints as **"XC. 28–38."** (NOT "XC. 28-42."; the transcription also adds "Enoch awakes and weeps," which the print does not have; vv. 39–42 carry no separate head). 42 of 42 verses; nothing omitted, added, or reordered. ## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 91

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 91" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_91), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 225–228 and 232–234 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below. **The print is the authority on verse order and verse numbering:** Charles's 1912 print does NOT present XCI as vv. 1–19 in sequence. It prints XCI.1–10, [11], 18–19 on pp. 225–228 (between XCII and XCIII), and restores XCI.12–17 after XCIII.1–10 on pp. 232–234 under the head "XCI. 12–17. The Last Three Weeks." The transcription reassembles the verses as 1–19 — a normalization, recorded as a discrepancy. The base below follows the print's order and the print's verse numbering.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCI = vv. 1–10, [11], 18–19 (printed pp. 225–228) + vv. 12–17 (printed pp. 232–234). Display heads: p. 224 "XCII. XCI. 1–10, 18–19. *Enoch's Book of Admonition for his Children.*"; p. 225 inline "XCI. 1–11, 18–19. *Enoch's Admonition to his Children.*"; p. 228 display "XCIII, XCI. 12–17. *The Apocalypse of Weeks.*"; p. 232 display "XCI. 12–17. *The Last Three Weeks.*". Inline verse heads: "XCI. 1." (p. 225), "12.", "13.", "14d.", "14a.", "b.", "c.", "15.", "16.", "17." (pp. 232–233). The transcription's display lines ("XCII. 1-10, 18-19. Enoch's Admonition to his Children." / "CHAPTER XCI.") are normalizations — and the first is misnumbered (see Material corrections). Running heads: p. 225 "Chapters XCII. 1—XCI. 4"; p. 226 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V"; p. 227 "Chapter XCI. 5–11"; p. 232 (display page); p. 233 "Chapters XCIII. 13—XCI. 17". **Thick type (Charles's emendation, invisible in the transcription):** "**must**" (v. 5) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Square brackets [ ] (interpolation):** "[11. ...]" (p. 227). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(i.e. the heathen)" (v. 9). No daggers, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in the main text of XCI. The quoted speech of vv. 1–3, 18–19 is set with single quotation marks in print (flattened to double quotes in the draft — disclosed).

—— Printed pp. 225–228, under "XCI. 1–11, 18–19. Enoch's Admonition to his Children." ——

1. 'And now, my son Methuselah, call to me all thy brothers
And gather together to me all the sons of thy mother,
For the word calls me,
And the spirit is poured out upon me,
That I may show you everything
That shall befall you for ever.'
2. And thereupon Methuselah went and summoned to him all his brothers and assembled his relatives. 3. And he spake unto all the children of righteousness and said:
'Hear, ye sons of Enoch, all the words of your father,
And hearken aright to the voice of my mouth;
For I exhort you and say unto you, beloved:
Love uprightness and walk therein.
4. And draw not nigh to uprightness with a double heart,
And associate not with those of a double heart,
But walk in righteousness, my sons.
And it shall guide you on good paths,
And righteousness shall be your companion.
5. For I know that violence **must** increase on the earth,
And a great chastisement be executed on the earth,
And all unrighteousness come to an end:
Yea, it shall be cut off from its roots,
And its whole structure be destroyed.
6. And unrighteousness shall again be consummated on the earth,
And all the deeds of unrighteousness and of violence
And transgression shall prevail in a twofold degree.
7. And when sin and unrighteousness and blasphemy
And violence in all kinds of deeds increase,
And apostasy and transgression and uncleanness increase,
A great chastisement shall come from heaven upon all these,
And the holy Lord will come forth with wrath and chastisement
To execute judgement on earth.
8. In those days violence shall be cut off from its roots,
And the roots of unrighteousness together with deceit,
And they shall be destroyed from under heaven.
9. And all the idols of the heathen shall be abandoned,
And the temples burned with fire,
And they shall remove them from the whole earth,
And they (i.e. the heathen) shall be cast into the judgement of fire,
And shall perish in wrath and in grievous judgement for ever.
10. And the righteous shall arise from their sleep,
And wisdom shall arise and be given unto them.
[11. And after that the roots of unrighteousness shall be cut off, and the sinners shall be destroyed by the sword ... shall be cut off from the blasphemers in every place, and those who plan violence and those who commit blasphemy shall perish by the sword.]
18. And now I tell you, my sons, and show you
The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence.
Yea, I will show them to you again
That ye may know what will come to pass.
19. And now, hearken unto me, my sons,
And walk in the paths of righteousness,
And walk not in the paths of violence;
For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'

—— Printed pp. 232–234, after XCIII.1–10, under "XCI. 12–17. The Last Three Weeks." ——

12. And after that there shall be another, the eighth week, that of righteousness,
And a sword shall be given to it that a righteous judgement may be executed on the oppressors,
And sinners shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous.
13. And at its close they shall acquire houses through their righteousness,
And a house shall be built for the Great King in glory for evermore,
14d. And all mankind shall look to the path of uprightness.
14a. And after that, in the ninth week, the righteous judgement shall be revealed to the whole world,
b. And all the works of the godless shall vanish from all the earth,
c. And the world shall be written down for destruction.
15. And after this, in the tenth week in the seventh part,
There shall be the great eternal judgement,
In which He will execute vengeance amongst the angels.
16. And the first heaven shall depart and pass away,
And a new heaven shall appear,
And all the powers of the heavens shall give sevenfold light.
17. And after that there will be many weeks without number for ever,
And all shall be in goodness and righteousness,
And sin shall no more be mentioned for ever.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 3's quoted speech ends with "Love uprightness and walk therein." — the print numbers that line as the close of v. 3, and v. 4 opens with "And draw not nigh to uprightness with a double heart," (see Material corrections). v. 5 "**must**" is in unmistakable thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "Violence must increase. The text reads 'the state (or 'essence') of violence shall increase'. But this is wholly unlikely. I have therefore emended hĕlâwê (='state') into halawô, i.e. the substantive verb with suffix. When we combine halawô with jĕṣan'ĕ the two = 'must increase'." v. 9 "(i.e. the heathen)" is Charles's round-bracket gloss. v. [11] is in square brackets on p. 227 (running head "Chapter XCI. 5–11"); Charles's note (sighted) calls it "an interpolation added by the final editor in order to introduce vv. 12–17 which he had torn from their original context." 14d is printed before 14a — Charles's note (sighted): "I have transposed 14d to the close of the preceding stanza." The v. 14c note (sighted) cites the Greek: "The world shall be written down for destruction (m, β). g 'He shall write down (i.e. decree) the destruction of the world'." No thick type elsewhere in XCI; no daggers; no corner or angle brackets.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):**
1. **Verse order:** the transcription reassembles XCI as vv. 1–19 in sequence; the print splits the chapter — vv. 1–10, [11], 18–19 on pp. 225–228 and vv. 12–17 on pp. 232–234 (after XCIII.1–10). The base above follows the print.
2. **Verse 3/4 boundary:** the transcription numbers "Love uprightness and walk therein." as v. 4's first line; the print numbers it as the last line of v. 3's quoted speech, with v. 4 opening "And draw not nigh to uprightness with a double heart,". The base above follows the print.
3. **Display head misnumbered in the transcription:** the transcription's head reads "XCII. 1-10, 18-19. Enoch's Admonition to his Children."; the print (p. 225) reads "XCI. 1–11, 18–19. Enoch's Admonition to his Children." — wrong chapter numeral and wrong verse span in the transcription.
4. **Thick type invisible in the transcription:** "must" (v. 5) is Charles's emendation (hĕlâwê → halawô), marked in the base above.

1. "And now, my son Methuselah, call all your brothers to me, and gather to me all the sons of your mother. For the word calls me, and the spirit is poured out on me, so that I may show you everything that will happen to you forever."

And he spoke to all the children of righteousness and said: "Hear, you sons of Enoch, all the words of your father, and listen well to the voice of my mouth. For I urge you and say to you, my loved ones: Love what is right and walk in it.
4. Do not come near to what is right with a double heart, and do not keep company with those of a double heart. Walk in righteousness, my sons, and it will guide you on good paths, and righteousness will be your companion.
5. For I know that violence **must** grow on the earth, and a great punishment will be carried out on the earth, and all unrighteousness will come to an end. Yes, it will be cut off from its roots, and its whole building will be destroyed.
6. And unrighteousness will again be completed on the earth, and all the deeds of unrighteousness and violence and wrongdoing will grow twice as strong.
7. And when sin and unrighteousness and blasphemy and violence in every kind of deed grow, and falling away and wrongdoing and uncleanness grow, a great punishment will come from heaven on all these, and the holy Lord will come out with anger and punishment to carry out judgment on earth.
8. In those days violence will be cut off from its roots, and the roots of unrighteousness together with deceit, and they will be destroyed from under heaven.
9. And all the idols of the nations will be left behind, and the temples burned with fire, and they will remove them from the whole earth, and they (that is, the nations) will be thrown into the judgment of fire, and will die in anger and in heavy judgment forever.
10. And the righteous will rise from their sleep, and wisdom will rise and be given to them.
[11. And after that the roots of unrighteousness will be cut off, and the sinners will be destroyed by the sword ... will be cut off from the blasphemers in every place, and those who plan violence and those who commit blasphemy will die by the sword.]
18. And now I tell you, my sons, and show you the paths of righteousness and the paths of violence. Yes, I will show them to you again so that you may know what will come to pass.
19. And now, listen to me, my sons, and walk in the paths of righteousness, and do not walk in the paths of violence; for all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness will die forever."

14d. and all mankind will look to the path of what is right.
14a. And after that, in the ninth week, the righteous judgment will be shown to the whole world, b. and all the works of the godless will disappear from the whole earth, c. and the world will be written down for destruction.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **The split chapter:** Charles's print presents XCI in two places — vv. 1–10, [11], 18–19 as "Enoch's Admonition to his Children" (pp. 225–228) and vv. 12–17 as "The Last Three Weeks" closing the Apocalypse of Weeks (pp. 232–234). His Sect. V introduction (p. 218, sighted) explains the arrangement: the section "begins with 92 — 'Written by Enoch the scribe,' &c."; "On 92 follows 91^1–10, 18–19"; "Then comes the Apocalypse of Weeks, 93^1–10 91^12–17"; the interpolations are "91:11, 93:11–14, 94:7d, 96:2"; and "91^12–17 should undoubtedly be read directly after 93." The draft keeps the print's order and marks the two print locations; it does not reassemble the chapter into 1–19. Whether a reader-facing note explains the split stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your (vv. 1, 18–19):** plain register per the ch. 9 standing rule; disclosed. The question whether "You" stands was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"must" in thick type (v. 5):** Charles's own emendation (hĕlâwê → halawô) — marked in base and draft per the ch. 2 standing rule. Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **[11] kept in square brackets:** Charles's interpolation bracket; the draft keeps it visible and does not smooth it away. The question of bracket visibility for readers was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"(i.e. the heathen)" → "(that is, the nations)" (v. 9):** Charles's round-bracket gloss kept visible; "heathen" → "nations" is plain register, disclosed.
- **14d printed before 14a:** Charles's transposition ("I have transposed 14d to the close of the preceding stanza" — sighted); the draft keeps the print's order. Disclosed.
- **"be consummated" → "be completed" (v. 6):** plain register; disclosed.
