## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 92

Drafting copy: the 1912 print itself — the Wikisource transcription page for Chapter 92 returned HTTP 403 ("do not repeat this request") for this worker, so the base was transcribed directly from the print scans (the print is the authority in any case). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 224–225 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections apply (no transcription was usable).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCII = vv. 1–5 exactly, spanning printed pp. 224–225; "XCI. 1." begins on p. 225 immediately after v. 5. Display head (p. 224): "XCII. XCI. 1–10, 18–19. *Enoch's Book of Admonition for his Children.*" Inline head: bold "XCII. 1." run into the text (any display "CHAPTER XCII." would be a normalization). Running heads: p. 224 "The Book of Enoch" center, "[Sect. V" top right (even-page pattern); p. 225 "Chapters XCII. 1—XCI. 4". **No thick type** in XCII (no Charles emendation in this chapter). **Square brackets [ ] (interpolation):** "[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth]" (v. 1); "[Shall arise]" (v. 3). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(which is)" (v. 1); "(endowed)" (v. 4). No daggers, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in XCII.

XCII. 1. The book written by Enoch—[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth] for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace.
2. Let not your spirit be troubled on account of the times;
For the Holy and Great One has appointed days for all things.
3. And the righteous one shall arise from sleep,
[Shall arise] and walk in the paths of righteousness,
And all his path and conversation shall be in eternal goodness and grace.
4. He will be gracious to the righteous and give him eternal uprightness,
And He will give him power so that he shall be (endowed) with goodness and righteousness,
And he shall walk in eternal light.
5. And sin shall perish in darkness for ever,
And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore.

**Print-level findings (both scans):** v. 1's bracketed clause is Charles's interpolation bracketing — his footnote (sighted): "[Enoch indeed ... all the earth]. I have, with some hesitation, bracketed these words as an interpolation. Enoch does not attempt a complete doctrine of wisdom, and seeing that it was for the chosen race only it could hardly be said to be 'praised of all men'." The same note gives the Ge'ez fork: "The book ... indeed wrote (g). Other MSS. 'written by Enoch the scribe'." and "This complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised (α–t reading zakuĕllô). t 'of the complete doctrine', &c., β–y 'this complete doctrine of wisdom is praised'. A judge, &c. Wisdom is represented as the πάρεδρος or assessor of God in 84^3 (note)." — Greek πάρεδρος cited. v. 2's note (sighted): "The times are evil; but these too are the ordination of God. The Holy and Great One (gq, cl1a). ml, β–cl1a 'the Holy Great One'; see 1^3 (note)." v. 3's note (sighted): "The righteous one. Used collectively as in 91^10. Instead of 'and the righteous ... from sleep, shall arise' g reads 'and wisdom shall arise'. Paths (mqt), β 'path'." v. 4's note (sighted): "The righteous (tu, β). gq 'righteousness'. Power. Uprightness and power will no longer be dissevered. He shall (mt, β). gqu 'they shall'. In eternal light; see 38^4 (note)." v. 5's note (sighted): "Cf. 10^16, 20." The chapter note (sighted): "XCII. This chapter obviously forms the beginning of a new book just as 1^1 formed originally the beginning of the section 12–16; see p. 27." The rearrangement note (sighted): "In this edition I have rearranged these chapters in what I suggested was their original order in my first edition, i.e. 92 91^1–10, 18–19 93^1–10 91^12–17 94."

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. The book written by Enoch — [Enoch indeed wrote this complete teaching of wisdom, (which is) praised by all men, and a judge of all the earth] — for all my children who will live on the earth, and for the generations to come who will keep what is right and peace.
2. Do not let your spirit be troubled because of the times; for the Holy and Great One has set days for all things.
3. And the righteous one will rise from sleep, [will rise] and walk in the paths of righteousness, and all his path and his way of life will be in everlasting goodness and grace.
4. He will be kind to the righteous and give him everlasting uprightness, and He will give him power so that he will be (given) goodness and righteousness, and he will walk in everlasting light.
5. And sin will die in darkness forever, and will never be seen again from that day on.

Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 228–232 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse, sign, and bracket faithfully), but the thick-type emendation invisible in the transcription was settled on the scans and is marked in the base below.

XCIII. 1. And after that Enoch both †gave† and began to recount from the books. 2. And Enoch said:
'Concerning the children of righteousness and concerning the elect of the world,
And concerning the plant of uprightness, I will speak these things,
Yea, I Enoch will declare (them) unto you, my sons:
According to that which appeared to me in the heavenly vision,
And which I have known through the word of the holy angels,
And have learnt from the heavenly tablets.'
3. And Enoch began to recount from the books and said:
'I was born the seventh in the first week,
While judgement and righteousness still endured.
4. And after me there shall arise in the second week great wickedness,
And deceit shall have sprung up;
And in it there shall be the first end.
And in it a man shall be saved;
And after it is ended unrighteousness shall grow up,
And a law shall be made for the sinners.
5. And after that in the third week at its close
A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement,
And **his posterity** shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.
6. And after that in the fourth week, at its close,
Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen,
And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.
7. And after that in the fifth week, at its close,
The house of glory and dominion shall be built for ever.
8. And after that in the sixth week all who live in it shall be blinded,
And the hearts of all of them shall godlessly forsake wisdom.
And in it a man shall ascend;
And at its close the house of dominion shall be burnt with fire,
And the whole race of the chosen root shall be dispersed.
9. And after that in the seventh week shall an apostate generation arise,
And many shall be its deeds,
And all its deeds shall be apostate.
10. And at its close shall be elected
The elect righteous of the eternal plant of righteousness,
To receive sevenfold instruction concerning all His creation.
[11. For who is there of all the children of men that is able to hear the voice of the Holy One without being troubled? And who can think His thoughts? and who is there that can behold all the works of heaven? 12. And how should there be one who could behold the heaven, and who is there that could understand the things of heaven and see a soul or a spirit and could tell thereof, or ascend and see all their ends and think them or do like them? 13. And who is there of all men that could know what is the breadth and the length of the earth, and to whom has been shown the measure of all of them? 14. Or is there any one who could discern the length of the heaven and how great is its height, and upon what it is founded, and how great is the number of the stars, and where all the luminaries rest?]

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 1 "†gave†" carries daggers on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "Gave. The text is corrupt." v. 2 "(them)" is Charles's round-bracket supply. v. 5 "**his posterity**" is in unmistakable thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "His posterity. The text reads 'after him (or 'it') it shall come (or 'become') the plant of righteousness', &c. But, since this is unsatisfactory however we take it, I suggest that אחריו (='after him' or 'it') stood before the translator but was corrupt for אחריתו ='his posterity'." — a Hebrew retroversion emendation. The interpolation [93:11–14] is in square brackets spanning pp. 231–232; Charles's introduction (p. 218, sighted) lists "93:11–14" among the interpolations and notes the Apocalypse of Weeks "has all the appearance of an earlier fragment incorporated in his work by the original author of 91–104." The v. 8 note (sighted): "An apostate generation. The sixth week: the apostasy of Israel and the destruction of the Temple." The v. 10 note (sighted): "Sevenfold instruction. The sevenfold instruction of the elect." No corner or angle brackets in XCIII.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And after that Enoch both †gave† and began to tell from the books. 2. And Enoch said: "About the children of righteousness and about the chosen of the world, and about the plant of what is right, I will speak these things — yes, I, Enoch, will tell (them) to you, my sons: according to what appeared to me in the heavenly vision, and what I have come to know through the word of the holy angels, and have learned from the heavenly tablets."
3. And Enoch began to tell from the books and said: "I was born seventh in the first week, while judgment and righteousness still held.
4. And after me, in the second week, great wickedness will rise, and deceit will have sprung up. And in it there will be the first end. And in it a man will be saved. And after it ends, unrighteousness will grow, and a law will be made for the sinners.
5. And after that, in the third week, at its end, a man will be chosen as the plant of righteous judgment, and **his posterity** will become the plant of righteousness forevermore.
6. And after that, in the fourth week, at its end, visions of the holy and righteous will be seen, and a law for all generations and an enclosure will be made for them.
7. And after that, in the fifth week, at its end, the house of glory and rule will be built forever.
8. And after that, in the sixth week, all who live in it will be blinded, and the hearts of all of them will godlessly leave wisdom behind. And in it a man will go up; and at its end the house of rule will be burned with fire, and the whole race of the chosen root will be scattered.
9. And after that, in the seventh week, a generation of deserters will rise, and many will be its deeds, and all its deeds will be desertion.
10. And at its end will be chosen the chosen righteous of the everlasting plant of righteousness, to receive sevenfold teaching about all His creation.
[11. For who is there of all the children of men that can hear the voice of the Holy One without being troubled? And who can think His thoughts? And who is there that can look on all the works of heaven? 12. And how could there be one who could look on the heaven, and who is there that could understand the things of heaven and see a soul or a spirit and could tell of it, or go up and see all their ends and think them or do like them? 13. And who is there of all men that could know what is the breadth and the length of the earth, and to whom has been shown the measure of all of them? 14. Or is there anyone who could discern the length of the heaven and how great is its height, and on what it is founded, and how great is the number of the stars, and where all the lights of heaven rest?]

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 94

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 94" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_94), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 234–236 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse, sign, and bracket faithfully), but the thick-type emendation invisible in the transcription was settled on the scans and is marked in the base below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCIV = vv. 1–11 exactly, spanning printed pp. 234–236; "XCV. 1." begins on p. 236 immediately after v. 11. Display heads: "XCIV. 1–5. *Admonitions to the Righteous.*" (p. 234) and "XCIV. 6–11. *Woes for the Sinners.*" (p. 235). Inline head: bold "XCIV. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER XCIV." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 234 (even-page pattern); p. 235 "Chapter XCIV. 1–10"; p. 236 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **Thick type (Charles's emendation, invisible in the transcription):** "**evilly-entreat**" (v. 5) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Square brackets [ ] (interpolation):** "[And those who acquire gold and silver in judgement suddenly shall perish.]" (v. 7d). No daggers, no corner brackets, no angle brackets, no round parentheses in XCIV.

XCIV. 1. And now I say unto you, my sons, love righteousness and walk therein;
For the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptation,
But the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish.
2. And to certain men of a generation shall the paths of violence and of death be revealed,
And they shall hold themselves afar from them,
And shall not follow them.
3. And now I say unto you the righteous:
Walk not in the paths of wickedness, nor in the paths of death,
And draw not nigh to them, lest ye be destroyed.
4. But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life,
And walk in the paths of peace,
And ye shall live and prosper.
5. And hold fast my words in the thoughts of your hearts,
And suffer them not to be effaced from your hearts;
For I know that sinners will tempt men to **evilly-entreat** wisdom,
So that no place may be found for her,
And no manner of temptation may minish.
6. Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression
And lay deceit as a foundation;
For they shall be suddenly overthrown,
And they shall have no peace.
7. Woe to those who build their houses with sin;
For from all their foundations shall they be overthrown,
And by the sword shall they fall.
[And those who acquire gold and silver in judgement suddenly shall perish.]
8. Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches,
And from your riches shall ye depart,
Because ye have not remembered the Most High in the days of your riches.
9. Ye have committed blasphemy and unrighteousness,
And have become ready for the day of slaughter,
And the day of darkness and the day of the great judgement.
10. Thus I speak and declare unto you:
He who hath created you will overthrow you,
And for your fall there shall be no compassion,
And your Creator will rejoice at your destruction.
11. And your righteous ones in those days shall be
A reproach to the sinners and the godless.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 5 "**evilly-entreat**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "'make ... evil', apparently a misrendering of κακοποιεῖν." — the thick type marks his restoration of the verb. The v. 5 note also gives "No place may be found for her: cf. 42^1." The [7d] interpolation is in square brackets on p. 235 (running head "Chapter XCIV. 1–10"); Charles's note (sighted): "[And those who acquire ... perish.] I have bracketed this sentence as an interpolation. The subject of riches is not dealt with till the next woe in ver. 8." and "8. Our author does not condemn the acquisition of wealth in itself but its acquisition by wrong means. Cf. 97^8, from which passage this interpolation may in part be drawn." The v. 1 note (sighted) cites the Greek parallel "1 Tim. 1^15 ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος" ("worthy of acceptation"). The v. 7 note (sighted) cites Jer. 22^13 with the Hebrew "הוי בנה ביתו בלא־צדק" ("Woe to him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness"). No daggers, no corner or angle brackets, no round parentheses in XCIV.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** one — the thick-type "**evilly-entreat**" (v. 5) is Charles's emendation (restoring the verb behind the corrupt Ge'ez, cf. κακοποιεῖν), invisible in the transcription, marked in the base above. Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word. The transcription's display heads ("XCIV. 1-5. Admonitions to the Righteous." / "XCIV. 6-11. Woes for the Sinners.") match the print's display heads; its "CHAPTER XCIV." is a normalization of the inline "XCIV. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And now I say to you, my sons: love righteousness and walk in it. For the paths of righteousness deserve to be embraced, but the paths of unrighteousness will suddenly be destroyed and disappear.
2. And to certain men of a generation the paths of violence and of death will be shown, and they will keep themselves far from them, and will not follow them.
3. And now I say to you, the righteous: do not walk in the paths of wickedness, nor in the paths of death, and do not come near to them, or you will be destroyed.
4. But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and a chosen life, and walk in the paths of peace, and you will live and prosper.
5. And hold my words fast in the thoughts of your hearts, and do not let them be wiped from your hearts. For I know that sinners will lure men to **treat wisdom badly**, so that no place will be found for her, and no kind of lure will grow less.
6. Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression and lay deceit as a foundation; for they will be suddenly thrown down, and they will have no peace.
7. Woe to those who build their houses with sin; for from all their foundations they will be thrown down, and by the sword they will fall. [And those who gather gold and silver by judgment will suddenly die.]
8. Woe to you, you rich, for you have trusted in your riches, and from your riches you will go away, because you have not remembered the Most High in the days of your riches.
9. You have done blasphemy and unrighteousness, and have become ripe for the day of slaughter, and the day of darkness and the day of the great judgment.
10. This is what I say and tell to you: He who created you will throw you down, and for your fall there will be no pity, and your Maker will rejoice at your ruin.
11. And your righteous ones in those days will be a shame to the sinners and the godless.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **The Two Ways, pressed home:** Charles's note on 91:18–19 (sighted at ch. 91's G1) already flags 94:1–4 as the fullest statement of the "Two Ways" — "'paths of righteousness' 94^1, 'paths of peace' 94^4, 'paths of unrighteousness' 94^1, 'paths of violence and of death' 94^2, 'paths of wickedness' and 'paths of death' 94^3" — "one of the earliest non-canonical references to the 'Two Ways'." The draft keeps every "paths" phrase verbatim and does not flatten them. G3 item. The cross-references stand in the apparatus only, as built.
- **The woe parallelism kept:** vv. 6–8 are three woe-oracles in parallel ("Woe to those who build... / Woe to those who build their houses... / Woe to you, ye rich..."); the draft keeps the "Woe to..." openings and the parallel structure, not prose summaries. Disclosed.
- **Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your (vv. 1, 3–5, 8–10):** plain register per the ch. 9 standing rule; disclosed.
- **"**evilly-entreat**" in thick type (v. 5) → "**treat wisdom badly**":** Charles's own emendation (restoring the verb; cf. κακοποιεῖν) — marked in base and draft per the ch. 2 standing rule. "evilly-entreat" is not plain English; "treat badly" keeps the sense. Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"worthy of acceptation" → "deserve to be embraced" (v. 1):** plain register; "acceptation" is archaic. Charles's Greek parallel (1 Tim. 1:15 ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος) is apparatus. Disclosed.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 95

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 95" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_95), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 236–237 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below. One material transcription-vs-print correction was needed (the dagger span in v. 1); the base below follows the print.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCV = vv. 1–7 exactly, spanning printed pp. 236–237; "XCVI. 1." begins on p. 237 immediately after v. 7. Display subhead (p. 236, italic, with NO chapter-number prefix): "*Enoch's Grief: fresh Woes against the Sinners.*" Inline head: bold "XCV. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER XCV." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 236 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 237 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **No thick type** in XCV. **Daggers † (corrupt):** "†of†" (v. 1 — daggers on "of" ONLY, see Material corrections); the whole of v. 2 ("†Who has permitted you to practise reproaches and wickedness? And so judgement shall overtake you, sinners.†"). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial):** "[a cloud of]" (v. 1). No corner brackets, no angle brackets, no round parentheses in XCV.

XCV. 1. Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters
That I might weep over you,
And pour down my tears as a cloud †of† waters:
That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!
2. †Who has permitted you to practise reproaches and wickedness?
And so judgement shall overtake you, sinners.†
3. Fear not the sinners, ye righteous;
For again will the Lord deliver them into your hands,
That ye may execute judgement upon them according to your desires.
4. Woe to you who fulminate anathemas which cannot be reversed:
Healing shall therefore be far from you because of your sins.
5. Woe to you who requite your neighbour with evil;
For ye shall be requited according to your works.
6. Woe to you, lying witnesses,
And to those who weigh out injustice,
For suddenly shall ye perish.
7. Woe to you, sinners, for ye persecute the righteous;
For ye shall be delivered up and persecuted because of injustice,
And heavy shall its yoke be upon you.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 1's third line reads "And pour down my tears as a cloud †of† waters:" — the daggers enclose "of" alone, on both scans (see Material corrections). "[a cloud of]" is in square brackets on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "'Cloud' here is impossible, however it may be in the next line. Its genesis is, I think, clear. The text = מי־יתן עיני ענן מים. Here the impossible ענן is either a dittograph of עיני: then we should have 'Oh that mine eyes were waters': or it is a corruption of עין. In that case we should have 'Oh that mine eyes were a spring of waters'. In this latter case we might compare 2 Bar. 35^2 'Become ye springs, O mine eyes, and ye, mine eyelids, a fount of tears'. Our text, of course, is based on Jer. 9^1 'Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears'." The note on "as a cloud of waters" (sighted): "= כענן מים, which should probably have been translated 'as a cloud pours waters': or still better take מים as corrupt for ודם: then we should have 'as a cloud (pours) rain'." v. 2's daggers enclose the whole verse on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "Who has permitted (lit. 'given') you (g, β [= מי נתנכם]). But α–g [= מי תתנכם] 'Who will give you' or 'Oh that ye were' is probably right. Then either omitting 'to practise' with g, or emending tĕgabĕrû into tĕtgabarû, we should have 'Oh that ye were become a reproach and wickedness'. ... The couplet would then run: 'Oh that ye were become a reproach and an evil / And that so judgement might overtake you, sinners.'" v. 3's note (sighted): "Yet let not the righteous fear; for the period of their supremacy is at hand; cf. 91^12. Again. The writer may refer to the Maccabean victories."

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** one — v. 1's dagger span: the transcription reads "as a cloud †of waters†" (daggers on "of waters"); the print on both scans reads "as a cloud †of† waters:" (daggers on "of" only). The base above follows the print. Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word. The transcription's display head ("XCV. Enoch's Grief: fresh Woes against the Sinners.") matches the print's italic subhead; its "CHAPTER XCV." is a normalization of the inline "XCV. 1.".

## Control column (labelled, not independently transcribed in this lane)

- **Greek (Chester Beatty papyrus covers 97–107; older Greek stream for this chapter):** ch. 95 lies outside the Chester Beatty coverage. Greek control for this chapter exists only through Charles's printed footnotes — sighted here: the v. 2 note citing *g* (omitting "to practise") and the *g*/β/α fork on "Who has permitted you." No Greek wording independently transcribed in this lane; none of the Greek forks is imported into the translation.
- **Aramaic (Qumran):** scraps exist for the section in principle; no Aramaic wording is claimed for ch. 95 here.
- **Laurence (1821, PD, check-only):** not consulted as a skeleton in this slice.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Oh, that my eyes were [a cloud of] waters, that I might weep over you, and pour down my tears as a cloud †of† waters — that I might rest from the trouble of my heart!
2. †Who has allowed you to keep doing shameful things and wickedness? And so judgment will catch up with you, sinners.†
3. Do not fear the sinners, you righteous; for the Lord will again give them into your hands, so that you may pass judgment on them as you see fit.
4. Woe to you who hurl curses that cannot be taken back: healing will be far from you because of your sins.
5. Woe to you who pay back your neighbor with evil; for you will be paid back for what you have done.
6. Woe to you, lying witnesses, and to those who measure out injustice, for you will suddenly die.
7. Woe to you, sinners, for you hunt down the righteous; for you will be handed over and hunted down for your injustice, and its yoke will lie heavy on you.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Enoch's grief:** the chapter opens with Enoch's lament (v. 1, after Jer. 9:1) before the fresh woes (vv. 4–7) — the draft keeps the lament's "Oh that..." shape, not a prose summary. The italic subhead has no chapter-number prefix in print — a typographic fact, recorded.
- **The †of† correction (v. 1):** the print daggers "of" alone; the transcription's "†of waters†" is corrected. The draft keeps "†of†" visible. Whether the reading text keeps the daggers stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"[a cloud of]" kept in square brackets (v. 1):** Charles's editorial bracket ("'Cloud' here is impossible"); the draft keeps it visible. The Hebrew discussion (dittograph/corruption, Jer. 9:1, 2 Bar. 35:2) is apparatus. The question of bracket visibility was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.

Charles's proposed reconstruction ("Oh that ye were become a reproach and an evil...") is apparatus, not imported. The question of keeping the daggers was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 96

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 96" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_96), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 237–239 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse, sign, and bracket faithfully), but two thick-type emendations invisible in the transcription were settled on the scans and are marked in the base below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCVI = vv. 1–8 exactly, spanning printed pp. 237–239; "XCVII. 1." begins on p. 239 immediately after v. 8. Display head (p. 237): "XCVI. *Grounds of Hopefulness for the Righteous: Woes for the Wicked.*" Inline head: bold "XCVI. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER XCVI." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 237 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 238 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 239 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **Thick type (Charles's emendations, invisible in the transcription):** "**wine in large bowls**" (v. 5) and "**from every fountain**" (v. 6) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Square brackets [ ] (interpolation):** the whole of v. 2 ("[2. No daggers in the main text of XCVI (but see the apparatus oddity below); no corner brackets, no angle brackets.

XCVI. 1. Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you,
And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.
[2. And in the day of the tribulation of the sinners,
Your children shall mount and rise as eagles,
And higher than the vultures will be your nest,
And ye shall ascend and enter the crevices of the earth,
And the clefts of the rock for ever as coneys before the unrighteous,
And the sirens shall sigh because of you—and weep.]
3. Wherefore fear not, ye that have suffered;
For healing shall be your portion,
And a bright light shall enlighten you,
And the voice of rest ye shall hear from heaven.
4. Woe unto you, ye sinners, for your riches make you appear like the righteous,
But your hearts convict you of being sinners,
And this fact shall be a testimony against you for a memorial of (your) evil deeds.
5. Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat,
And drink **wine in large bowls**,
And tread under foot the lowly with your might.
6. Woe to you who drink water **from every fountain**,
For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away,
Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.
7. Woe to you who work unrighteousness
And deceit and blasphemy:
It shall be a memorial against you for evil.
8. Woe to you, ye mighty,
Who with might oppress the righteous;
For the day of your destruction is coming.
In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 5 "**wine in large bowls**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "†Wine in large bowls†, i.e. not in wine cups. " — the footnote LEMMA carries daggers (†Wine in large bowls†) while the main text carries thick type: an apparatus oddity, recorded, not acted on (the main text is followed). The emendation restores the Amos 6:6 phrase. v. 6 "**from every fountain**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted) emends the Ge'ez reading "at all times" (בְּכָל־עֵת) to "from every fountain" (מִכָּל־עַיִן). The [v. 2] interpolation is in square brackets spanning pp. 237–238 on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "must be an interpolation: it is foolish in itself and interrupts the context. It is the wicked who will flee to hide themselves in secret places, 97^3 100^4 102^1, and not the righteous." The v. 2 "sirens" note (sighted): "The sirens. Whether sirens (so the Ethiopic version renders σειρῆνες Is. 13^21 Jer. 27^39) or satyrs, the meaning of the word is uncertain. gt, β read 'as the sirens'." The v. 5 "finest of the wheat" note (sighted): "Pss. 81^17 (חלב חטה) 147^14." — Hebrew cited. "(your)" (v. 4) is Charles's round-bracket supply. No daggers in the XCVI main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** two — the thick-type "**wine in large bowls**" (v. 5) and "**from every fountain**" (v. 6) are Charles's emendations, invisible in the transcription, marked in the base above. ## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Take hope, you righteous; for the sinners will suddenly die before your eyes, and you will rule over them as you wish.
[2. And in the day of trouble for the sinners, your children will rise and soar like eagles, and your nest will be higher than the vultures'. And you will go up and enter the cracks of the earth, and the clefts of the rock forever, like rabbits hiding from the wicked, and the sirens will sigh over you — and weep.]
3. So do not be afraid, you who have suffered; for healing will be your share, and a bright light will shine on you, and you will hear the voice of rest from heaven.
4. Woe to you, you sinners, for your riches make you look like the righteous, but your hearts prove you are sinners, and this will stand as a witness against you, a reminder of (your) evil deeds.
5. Woe to you who eat the finest wheat, and drink **wine in large bowls**, and trample the lowly underfoot with your power.
6. Woe to you who drink water **from every fountain**, for you will suddenly be used up and dry up, because you have left the fountain of life.
7. Woe to you who do unrighteousness and deceit and blasphemy: it will stand as a reminder against you, for evil.
8. Woe to you, you mighty, who crush the righteous with your power; for the day of your ruin is coming. In those days many good days will come to the righteous — in the day of your judgment.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **Hope and woes:** vv. 1–3 comfort the righteous; vv. 4–8 are five woe-oracles in parallel ("Woe unto you, ye sinners... / Woe to you who devour... / Woe to you who drink water... / Woe to you who work unrighteousness... / Woe to you, ye mighty..."). The draft keeps the "Woe to..." openings, not prose summaries. V. 8's closing promise ("many and good days shall come to the righteous") is kept as the oracle's turn, not flattened.
- **Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your (vv. 1–4, 6, 8):** "ye righteous" → "you righteous"; "ye that have suffered" → "you who have suffered"; plain register per the ch. 9 standing rule; disclosed.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 97

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 97" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_97), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 239–241 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below. Three material transcription-vs-print corrections were needed (the 9^c/9^d labels, the "(brim)full" spacing, the closing quote); the base below follows the print.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCVII = vv. 1–10 exactly, spanning printed pp. 239–241; "XCVIII. 1." begins on p. 241 immediately after v. 10, under the display head "*Self-indulgence of Sinners: Sin originated by Man: all Sin recorded in Heaven: Woes for the Sinners.*" Display head (p. 239): "XCVII. *The Evils in Store for Sinners and the Possessors of Unrighteous Wealth.*" Inline head: bold "XCVII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER XCVII." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 239 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 240 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 241 "Chapters XCVII. 3—XCVIII. 2". **No thick type** in XCVII. **No daggers** in the XCVII main text. **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(ye sinners)" (v. 2); "(brim)" (v. 9^c). No square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in XCVII. The rich men's quoted speech (vv. 8–9^c) is set with double quotation marks in print; the print CLOSES the speech with ."" at the end of 9^c (see Material corrections).

XCVII. 1. Believe, ye righteous, that the sinners will become a shame
And perish in the day of unrighteousness.
2. Be it known unto you (ye sinners) that the Most High is mindful of your destruction,
And the angels of heaven rejoice over your destruction.
3. What will ye do, ye sinners,
And whither will ye flee on that day of judgement,
When ye hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous?
4. Yea, ye shall fare like unto them,
Against whom this word shall be a testimony:
"Ye have been companions of sinners."
5. And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach unto the Lord,
And for you the days of your judgement shall come.
6. And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One,
And your faces shall be covered with shame,
And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness.
7. Woe to you, ye sinners, who live on the mid ocean and on the dry land,
Whose remembrance is evil against you.
8. Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say:
"We have become rich with riches and have possessions;
And have acquired everything we have desired.
9. And now let us do what we purposed:
For we have gathered silver,
9d. And many are the husbandmen in our houses,
9c. And our granaries are (brim)full as with water."
10. Yea and like water your lies shall flow away;
For your riches shall not abide
But speedily ascend from you;
For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness,
And ye shall be given over to a great curse.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** the print's order at v. 9 is 9, **9^d** ("And many are the husbandmen in our houses,"), **9^c** ("And our granaries are (brim)full as with water.") — see Material corrections. The print closes the rich men's speech with ."" after "water" (both scans); the v. 8 speech opens with '"We have become rich'. "(ye sinners)" (v. 2) and "(brim)" (v. 9^c) are Charles's round-bracket supplies. Charles's footnotes (sighted) cite the Chester Beatty Greek throughout: v. 4 "Shall fare (gqu). mt, β 'shall not fare'. Against whom (g)."; v. 5 "Righteous (α–g, β–afhilpv). g1, afhikpv 'holy'."; v. 6 "All the words of (mqt, β–α). g 'all'." and "Great Holy One (g1gmq, n). tu, β–n1a 'Great and Holy One'." with the Matt. 12:36 Greek parallel (πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργόν ...); v. 8 "With riches (mqt, β). > gu."; v. 9 "And many (g1g, 1b). qt, β–1b 'many'. As with water (1g)."; v. 10 "All (gmt, β–n). > 1gqu, n." and "Your lies: i.e. the false things in which you trust." The v. 9 footnote gives Charles's Hebrew retroversion of the rich men's boast (rhyming, cf. Lam. 5:2). No thick type, no daggers in the XCVII main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** three, all at v. 9 —
1. **The 9^c/9^d labels are swapped in the transcription:** the transcription labels "And many are the husbandmen in our houses" as 9c and "And our granaries are (brim) full as with water" as 9d; the print on both scans labels them 9^d and 9^c respectively (the husbandmen line is 9^d, the granaries line is 9^c). The base above follows the print.
2. **"(brim) full" spacing:** the transcription spaces "(brim) full"; the print on both scans reads "(brim)full" (one word). Corrected.
3. **The closing quote:** the transcription omits the closing mark after "water"; the print on both scans closes the rich men's quoted speech with ."" at the end of 9^c. Restored.
Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER XCVII." is a normalization of the inline "XCVII. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Believe, you righteous, that the sinners will become a shame and die in the day of unrighteousness.
2. Let it be known to you (you sinners) that the Most High remembers your ruin, and the angels of heaven rejoice over your ruin.
3. What will you do, you sinners, and where will you run on that day of judgment, when you hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous?
4. Yes, you will share the fate of those against whom this word will stand as a witness: "You have been friends of sinners."
5. And in those days the prayer of the righteous will reach the Lord, and for you the days of your judgment will come.
6. And all the words of your unrighteousness will be read out before the Great Holy One, and your faces will be covered with shame, and He will throw out every work that is built on unrighteousness.
7. Woe to you, you sinners, who live on the open sea and on the dry land, whose memory counts as evil against you.
8. Woe to you who gather silver and gold by unrighteousness and say: "We have become rich with riches and have property; and we have gotten everything we wanted.
9. And now let us do what we planned: for we have piled up silver, 9d. and many are the farm workers in our houses, 9c. and our barns are (brim)full as with water."
10. Yes, your lies will flow away like water; for your riches will not last but will quickly leave you; for you got it all by unrighteousness, and you will be handed over to a great curse.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 98

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 98" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_98), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 241–244 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse and sign faithfully).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCVIII = vv. 1–16 exactly, spanning printed pp. 241–244; "XCIX. 1." begins on p. 244 immediately after v. 16. Display head (p. 241): "*Self-indulgence of Sinners: Sin originated by Man: all Sin recorded in Heaven: Woes for the Sinners.*" Inline head: bold "XCVIII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER XCVIII." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 241 "Chapters XCVII. 3—XCVIII. 2"; p. 242 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 243 "Chapter XCVIII. 3–13"; p. 244 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **No thick type** in XCVIII. **No daggers** in the XCVIII main text. **No square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets, no round parentheses** in the XCVIII main text.

XCVIII. 1. And now I swear unto you, to the wise and to the foolish,
For ye shall have manifold experiences on the earth.
2. For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman,
And coloured garments more than a virgin:
In royalty and in grandeur and in power,
And in silver and in gold and in purple,
And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.
3. Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom,
And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions;
And with all their glory and their splendour,
And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution,
Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.
4. I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, as a mountain has not become a slave,
And a hill does not become the handmaid of a woman,
Even so sin has not been sent upon the earth,
But man of himself has created it,
And under a great curse shall they fall who commit it.
5. And barrenness has not been given to the woman,
But on account of the deeds of her own hands she dies without children.
6. I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, by the Holy Great One,
That all your evil deeds are revealed in the heavens,
And that none of your deeds of oppression are covered and hidden.
7. And do not think in your spirit nor say in your heart that ye do not know and that ye do not see that every sin is every day recorded in heaven in the presence of the Most High. 8. From henceforth ye know that all your oppression wherewith ye oppress is written down every day till the day of your judgement.
9. Woe to you, ye fools, for through your folly shall ye perish: and ye transgress against the wise, and so good hap shall not be your portion. 10. And now, know ye that ye are prepared for the day of destruction: wherefore do not hope to live, ye sinners, but ye shall depart and die; for ye know no ransom; for ye are prepared for the day of the great judgement, for the day of tribulation and great shame for your spirits.
11. Woe to you, ye obstinate of heart, who work wickedness and eat blood:
Whence have ye good things to eat and to drink and to be filled? From all the good things which the Lord the Most High has placed in abundance on the earth; therefore ye shall have no peace. 12. Woe to you who love the deeds of unrighteousness: wherefore do ye hope for good hap unto yourselves? know that ye shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous, and they shall cut off your necks and slay you, and have no mercy upon you. 13. Woe to you who rejoice in the tribulation of the righteous; for no grave shall be dug for you. 14. Woe to you who set at nought the words of the righteous; for ye shall have no hope of life. 15. Woe to you who write down lying and godless words; for they write down their lies that men may hear them and act godlessly towards (their) neighbour. 16. Therefore they shall have no peace but die a sudden death.

**Print-level findings (both scans):** no thick type, no daggers, no brackets of any kind in the XCVIII main text — the chapter is typographically plain. Charles's footnotes (sighted) cite the Chester Beatty Greek: v. 6 "Holy Great One (gqtu)" with "1gm, β–n 'Holy and Great One'"; v. 9 "Transgress against (g1g). m 'know not', q 'tend not', t, β 'hearken not to'."; v. 10 "For (1y, β). g 'and'. > mqt."; v. 11 "Who work (2nd sing. t, β). In 3rd sing. g1gmq." The v. 11 "Eat blood" note (sighted): "cf. 7^5. Not content with enjoying the best of everything that God gives, these sinners eat blood and break the divine law; cf. Book of Jubilees 7^28–32 21^6 Acts 15^29." The v. 10 "No ransom" note (sighted): "Ps. 49^7, 8, 9." The v. 7 "Recorded" note (sighted): "cf. 97^6 98^8 100^10 104^7, 8." The XCVIII division note (p. 241, sighted): "This chapter introduces a fresh division in 91–104. This division, 98–102^3, consists mainly of a denunciation of the sinners, of their errors in life and doctrine, and announces their coming judgement."

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** none — the transcription matched the print word-for-word on wording, punctuation, and verse numbering. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER XCVIII." is a normalization of the inline "XCVIII. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And now I swear to you — to the wise and to the foolish — for you will go through many things on the earth.
2. For you men will dress up more than a woman, and wear colored clothes more than a young girl: in royal splendor and grandeur and power, and in silver and in gold and in purple, and in luxury and in food, they will be lavished like water.
3. So they will lack teaching and wisdom, and they will die for it together with what they own; and with all their glory and their splendor, and in shame and in slaughter and in utter need, their spirits will be thrown into the furnace of fire.
4. I have sworn to you, you sinners: as a mountain has not become a slave, and a hill does not become a woman's servant, so sin has not been sent down on the earth — man on his own has made it, and those who do it will fall under a great curse.
5. And childlessness has not been put on the woman, but because of what her own hands have done, she dies without children.
6. I have sworn to you, you sinners, by the Holy Great One, that all your evil deeds lie open in the heavens, and none of your acts of oppression are covered or hidden.
7. And do not think in your spirit, nor say in your heart, that you do not know and do not see that every sin is written down every day in heaven before the Most High. 8. From now on, know that every act of oppression you do is written down every day until the day of your judgment.
9. Woe to you, you fools, for your folly will kill you: you sin against the wise, and so good fortune will not be yours. 10. And now know that you are headed for the day of ruin: so do not hope to live, you sinners — you will go away and die. For you know of no price that can buy you back; you are headed for the day of the great judgment, for the day of trouble and deep shame for your spirits.
11. Woe to you, you stubborn-hearted, who do wickedness and eat blood. Where do you get good things to eat and drink and your fill? From all the good things the Lord the Most High has put in plenty on the earth — and yet you will have no peace. 12. Woe to you who love to do unrighteousness: why do you hope for good luck for yourselves? Know that you will be handed over to the righteous, and they will cut off your necks and kill you, and show you no mercy. 13. Woe to you who celebrate when the righteous suffer; for no grave will be dug for you. 14. Woe to you who despise the words of the righteous; for you will have no hope of life. 15. Woe to you who write down lying, godless words; for they write down their lies so that men will hear them and treat (their) neighbor without godliness. 16. So they will have no peace, but will die a sudden death.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 99

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 99" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_99), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 244–247 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse, sign, and bracket faithfully), but the thick-type emendation invisible in the transcription was settled on the scans and is marked in the base below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter XCIX = vv. 1–16 exactly, spanning printed pp. 244–247; "C. 1." begins on p. 248 immediately after v. 16. Display head (p. 244): "XCIX. *Woes pronounced on the Godless, the Lawbreakers: evil Plight of Sinners in the Last Days: further Woes.*" Inline head: bold "XCIX. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER XCIX." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 244 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 245 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 246 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 247 "Chapter XCIX. 8–16". **Thick type (Charles's emendation, invisible in the transcription):** "**His fierce indignation**" (v. 16) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Angle brackets ⟨ ⟩ (Charles's supply):** "⟨and stone⟩" (v. 7). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial gloss):** "[into sinners]" (v. 2). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(that are still)" (v. 5); "(to them)" (v. 12); "(their)" (v. 15). No daggers, no corner brackets in the XCIX main text.

XCIX. 1. Woe to you who work godlessness,
And glory in lying and extol them:
Ye shall perish, and no happy life shall be yours.
2. Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness,
And transgress the eternal law,
And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]:
They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.
3. In those days make ready, ye righteous, to raise your prayers as a memorial,
And place them as a testimony before the angels,
That they may place the sin of the sinners for a memorial before the Most High.
4. In those days the nations shall be stirred up,
And the families of the nations shall arise on the day of destruction.
5. And in those days the destitute shall go forth and carry off their children,
And they shall abandon them, so that their children shall perish through them:
Yea, they shall abandon their children (that are still) sucklings, and not return to them,
And shall have no pity on their beloved ones.
6. And again I swear to you, ye sinners, that sin is prepared for a day of unceasing bloodshed. 7. And they who worship stones, and grave images of gold and silver and wood ⟨and stone⟩ and clay, and those who worship impure spirits and demons, and all kinds of idols not according to knowledge, shall get no manner of help from them.
8. And they shall become godless by reason of the folly of their hearts,
And their eyes shall be blinded through the fear of their hearts
And through visions in their dreams.
9. Through these they shall become godless and fearful;
For they shall have wrought all their work in a lie,
And shall have worshipped a stone:
Therefore in an instant shall they perish.
10. But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, and understand them,
And observe the paths of the Most High, and walk in the path of His righteousness,
And become not godless with the godless;
For they shall be saved.
11. Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours;
For you shall be slain in Sheol.
12. Woe to you who make deceitful and false measures,
And (to them) who cause bitterness on the earth;
For they shall thereby be utterly consumed.
13. Woe to you who build your houses through the grievous toil of others,
And all their building materials are the bricks and stones of sin;
I tell you ye shall have no peace.
14. Woe to them who reject the measure and eternal heritage of their fathers
And whose souls follow after idols;
For they shall have no rest.
15. Woe to them who work unrighteousness and help oppression,
And slay their neighbours until the day of the great judgement.
16. For He shall cast down your glory,
And bring affliction on your hearts,
And shall arouse **His fierce indignation**
And destroy you all with the sword;
And all the holy and righteous shall remember your sins.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 16 "**His fierce indignation**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "His fierce indignation. 1yβ read 'the spirit of His indignation' = רוח אפו corrupt for חרון אפו 'His fierce indignation'. gmqt read 'His indignation and His spirit'." — a Hebrew retroversion emendation. v. 7 "⟨and stone⟩" is in angle brackets on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "I have added 'and stone' in accordance with Tertullian, De Idol. iv" — quoting Tertullian's Latin in the note. The v. 6 note (sighted) quotes Tertullian's rendering of the verse: "in diem sanguinis perditionis" (= εἰς ἡμέραν αἵματος ἀπωλείας, "for a day of blood of perdition"). v. 2 "[into sinners]" is in square brackets on both scans — Charles's gloss. The v. 12 note (sighted): "Cause bitterness (mt, β). gq 'know', 1g 'tempt'." The v. 14 note (sighted): "Whose souls follow after (1gm). gqtu 'and follow after the souls of'. β 'who cause their souls to follow after'." The v. 16 "Holy and righteous" note (sighted): "(g1gmq). ∽ t, β." No daggers, no corner brackets in the XCIX main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** one — the thick-type "**His fierce indignation**" (v. 16) is Charles's emendation (רוח אפו → חרון אפו), invisible in the transcription, marked in the base above. Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word, including the ⟨and stone⟩ angle brackets, the [into sinners] gloss, and the round-bracket supplies. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER XCIX." is a normalization of the inline "XCIX. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Woe to you who do godless things, and take pride in lying and praise it: you will die, and no happy life will be yours.
2. Woe to those who twist the words of what is right, and break the everlasting law, and turn themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: they will be trampled underfoot on the earth.
3. In those days, get ready, you righteous, to lift up your prayers as a reminder, and set them as a witness before the angels, so that they may set the sin of the sinners as a reminder before the Most High.
4. In those days the nations will be stirred up, and the families of the nations will rise on the day of ruin.
5. And in those days the poor will go out and carry off their children, and will leave them, so that their children will die because of them. Yes, they will leave their children (who are still) babies, and will not come back to them, and will feel no pity for their loved ones.
6. And again I swear to you, you sinners, that sin is set aside for a day of endless bloodshed. 7. And those who worship stones, and carved images of gold and silver and wood ⟨and stone⟩ and clay, and those who worship unclean spirits and demons, and every kind of idol without knowing, will get no help at all from them.
8. And they will become godless because their hearts are foolish, and their eyes will be blinded by the fear in their hearts and by visions in their dreams.
9. Because of these they will become godless and afraid; for they have done all their work in a lie, and have worshiped a stone — so in a moment they will die.
10. But in those days, blessed are all who take the words of wisdom to heart, and understand them, and keep the paths of the Most High, and walk in the path of His righteousness, and do not become godless with the godless; for they will be saved.
11. Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbors; for you will be killed in Sheol.
12. Woe to you who make dishonest, false measures, and (to those) who bring bitterness on the earth; for they will be completely used up by it.
13. Woe to you who build your houses with the hard labor of others, and all their building stuff is bricks and stones of sin — I tell you, you will have no peace.
14. Woe to those who throw away the measure and everlasting inheritance of their fathers, and whose souls chase after idols; for they will have no rest.
15. Woe to those who do unrighteousness and help oppression, and kill their neighbors until the day of the great judgment.
16. For He will bring down your glory, and bring pain on your hearts, and will stir up **His fierce anger**, and destroy you all with the sword; and all the holy and righteous will remember your sins.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **The woes, the plight, the further woes:** the chapter moves from woes on the godless (vv. 1–2), to the righteous' memorial-prayers and the nations' stirring (vv. 3–4), to the last-days plight of the destitute (v. 5), to the idol-worshipers' oath (vv. 6–9), to the blessed (v. 10), to further woes (vv. 11–16). The draft keeps the "Woe to..." parallelism throughout, not prose summaries.
- **Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your throughout:** "ye shall perish" → "you will die"; plain register per the ch. 9 standing rule; disclosed. Referred to the editor's read-through and closed there on 2026-10-14. (Note: v. 11 already reads "For you shall be slain" in the base — "you," not "ye.")
- **"**His fierce indignation**" in thick type (v. 16) → "**His fierce anger**":** Charles's own emendation (Hebrew retroversion רוח אפו → חרון אפו) — marked in base and draft per the ch. 2 standing rule. "indignation" → "anger" is plain register; disclosed. Whether the reading text signals the emendation stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"⟨and stone⟩" kept in angle brackets (v. 7):** Charles's supply "in accordance with Tertullian" — kept visible; the Tertullian Latin (De Idol. iv) is apparatus. The question of bracket visibility was closed at the editor's read-through on 2026-10-14; the printed choice stands.
- **"[into sinners]" kept in square brackets (v. 2):** Charles's gloss — kept visible; disclosed.
- **"(that are still)" (v. 5), "(to them)" (v. 12), "(their)" (v. 15):** Charles's round-bracket supplies kept visible per the standing rule.
- **"work godlessness" → "do godless things" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"glory in lying and extol them" → "take pride in lying and praise it" (v. 1):** "glory in" → "take pride in"; "extol" → "praise"; disclosed.
- **"no happy life shall be yours" → "no happy life will be yours" (v. 1):** kept; disclosed.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 100

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 100" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_100), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 248–251 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse and sign faithfully), but the thick-type emendation invisible in the transcription was settled on the scans and is marked in the base below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter C = vv. 1–13 exactly, spanning printed pp. 248–251; "CI. 1." begins on p. 251 immediately after v. 13. Display head (p. 248): "C. *The Sinners destroy each other: Judgement of the Fallen Angels: the Safety of the Righteous: further Woes for the Sinners.*" Inline head: bold "**C. 1.**" run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER C." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 248 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 249 "Chapter C. 1–6"; p. 250 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 251 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **Thick type (Charles's emendation, invisible in the transcription):** "**security**" (v. 6) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(then)" (v. 6). No daggers, no square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in the C main text.

C. 1. And in those days in one place the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten
And brothers one with another shall fall in death
Till the streams flow with their blood.
2. For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons' sons,
And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother:
From dawn till sunset they shall slay one another.
3. And the horse shall walk up to the breast in the blood of sinners,
And the chariot shall be submerged to its height.
4. In those days the angels shall descend into the secret places
And gather together into one place all those who brought down sin,
And the Most High will arise on that day of judgement
To execute great judgement amongst sinners.
5. And over all the righteous and holy He will appoint guardians from amongst the holy angels
To guard them as the apple of an eye,
Until He makes an end of all wickedness and all sin,
And though the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nought to fear.
6. And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in **security**,
And shall understand all the words of this book,
And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them
In the overthrow of their sins.
7. Woe to you, Sinners, on the day of strong anguish,
Ye who afflict the righteous and burn them with fire:
Ye shall be requited according to your works.
8. Woe to you, ye obstinate of heart,
Who watch in order to devise wickedness:
Therefore shall fear come upon you
And there shall be none to help you.
9. Woe to you, ye sinners, on account of the words of your mouth,
And on account of the deeds of your hands which your godlessness has wrought,
In blazing flames burning worse than fire shall ye burn.
10. And now, know ye that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins because upon the earth ye execute judgement on the righteous. 11. And He will summon to testify against you every cloud and mist and dew and rain; for they shall all be withheld because of you from descending upon you, and they shall be mindful of your sins. 12. And now give presents to the rain that it be not withheld from descending upon you, nor yet the dew, when it has received gold and silver from you that it may descend. 13. When the hoar-frost and snow with their chilliness, and all the snow-storms with all their plagues fall upon you, in those days ye shall not be able to stand before them.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 6 "**security**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "I have here transposed the words 'the children of the earth' from the second line to the first, and with 1gq taken 'the wise' in the acc. and not in the nom. as in gmt, β. Further, for the phrase 'in security' we find 'ĕmûna (in t, β) = πιστόν or πεποιθότα (cf. Prov. 10^9), 'emani (in g1gm) corrupt." — the thick type marks his adoption of the 'ĕmûna = πιστόν/πεποιθότα reading with the transposition. "(then)" (v. 6) is Charles's round-bracket supply. The v. 4 note (sighted): "Day of judgement (α–tu). tu, β 'day'. Amongst (1gmqu). g 'and amongst', t, β 'on all the'." The v. 5 note (sighted): "All 1^10. > 1gu. The apple of an eye: cf. Deut. 32^10 Ps. 17^8. He makes an end of all (g1gmq^2). q11u, β 'all — has been made an end of'." The v. 7 note (sighted): Charles restores "on the day of strong anguish" by transposition, but prints it in REGULAR type — recorded as a typographic fact (a restoration not marked as an emendation). No daggers, no brackets in the C main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** one — the thick-type "**security**" (v. 6) is Charles's emendation (with transposition; 'ĕmûna = πιστόν/πεποιθότα), invisible in the transcription, marked in the base above. Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER C." is a normalization of the inline "C. 1.". The v. 7 "day of strong anguish" restoration is in regular type in print — the transcription correctly shows no marking.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. And in those days, in one place, fathers together with their sons will be struck down, and brothers will fall dead side by side, until the streams run with their blood.
2. For a man will not hold back his hand from killing his sons and his grandsons, and the sinner will not hold back his hand from his honored brother. From sunrise to sunset they will kill one another.
3. And the horse will wade breast-deep in the blood of sinners, and the chariot will sink up to its top.
4. In those days the angels will go down into the hidden places and gather into one place all those who brought sin down, and the Most High will rise on that day of judgment to carry out great judgment among sinners.
5. And over all the righteous and holy He will set guards from among the holy angels, to guard them as the apple of an eye, until He puts an end to all wickedness and all sin. And though the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nothing to fear.
6. And (then) the children of the earth will see the wise in **safety**, and will understand all the words of this book, and will see that their riches cannot save them when their sins are overthrown.
7. Woe to you, sinners, on the day of great suffering — you who crush the righteous and burn them with fire: you will be paid back for what you have done.
8. Woe to you, you stubborn-hearted, who stay awake to plan wickedness: fear will come on you, and no one will help you.
9. Woe to you, you sinners, because of the words of your mouth, and because of what your hands have done, which your godlessness has worked — in blazing flames, burning worse than fire, you will burn.
10. And now know that He will ask the angels in heaven about your deeds, and the sun and the moon and the stars about your sins, because on earth you pass judgment on the righteous. 11. And He will call every cloud and mist and dew and rain to witness against you; for they will all be held back from coming down on you because of you, and they will remember your sins. 12. So now, offer gifts to the rain so it will come down on you, and to the dew, when it has taken gold and silver from you so it will come down. 13. When the frost and snow with their cold, and all the blizzards with all their plagues, fall on you, in those days you will not be able to stand up against them.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 101

Drafting copy: the 1912 print itself — the Wikisource transcription page for Chapter 101 returned HTTP 403 ("do not repeat this request") for this worker, so the base was transcribed directly from the print scans (the print is the authority in any case). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 251–253 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections apply (no transcription was usable).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter CI = vv. 1–9 exactly, spanning printed pp. 251–253; "CII. 1." begins on p. 253 immediately after v. 9, under the display head "*Terrors of the Day of Judgement: the adverse Fortunes of the Righteous on the Earth.*" Display head (p. 251): "*Exhortation to the Fear of God: all Nature fears Him but not the Sinners.*" Inline head: bold "CI. 1." run into the text. Running heads: p. 251 "Chapters C. 7—CI. 1"; p. 252 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 253 "Chapters CI. 2—CII. 4". **Thick type (Charles's emendations):** "**sailors**" (v. 4 and v. 9) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. No daggers, no square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets, no round parentheses in the CI main text.

CI. 1. Observe the heaven, ye children of heaven, and every work of the Most High, and fear ye Him and work no evil in His presence.
2. If He closes the windows of heaven, and withholds the rain and the dew from descending on the earth on your account, what will ye do then?
3. And if He sends His anger upon you because of your deeds, ye cannot petition Him; for ye spake proud and insolent words against His righteousness: therefore ye shall have no peace.
4. And see ye not the **sailors** of the ships, how their ships are tossed to and fro by the waves, and are shaken by the winds, and are in sore trouble?
5. And therefore do they fear because all their goodly possessions go upon the sea with them, and they have evil forebodings of heart that the sea will swallow them and they will perish therein.
6. Are not the entire sea and all its waters, and all its movements, the work of the Most High, and has He not set limits to its doings, and confined it throughout by the sand?
7. And at His reproof it is afraid and dries up, and all its fish die and all that is in it; but ye sinners that are on the earth fear Him not.
8. Has He not made the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein? Who has given understanding and wisdom to every thing that moves on the earth and in the sea?
9. Do not the **sailors** of the ships fear the sea? Yet sinners fear not the Most High.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** "**sailors**" is in thick type at v. 4 and v. 9 on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "Sailors of the ships. Text = 'kings of the ships' = מלכי האניות corrupt, as Halévy pointed out, for מלחי האנ[יות] = 'sailors of the ships'." — a Hebrew retroversion emendation (מלכי → מלחי). The v. 1 footnote (sighted): "The phrase 'children of heaven' (cf. Pirke Aboth, iii. 22 בנים למקום) is the equivalent of 'sons of God'. The designation is here limited to the righteous Israelites." The v. 4–7 note (sighted): "They who go down to the sea in ships are filled with fear at the might of the sea: how much more should not men fear God by whom the sea has been made and of whom it is sore afraid?" with Ps. 107:23–27 cited. The v. 6 note (sighted) discusses the verb "set limits" with Jer. 5:22, Job 26:10, 38:8–11, Ps. 89:9, 104:9, Prov. 8:29. The v. 9 note (sighted): "The whole argument of the chapter summed up in a few pregnant words." No daggers, no brackets in the CI main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** none applicable — no usable transcription existed (Wikisource HTTP 403, do-not-repeat — not retried); the base is transcribed from the print, which is the authority. The c2 copy confirms the print text word-for-word, including the thick-type "sailors" at vv. 4 and 9.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. Look at the sky, you children of heaven, and every work of the Most High, and fear Him, and do no evil in His presence.
2. If He shuts the windows of heaven, and holds back the rain and the dew from coming down on the earth because of you, what will you do then?
3. And if He sends His anger on you because of what you have done, you cannot beg Him for mercy; for you spoke proud, disrespectful words against His righteousness — so you will have no peace.
4. And do you not see the **sailors** on the ships, how their ships are thrown back and forth by the waves, and shaken by the winds, and in great distress?
5. That is why they are afraid: all their fine belongings go on the sea with them, and they have dark fears in their hearts that the sea will swallow them and they will die there.
6. Is not the whole sea, and all its waters, and all its motions, the work of the Most High? Has He not set bounds to what it does, and fenced it in everywhere with sand?
7. At His rebuke it is afraid and dries up, and all its fish die, and everything in it; but you sinners on the earth do not fear Him.
8. Has He not made heaven and earth, and everything in them? Who has given sense and wisdom to everything that moves on the earth and in the sea?
9. Do not the **sailors** on the ships fear the sea? Yet sinners do not fear the Most High.
