## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 102

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 102" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_102), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 253–255 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below. Two material transcription-vs-print corrections were needed (the "accursed"/"cursed" wording and the thick-type emendations); the base below follows the print.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter CII = vv. 1–11 exactly, spanning printed pp. 253–255; "CIII. 1." begins on p. 255 immediately after v. 11. Display head (p. 253): "*Terrors of the Day of Judgement: the adverse Fortunes of the Righteous on the Earth.*" Inline head: bold "CII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER CII." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 253 "Chapters CI. 2—CII. 4"; p. 254 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 255 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **Thick type (Charles's emendations, invisible in the transcription):** "**wait for**" and "**judgement**" (v. 5) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Daggers † (corrupt):** "†angels shall execute their commands†" (v. 3). No square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets, no round parentheses in the CII main text. The sinners' quoted speech (vv. 6–8) opens with '"As we die' and closes with 'see no light."' (v. 8) — the print's quotation marks.

CII. 1. In those days when He hath brought a grievous fire upon you,
Whither will ye flee, and where will ye find deliverance?
And when He launches forth His word against you
Will you not be affrighted and fear?
2. And all the luminaries shall be affrighted with great fear,
And all the earth shall be affrighted and tremble and be alarmed.
3. And all the †angels shall execute their commands†
And shall seek to hide themselves from the presence of the Great Glory,
And the children of earth shall tremble and quake;
And ye sinners shall be accursed for ever,
And ye shall have no peace.
4. Fear ye not, ye souls of the righteous,
And be hopeful ye that have died in righteousness.
5. And grieve not if your soul into Sheol has descended in grief,
And that in your life your body fared not according to your goodness,
But **wait for** the day of the **judgement** of sinners
And for the day of cursing and chastisement.
6. And yet when ye die the sinners speak over you:
"As we die, so die the righteous,
And what benefit do they reap for their deeds?
7. Behold, even as we, so do they die in grief and darkness,
And what have they more than we?
From henceforth we are equal.
8. And what will they receive and what will they see for ever?
Behold, they too have died,
And henceforth for ever shall they see no light."
9. I tell you, ye sinners, ye are content to eat and drink, and rob and sin, and strip men naked, and acquire wealth and see good days. 10. Have ye seen the righteous how their end falls out, that no manner of violence is found in them till their death? 11. 'Nevertheless they perished and became as though they had not been, and their spirits descended into Sheol in tribulation.'

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 3 "†angels shall execute their commands†" carries daggers on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "The †angels shall execute their commands†. The text is against the parallelism and is clearly here corrupt. It is not good angels that will seek to hide themselves. 'Angels' = מלאכים corrupt for מלכים = 'kings'. We have then a parallel here to Rev. 6^15. But what is the original text behind 'execute their commands' I cannot see." v. 3 "accursed" (not "cursed") on both scans — see Material corrections. v. 5 "**wait for**" and "**judgement**" are in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "Wait for. Here I emend 'ĕnka ba (='moreover' which is here unmeaning) into ṣenḥû la = 'wait for' in 108^2, where this verb occurs in a like context: 'wait for those days', i.e. the days of judgement. Judgement of sinners. Here the text has 'ye became sinners', i.e. kônkemmû ḥaṭeâna (ḥaṭeân g1g, α), which I have emended into kuenanê ḥaṭeân = 'judgement of sinners'. The next line shows that it is the judgement day to which this line must refer. The parallelism is thus restored." The v. 4 note (sighted): "4—CIV. 9. The discussion and condemnation of the Sadducean views of the future life. 4, 5. The righteous are bidden to be of good cheer though their life be such as only sinners deserved, and their latter end be full of grief (vv. 4, 5)." The v. 6–8 note (sighted): "The sinners—the Sadducean opponents—start from the O.T. doctrine of retribution which taught the prosperity of the righteous in this life, and argue that as there is no difference in the lot of the righteous and the wicked in this life ... so there is none in an existence beyond this life; cf. Book of Wisdom 2^1–5 3^2–4 Eccles. 2^14–16 3^19–21, &c." No square brackets, no corner or angle brackets, no round parentheses in the CII main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** two —
1. **"cursed" vs "accursed" (v. 3):** the transcription reads "And ye sinners shall be cursed for ever,"; the print on both scans reads "And ye sinners shall be **accursed** for ever,". The base above follows the print.
2. **Thick type invisible in the transcription:** "**wait for**" and "**judgement**" (v. 5) are Charles's emendations ('ĕnka ba → ṣenḥû la; kônkemmû ḥaṭeâna → kuenanê ḥaṭeân), marked in the base above.
Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER CII." is a normalization of the inline "CII. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. In those days, when He has brought a painful fire on you, where will you run, and where will you find rescue? And when He hurls His word against you, will you not be terrified and afraid?
2. And all the lights of heaven will be terrified with great fear, and the whole earth will be terrified and shake and be alarmed.
3. And all the †angels shall carry out their orders†, and will try to hide from the presence of the Great Glory, and the children of earth will tremble and shake; and you sinners will be cursed forever, and you will have no peace.
4. Do not be afraid, you souls of the righteous, and take hope, you who have died in righteousness.
5. And do not grieve if your soul has gone down to Sheol in sorrow, and if in your life your body did not fare as your goodness deserved — but **wait for** the day of **judgment** on sinners, and for the day of cursing and punishment.
6. And yet, when you die, the sinners say over you: "As we die, so the righteous die — what good do they get from what they have done?
7. Look, just like us, they die in sorrow and darkness. What do they have more than we do? From now on we are equal.
8. What will they get, and what will they see forever? Look, they have died too, and from now on they will never see light again."
9. I tell you, you sinners: you are happy to eat and drink, and steal and sin, and strip men naked, and get rich and enjoy good days. 10. Have you seen how the righteous end — that no violence at all is found in them until they die? 11. "Yet they died and became as if they had never been, and their spirits went down to Sheol in misery."

The draft keeps the debate's two voices distinct (Enoch's comfort, the sinners' quoted boast, Enoch's rejoinder), not a prose summary. ## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 103

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 103" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_103), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 255–259 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse, sign, and bracket faithfully).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter CIII = vv. 1–15 exactly, spanning printed pp. 255–259; "CIV. 1." begins on p. 259 immediately after v. 15. Display head (p. 255): "CIII. *Different Destinies of the Righteous and the Sinners: fresh Objections of the Sinners.*" Inline head: bold "CIII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER CIII." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 255 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 256 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 257 "Chapter CIII. 3–9"; p. 258 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 259 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **No thick type** in CIII. **Daggers † (corrupt):** the pair spanning the v. 12 line break — "that hated us †and smote us; / And to those that hated us †" (see Print-level findings). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial):** "[and destroyed]" (v. 10). No corner brackets, no angle brackets, no round parentheses in the CIII main text. The sinners' ironical speeches (vv. 5–6, 9–15) carry the print's quotation marks.

CIII. 1. Now, therefore, I swear to you, the righteous, by the glory of the Great and Honoured and 2. Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you.
I know a mystery
And have read the heavenly tablets,
And have seen the holy books,
And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them:
3. That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them,
And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness,
And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours,
And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.
4. And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice,
And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One
Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.
5. Woe to you, ye sinners, when ye have died,
If ye die in the wealth of your sins,
And those who are like you say regarding you:
"Blessed are the sinners: they have seen all their days.
6. And now they have died in prosperity and in wealth,
And have not seen tribulation or murder in their life;
And they have died in honour,
And judgement has not been executed on them during their life."
7. Know ye, that their souls will be made to descend into Sheol
And they shall be wretched in their great tribulation.
8. And into darkness and chains and a burning flame where there is grievous judgement shall your spirits enter;
And the great judgement shall be for all the generations of the world.
Woe to you, for ye shall have no peace.
9. Say not in regard to the righteous and good who are in life:
"In our troubled days we have toiled laboriously and experienced every trouble,
And met with much evil and been consumed,
And have become few and our spirit small.
10. And we have been destroyed and have not found any to help us even with a word:
We have been tortured [and destroyed], and not hoped to see life from day to day.
11. We hoped to be the head and have become the tail:
We have toiled laboriously and had no satisfaction in our toil;
And we have become the food of the sinners and the unrighteous,
And they have laid their yoke heavily upon us.
12. They have had dominion over us that hated us †and smote us;
And to those that hated us † we have bowed our necks
But they pitied us not.
13. We desired to get away from them that we might escape and be at rest,
But found no place whereunto we should flee and be safe from them.
14. And we complained to the rulers in our tribulation,
And cried out against those who devoured us,
But they did not attend to our cries
And would not hearken to our voice.
15. And they helped those who robbed us and devoured us and those who made us few; and they concealed their oppression, and they did not remove from us the yoke of those that devoured us and dispersed us and murdered us, and they concealed their murder, and remembered not that they had lifted up their hands against us.

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** the v. 12 daggers form a pair spanning the line break: the opening † stands after "us" in "that hated us †and smote us;" and the closing † stands after "us" in "And to those that hated us † we have bowed our necks" — the daggered span is "†and smote us; / And to those that hated us †", on both scans (the transcription's positions match). Charles's note (sighted): "To those that hated us. I think that this is a dittograph from the preceding line, and that the clause which should be here has been transposed into that line. Hence I suggest that we should read: 'They have had dominion over us that hated us, / And to those that smote us we have bowed our necks, / But they pitied us not.'" v. 10 "[and destroyed]" is in square brackets on both scans — Charles's editorial supply. The v. 9 "Our spirit small" note (sighted): "Not 'humble' but 'poor spirited' (μικρόψυχος)." The v. 9–15 frame note (sighted): "These verses are in the mouth of the wicked an ironical description of the lot of the righteous. For the time being they speak in the person of the righteous." with the 1st/3rd-person MS. discussion (1g vs the rest). The v. 8 "Of the world" note (sighted): "(α). β 'unto eternity'." No thick type, no corner or angle brackets, no round parentheses in the CIII main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** none — the transcription matched the print word-for-word on wording, punctuation, dagger positions, and brackets. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER CIII." is a normalization of the inline "CIII. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. So now, I swear to you, the righteous, by the glory of the Great and Honored and 2. Mighty One in power, and by His greatness I swear to you.
I know a secret, and have read the heavenly tablets, and have seen the holy books, and have found written in them about them:
3. that all goodness and joy and glory are ready for them, and written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, and that rich good will be given to you as pay for your hard work, and that your share is far greater than the share of the living.
4. And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness will live and rejoice, and their spirits will not die, nor will their memory fade from before the Great One, for all the generations of the world. So do not fear their insults any longer.
5. Woe to you, you sinners, when you have died — if you die loaded with your sins — and those like you say about you: "Good for the sinners! They have enjoyed all their days.
6. They have now died rich and wealthy, and never saw trouble or killing in their lives; they died honored, and judgment never caught up with them while they lived."
7. Know that their souls will be brought down to Sheol, and they will be miserable in their great suffering.
8. Your spirits will enter darkness and chains and a burning flame, where judgment is painful; and the great judgment will last for all the generations of the world. Woe to you, for you will have no peace.
9. Do not say about the righteous and good who are alive: "In our hard days we have worked ourselves to the bone and gone through every trouble, met with much evil and been worn down, and grown few, and our spirit is crushed.
10. We have been ruined, and found no one to help us even with a word. We have been tortured [and destroyed], and never hoped to see another day of life.
11. We hoped to be the head and have become the tail. We have worked ourselves to the bone and got no joy from our work; we have become food for the sinners and the wicked, and they have laid their yoke heavily on us.
12. Those who hated us †have ruled over us and beaten us; to those who hated us† we have bowed our necks, but they showed us no pity.
13. We wanted to get away from them, to escape and rest, but found no place to run where we would be safe from them.
14. We complained to the rulers in our suffering, and cried out against those who swallowed us up, but they paid no attention to our cries and would not listen to our voice.
15. They helped those who robbed us and swallowed us up and thinned our numbers; they hid what was done to us, and did not lift the yoke of those who swallowed us up and scattered us and murdered us — they hid the murder, and never remembered that they had raised their hands against us.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 104

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 104" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_104), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 259–262 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse and sign faithfully).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter CIV = vv. 1–13 exactly, spanning printed pp. 259–262; "CV. 1." begins on p. 262 immediately after v. 13. Display head (p. 259): "CIV. *Assurances given to the Righteous: Admonitions to Sinners and the Falsifiers of the Words of Uprightness.*" Inline head: bold "CIV. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER CIV." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 259 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 260 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 261 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 262 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **No thick type** in CIV. **No daggers** in the CIV main text. **No square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets, no round parentheses** in the CIV main text. The chapter closes with .' (v. 13: '...be recompensed.') — the print's closing quotation mark for the long speech.

CIV. 1. I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One. 2. Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you. 3. And in your cry, cry for judgement, and it shall appear to you; for all your tribulation shall be visited on the rulers, and on all who helped those who plundered you. 4. Be hopeful, and cast not away your hope; for ye shall have great joy as the angels of heaven. 5. What shall ye be obliged to do? Ye shall not have to hide on the day of the great judgement and ye shall not be found as sinners, and the eternal judgement shall be far from you for all the generations of the world. 6. And now fear not, ye righteous, when ye see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for ye shall become companions of the hosts of heaven. 7. And, although ye sinners say: "All our sins shall not be searched out and be written down," nevertheless they shall write down all your sins every day. 8. And now I show unto you that light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins. 9. Be not godless in your hearts, and lie not and alter not the words of uprightness, nor charge with lying the words of the Holy Great One, nor take account of your idols; for all your lying and all your godlessness issue not in righteousness but in great sin. 10. And now I know this mystery, that sinners will alter and pervert the words of righteousness in many ways, and will speak wicked words, and lie, and practise great deceits, and write books concerning their words. 11. But when they write down truthfully all my words in their languages, and do not change or minish ought from my words but write them all down truthfully—all that I first testified concerning them. 12. Then, I know another mystery, that books will be given to the righteous and the wise to become a cause of joy and uprightness and much wisdom. 13. And to them shall the books be given, and they shall believe in them and rejoice over them, and then shall all the righteous who have learnt therefrom all the paths of uprightness be recompensed.'

**Print-level findings (both scans):** no thick type, no daggers, no brackets of any kind in the CIV main text — typographically plain. Charles's footnotes (sighted): v. 1 "The Great One: cf. 14^2."; v. 2 "Now. This word (= עתה) is used here not of the immediate present but of the impending future. Shine as the lights: cf. Dan. 12^3 4 Ezra 7^97, 125."; v. 6 "Prospering in their ways: g1gmqt. β 'prospering in their lusts'." and the "hosts" note — "β reads ḥarâ; gmqt read ḥêrâna = τῶν ἀγαθῶν, possibly corrupt for τῶν ἀγγέλων" (= "of the good ones," possibly corrupt for "of the angels"); v. 11 "Aramaic and Greek are the languages here referred to." The v. 13 closing .' marks the end of the long quoted speech (vv. 1–13 are Enoch's oath). No thick type, no daggers.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** none — the transcription matched the print word-for-word on wording, punctuation, and verse numbering. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER CIV." is a normalization of the inline "CIV. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. I swear to you that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One, and your names are written before the glory of the Great One. 2. Take hope, for in the past you were shamed by suffering and hardship, but now you will shine like the lights of heaven — you will shine and be seen, and the gates of heaven will be opened to you. 3. And when you cry out, cry out for justice, and it will come to you; for all your suffering will be paid back on the rulers, and on all who helped those who robbed you. 4. Take hope, and do not throw away your hope, for you will have great joy like the angels of heaven. 5. What will you have to do? You will not have to hide on the day of the great judgment, and you will not be found among sinners, and the everlasting judgment will stay far from you for all the generations of the world. 6. And now do not be afraid, you righteous, when you see sinners growing strong and doing well in their ways. Do not keep company with them, but stay far from their violence; for you will become companions of the armies of heaven. 7. And though you sinners say, "Not all our sins will be searched out and written down," they will still write down all your sins every day. 8. And now I show you that light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins. 9. Do not be godless in your hearts, and do not lie or twist the words of what is right, or call the words of the Holy Great One lies, or give thought to your idols; for all your lying and all your godlessness leads not to righteousness but to great sin. 10. And now I know this secret: sinners will change and twist the words of righteousness in many ways, and will speak wicked words, and lie, and carry out great deceptions, and write books about their own words. 11. But when they write down all my words truthfully in their languages, and do not change or cut anything from my words, but write them all down truthfully — all that I first spoke about them — 12. then I know another secret: books will be given to the righteous and the wise, to bring joy and uprightness and much wisdom. 13. And the books will be given to them, and they will believe them and rejoice in them, and then all the righteous who have learned from them all the paths of uprightness will be repaid."

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

The v. 11 sentence is a long conditional ("But when they write down truthfully...") whose apodosis is v. 12 ("Then, I know another mystery...") — the draft keeps the "But when... Then..." shape, not a summary.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 105

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 105" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_105), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 262–263 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse and sign faithfully).

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter CV = vv. 1–2 exactly, spanning printed pp. 262–263; "CVI. 1." begins on p. 264 immediately after v. 2, under the display head "*FRAGMENT OF THE BOOK OF NOAH*". Display head (p. 262, italic, centered): "*God and the Messiah to dwell with Man.*" Inline head: bold "CV. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER CV." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 262 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 263 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **No thick type** in CV. **No daggers** in the CV main text. **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(them)" and "(it)" (v. 1). No square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in the CV main text.

CV. 1. In those days the Lord bade (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) unto them; for ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth. 2. For I and My Son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness in their lives; and ye shall have peace: rejoice, ye children of uprightness. Amen.

**Print-level findings (both scans):** no thick type, no daggers, no brackets except the two round-bracket supplies in the CV main text — typographically plain. Charles's chapter note (sighted): "CV. This chapter does not seem to belong to 91–104. For (1) the phrase 'children of earth', which in 91–104 is a synonym for the sinners or heathen, has here a good ethical signification: see 100^6 (note) 101^1 (note). (2) The Messiah is introduced in 105^2, to whom there is not the faintest allusion throughout 91–104. (3) The finite duration of the lives of the saints seems to be implied in 105^2. This is the doctrine in 1–36, but not in 91–104. (4) The emphasis is laid in 105 on the finite life on earth: in 91–104 on the immortal life in heaven. This chapter, like 56^5–57^3a, is a literary revival of O.T. thoughts and ideals." The v. 1 note (sighted): "In those (α–m). m, β 'and in those'. And testify. > m. Children of earth. This phrase has a good signification here; for the books of Enoch, which only 'the righteous and the wise' will receive, are the guides of those designated 'children of earth'. Contrast with this the technical meaning of this phrase in 100^6 102^3." The v. 2 note (sighted): "I and My Son. There is no difficulty about the phrase 'My Son' as applied" (continues on p. 263).

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** none — the transcription matched the print word-for-word on wording, punctuation, and verse numbering. The transcription's display head matches the print's; its "CHAPTER CV." is a normalization of the inline "CV. 1.".

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. In those days the Lord told (them) to call together and speak to the children of earth about their wisdom: Show (it) to them, for you are their guides, and a reward over the whole earth. 2. For I and My Son will be joined with them forever in the paths of uprightness in their lives; and you will have peace. Rejoice, you children of uprightness! Amen.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **A fragment out of place:** Charles's note (sighted) gives four reasons ch. 105 "does not seem to belong to 91–104" — (1) "children of earth" is used here in a good sense, unlike 91–104; (2) the Messiah appears only here; (3) the saints' finite lifespan (the 1–36 doctrine, not 91–104's); (4) the emphasis on finite earthly life vs 91–104's immortal heavenly life. The draft translates the fragment as printed, in place, and adds no harmonization. Whether a reader-facing note flags the displacement stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **Thou/Thy/Thee → You/Your:** "ye are their guides" → "you are their guides"; "ye shall have peace" → "you will have peace"; "ye children of uprightness" → "you children of uprightness"; plain register per the ch. 9 standing rule; disclosed.
- **"(them)" and "(it)" kept (v. 1):** Charles's round-bracket supplies kept visible per the standing rule.
- **"the Lord bade (them) to summon and testify" → "the Lord told (them) to call together and speak" (v. 1):** "bade" → "told"; "summon" → "call together"; "testify" → "speak" (plain register); disclosed.
- **"to the children of earth concerning their wisdom" → "to the children of earth about their wisdom" (v. 1):** plain register; the "children of earth" phrase kept (its good sense here is Charles's point); disclosed.
- **"Show (it) unto them" → "Show (it) to them" (v. 1):** plain register; disclosed.
- **"a recompense over the whole earth" → "a reward over the whole earth" (v. 1):** "recompense" → "reward" (plain register); disclosed. (Charles's note: cf. 104:13 — sighted.)
- **"For I and My Son will be united with them for ever" → "For I and My Son will be joined with them forever" (v. 2):** "united" → "joined" (plain register); "My Son" kept as Charles prints it (his note begins a discussion — sighted — recorded as apparatus); disclosed.
- **"in the paths of uprightness in their lives" kept (v. 2):** the Two-Ways language; disclosed.
- **"ye shall have peace: rejoice, ye children of uprightness. Amen." → "you will have peace. Rejoice, you children of uprightness! Amen." (v. 2):** plain register; the "Amen" kept; disclosed.
- **No thick type, no daggers, no brackets to settle:** the chapter is typographically plain apart from the two round-bracket supplies.
- **Greek control (via Charles's footnotes, sighted):** the sigla at v. 1. Recorded as apparatus; none imported, and no independent Greek transcription claimed.
- **No independently collated control reading** is claimed for any verse in this chapter: the draft is Charles-1912-based, witness-flagged, with the Chester Beatty Greek consulted here only through Charles's printed footnotes as verified on the scans. Any future claim of Greek-checked wording requires an actual transcription step that this lane has not performed.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 106

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 106" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_106), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 264–268 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below. The transcription carries the full English text (vv. 1–19); two thick-type emendations invisible in the transcription were settled on the scans and are marked in the base below. **Layout difference:** the print sets the Latin fragment SIDE-BY-SIDE with the English in two columns (pp. 264–267); the transcription prints the Latin AFTER the English — a normalization, recorded.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter CVI = vv. 1–19 exactly, spanning printed pp. 264–268; "CVII. 1." begins on p. 269 immediately after v. 19. Display heads (p. 264): "*FRAGMENT OF THE BOOK OF NOAH*" (left column) and "*LATIN FRAGMENT*" (right column). Inline head: bold "CVI. 1." run into the text. Running heads: p. 264 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 265 "Chapter CVI. 1–8"; p. 266 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap); p. 267 "Chapter CVI. 9–15"; p. 268 (page-level head not captured — recorded as a gap). **English verse order in print:** 14, **17**, 15, 16, 18, 19 — Charles's note (sighted): "17. I have restored this verse to its original place." **Thick type (Charles's emendations, invisible in the transcription):** "**wherefore**" (v. 8) and "**angels**" (v. 13) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Daggers † (corrupt):** "†and his long locks were white as wool, and his eyes beautiful †" (v. 2); "†conversed with†" (v. 3). **Square brackets [ ] (editorial):** "[he and his sons shall be saved]" (v. 16). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(them)" (v. 19). No corner brackets, no angle brackets in the English main text.

CVI. 1. And after some days my son Methuselah took a wife for his son Lamech, and she became pregnant by him and bore a son. 2. And his body was white as snow and red as the blooming of a rose, and the hair of his head †and his long locks were white as wool, and his eyes beautiful †. And when he opened his eyes, he lighted up the whole house like the sun, and the whole house was very bright. 3. And thereupon he arose in the hands of the midwife, opened his mouth, and †conversed with† the Lord of righteousness. 4. And his father Lamech was afraid of him and fled, and came to his father Methuselah. 5. And he said unto him: 'I have begotten a strange son, diverse from and unlike man, and resembling the sons of the God of heaven; and his nature is different and he is not like us, and his eyes are as the rays of the sun, and his countenance is glorious. 6. And it seems to me that he is not sprung from me but from the angels, and I fear that in his days a wonder may be wrought on the earth. 7. And now, my father, I am here to petition thee and implore thee that thou mayst go to Enoch, our father, and learn from him the truth, for his dwelling-place is amongst the angels.' 8. And when Methuselah heard the words of his son, he came to me to the ends of the earth; for he had heard that I was there, and he cried aloud, and I heard his voice and I came to him. And I said unto him: 'Behold, here am I, my son, **wherefore** hast thou come to me?' 9. And he answered and said: 'Because of a great cause of anxiety have I come to thee, and because of a disturbing vision have I approached. 10. And now, my father, hear me: unto Lamech my son there hath been born a son, the like of whom there is none, and his nature is not like man's nature, and the colour of his body is whiter than snow and redder than the bloom of a rose, and the hair of his head is whiter than white wool, and his eyes are like the rays of the sun, and he opened his eyes and thereupon lighted up the whole house. 11. And he arose in the hands of the midwife, and opened his mouth and blessed the Lord of heaven. 12. And his father Lamech became afraid and fled to me, and did not believe that he was sprung from him, but that he was in the likeness of the angels of heaven; and behold I have come to thee that thou mayst make known to me the truth.' 13. And I, Enoch, answered and said unto him: 'The Lord will do a new thing on the earth, and this I have already seen in a vision, and make known to thee that in the generation of my father Jared some of the **angels** of heaven transgressed the word of the Lord. 14. And behold they commit sin and transgress the law, and have united themselves with women and commit sin with them, and have married some of them, and have begot children by them. 17. And they shall produce on the earth giants not according to the spirit, but according to the flesh, and there shall be a great punishment on the earth, and the earth shall be cleansed from all impurity. 15. Yea, there shall come a great destruction over the whole earth, and there shall be a deluge and a great destruction for one year. 16. And this son who has been born unto you shall be left on the earth, and his three children shall be saved with him: when all mankind that are on the earth shall die [he and his sons shall be saved]. 18. And now make known to thy son Lamech that he who has been born is in truth his son, and call his name Noah; for he shall be left to you, and he and his sons shall be saved from the destruction, which shall come upon the earth on account of all the sin and all the unrighteousness, which shall be consummated on the earth in his days. 19. And after that there shall be still more unrighteousness than that which was first consummated on the earth; for I know the mysteries of the holy ones; for He, the Lord, has showed me and informed me, and I have read (them) in the heavenly tablets.'

**The Latin fragment** (printed side-by-side in the right column, pp. 264–267; the transcription appends it after the English — a layout normalization):
CVI. 1. Factum est autem [cum esset Lamech annorum tricentorum quinquagenta] natus est ei filiu(s)
2. Cui oculi sunt sicut radi solis capilli autem *eius* candi⟨di⟩ores in septies niue, corpori autem eius nemo hominum potest intueri.
3. et surexit *inter* man*us* obstetricis suae et adorauit do*minum* uiuentem in secula [laudauit].
4. et timuit Lamech.
6. ne *non* ex eo natus esset nisi *nontius* dei.
4, 5. et uenit ad patrem suum Mathusalem et narrauit illi om*nia*.
7. dixit Mathusalem: Ego autem non possum scire nisi eamus ad patrem *nostrum* Enoc.
8. qu*um* autem uidit Enoc filium suum Mathusalem uenientem ad se [et] ait. quid *est* quod uenisti ad me nate?
9. Dix*it*:
10. quod natus *est* filio suo [nomine] Lamech cui oculi sunt sicut radi solis capilli[s] eius candidiores septies niue, corpori *autem* eius nemo hominum potest intueri
11. et surexit inter manus obstetricis suae eadem hora qua *procidit* de utero matris suae. orauit do*minum* uiuente*m* in secula et laudauit.
12. et timuit Lamech.
13. et dixit Enoc: nontiatum *est* mihi fili *quia* post quingentos annos
15. mitt*et* deus cataclismu*m* [XL.] [et erunt nomina filiorum eius · Sem · Cham · Iafeth]
16. et erunt illi • III • filii
18. et ipse uocabitur Noe qui interpretatur requies quia requiem prestabit in archa*m*.

(Latin typography, both scans: square brackets on [cum esset...], [laudauit], [nomine], [et], [XL.], [et erunt nomina...]; angle brackets on candi⟨di⟩ores; parentheses on filiu(s), capilli[s]; italics on *eius*, *inter*, *manus*, *dominum*, *non*, *nontius*, *omnia*, *nostrum*, *quum*, *est*, *Dixit*, *autem*, *procidit*, *uiuente m*, *quia*, *mittet*, *cataclismum*. The transcription's Latin carries the same signs — verified against the print.)

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 8 "**wherefore**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "8. Wherefore. So Latin 'quid est quod' = διὰ τί. But the Ethiopic = διότι, a corruption of the former." v. 13 "**angels**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "Some of the angels. Here I emend 'ĕmmal'ĕlta (='some from the heights') of u, β–ehkn into emmalâ'ĕkta = 'some of the angels'." v. 2's dagger pair ("†and his long locks were white as wool, and his eyes beautiful †") on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "It is rather astonishing that the new-born infant should have 'long locks'. Since there is no mention of these in the Latin, and since it is possible that dĕmdĕmâhû ... šanây 'a'ĕjentûhû (='his long locks ... and (> 1gq) his eyes beautiful') is corrupt for 'ĕgarihû laṣaḥây 'a'ĕjentûhû." v. 3 "†conversed with†" on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "Here tanâgara = 'conversed with' is corrupt for tagânaja = προσκυνῆσαι or ἐξωμολογήσατο. Hence render 'praised'." The v. 17 note (sighted): "I have restored this verse to its original place." The CVI–CVII headnote (sighted): "We have here again a fragment of a Noah Apocalypse. Part of this section has been preserved in a Latin version which I print side by side with the translation of the Ethiopic." The Latin/Greek discussion (sighted): "the Ethiopic = εὐλόγησε and the Latin 'oravit' — evidently a corruption for 'adoravit' ... the Latin and the Ethiopic presuppose different words in the Greek version."

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** three —
1. **Thick type invisible in the transcription:** "**wherefore**" (v. 8) and "**angels**" (v. 13) are Charles's emendations, marked in the base above.
2. **Layout:** the transcription appends the Latin fragment after the English; the print sets them side-by-side in two columns (pp. 264–267). Recorded as a layout normalization, not a wording difference.
3. **Verse 19 present:** the transcription carries 106:19 ("And after that there shall be still more unrighteousness..."); the print confirms it. No omission. (An earlier working note misrecorded the transcription as ending at v. 18 — corrected: the transcription includes v. 19, matching the print.)
Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word on the English text, including the 14, 17, 15 order and all brackets, daggers, and parentheses.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above — English text only; the Latin is not rendered)

1. After some days, my son Methuselah took a wife for his son Lamech, and she became pregnant by him and bore a son. 2. His body was white as snow and red as a rose in bloom, and the hair of his head †and his long locks were white as wool, and his eyes beautiful†. When he opened his eyes, he lit up the whole house like the sun, and the whole house was very bright. 3. Then he stood up in the midwife's hands, opened his mouth, and †spoke with† the Lord of righteousness. 4. His father Lamech was afraid of him and ran away, and came to his father Methuselah. 5. He said to him: "I have fathered a strange son, different from other men and not like a man — he looks like the sons of the God of heaven. His nature is different; he is not like us. His eyes are like sunbeams, and his face is glorious. 6. It seems to me he is not my child but comes from the angels, and I fear that in his lifetime a miracle may happen on the earth. 7. Now, my father, I am here to beg you and plead with you: go to Enoch, our father, and learn the truth from him, for he lives among the angels." 8. When Methuselah heard his son's words, he came to me at the ends of the earth, for he had heard I was there. He cried out loud, and I heard his voice and went to him. I said to him: "Here I am, my son — **why** have you come to me?" 9. He answered: "I have come to you because something is weighing heavily on me, and because a troubling vision has brought me here. 10. Now, my father, hear me: my son Lamech has had a son born to him, like no other — his nature is not like human nature. His body is whiter than snow and redder than a rose in bloom, his hair whiter than white wool, his eyes like sunbeams. He opened his eyes and lit up the whole house. 11. He stood up in the midwife's hands, opened his mouth, and blessed the Lord of heaven. 12. His father Lamech was afraid and ran to me. He does not believe the boy is his — he thinks he looks like the angels of heaven. So I have come to you to learn the truth." 13. I, Enoch, answered him: "The Lord will do a new thing on the earth. I have already seen it in a vision. Let me tell you: in the days of my father Jared, some of the **angels** of heaven broke the Lord's command. 14. They sin and break the law — they have joined themselves to women and sin with them, married some of them, and fathered children by them. 17. They will bring forth giants on the earth — not spirit-beings but flesh — and there will be great punishment on the earth, and the earth will be washed clean of all filth. 15. Yes, a great ruin will come over the whole earth — a flood, and great ruin for a year. 16. This son born to you will be left on the earth, and his three sons will be saved with him. When everyone on earth dies [he and his sons will be saved]. 18. Now tell your son Lamech that the boy who was born is truly his son. Name him Noah, for he will be left for you — he and his sons will be saved from the ruin coming on the earth because of all the sin and unrighteousness that will run its course on earth in his lifetime. 19. After that, there will be even more unrighteousness than was first completed on the earth. For I know the secrets of the holy ones — the Lord has shown me and told me, and I have read (them) in the heavenly tablets."

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **A Noah fragment, not the Epistle proper:** Charles's headnote (sighted) calls 106–107 "a fragment of a Noah Apocalypse," printed here after the displaced ch. 105. - **The Latin left untranslated:** the Latin fragment is reproduced as printed (side-by-side in the original); this lane renders the English (Ethiopic-derived) text only. Whether the Latin should be rendered into English stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.
- **"**wherefore**" in thick type (v. 8) → "**why**":** Charles's own emendation (Ethiopic διότι corrupt for διὰ τί, per the Latin "quid est quod") — marked in base and draft per the ch. 2 standing rule. ## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above)

1. I saw written on them that generation after generation will go wrong, until a generation of righteousness rises, and wrongdoing is destroyed, and sin leaves the earth, and every kind of good comes on it. 2. Now, my son, go and tell your son Lamech that this boy who has been born is truly his son, and that (this) is no lie." 3. When Methuselah had heard his father Enoch's words — for he had shown him everything in secret — he went back and showed (them) to him, and named the boy Noah, for he will bring the earth comfort after all the ruin.

## Base text — R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912), ch. 108 — A LATER APPENDIX

Drafting copy: Wikisource transcription, "The Book of Enoch (Charles)/Chapter 108" (https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Book_of_Enoch_(Charles)/Chapter_108), carrying the Charles text (public domain). Full scan verification of the base on printed pp. 269–272 in both IA 1912 copies performed at G1 — see the "Print-level findings" below; no transcription-vs-print wording corrections were needed (the transcription carried every verse and sign faithfully), but the thick-type emendation invisible in the transcription was settled on the scans and is marked in the base below.

Chapter span, heading form, and scan facts (verified on both scans at G1): Chapter CVIII = vv. 1–15 exactly, spanning printed pp. 269–272; it is the last chapter of the book. "CVIII. 1." begins on p. 269 immediately after CVII.3. There is no display head for CVIII — the chapter opens with the inline head bold "CVIII. 1." run into the text (the transcription's display "CHAPTER CVIII." is a normalization). Running heads: p. 269 "Chapters CVI. 16—CVIII. 3"; p. 270 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern); p. 271 "Chapter CVIII. 4–11"; p. 272 "The Book of Enoch" / "[Sect. V" (even-page pattern). **Thick type (Charles's emendation, invisible in the transcription):** "**fire shall they burn**" (v. 3) — settled on the scans, marked in the base below. **Daggers † (corrupt):** "†look over†" (v. 4). **Round parentheses (Charles's supply):** "(even)" (v. 6). No square brackets, no corner brackets, no angle brackets in the CVIII main text. The divine speech (vv. 11–15) is God's word ("Verses 11 and 12 are represented as being spoken by God" — sighted); the print closes it with .' at v. 15.

CVIII. 1. Another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him, and keep the law in the last days. 2. Ye who have done good shall wait for those days till an end is made of those who work evil, and an end of the might of the transgressors. 3. And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the **fire shall they burn**; for there is no earth there. 4. And I saw there something like an invisible cloud; for by reason of its depth I could not †look over†, and I saw a flame of fire blazing brightly, and things like shining mountains circling and sweeping to and fro. 5. And I asked one of the holy angels who was with me and said unto him: 'What is this shining thing? for it is not a heaven but only the flame of a blazing fire, and the voice of weeping and crying and lamentation and strong pain.' 6. And he said unto me: 'This place which thou seest—here are cast the spirits of sinners and blasphemers, and of those who work wickedness, and of those who pervert every thing that the Lord hath spoken through the mouth of the prophets—(even) the things that shall be. 7. For some of them are written and inscribed above in the heaven, in order that the angels may read them and know that which shall befall the sinners, and the spirits of the humble, and of those who have afflicted their bodies, and been recompensed by God; and of those who have been put to shame by wicked men: 8. Who love God and loved neither gold nor silver nor any of the good things which are in the world, but gave over their bodies to torture. 9. Who, since they came into being, longed not after earthly food, but regarded everything as a passing breath, and lived accordingly, and the Lord tried them much, and their spirits were found pure so that they should bless His name. 10. And all the blessings destined for them I have recounted in the books. And He hath assigned them their recompense, because they have been found to be such as loved heaven more than their life in the world, and though they were trodden under foot of wicked men, and experienced abuse and reviling from them and were put to shame, yet they blessed Me. 11. And now I will summon the spirits of the good who belong to the generation of light, and I will transform those who were born in darkness, who in the flesh were not recompensed with such honour as their faithfulness deserved. 12. And I will bring forth in shining light those who have loved My holy name, and I will seat each on the throne of his honour. 13. And they shall be resplendent for times without number; for righteousness is the judgement of God; for to the faithful He will give faithfulness in the habitation of upright paths. 14. And they shall see those who were born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous shall be resplendent. 15. And the sinners shall cry aloud and see them resplendent, and they indeed shall go where days and seasons are prescribed for them.'

**Print-level findings (both scans, enlarged crops):** v. 3 "**fire shall they burn**" is in thick type on both scans; Charles's footnote (sighted): "In the fire shall they burn = ba'ĕsât jĕnaddû. So I emend ba'ĕsât naddû (g1gmqt, β–abcx) = 'in the fire they have burnt'. abcx emend into ba'ĕsât jĕnadĕdû 'in fire they shall burn'. But 21^3 ba'ĕsât ... jĕnaddû supports my emendation." v. 4 "†look over†" carries daggers on both scans; Charles's note (sighted): "We might emend lâ'ĕla (='over') into lĕ'ĕlnâhû and render 'behold its height' or emend both words into behîl ḥašĕrô 'tell its circuit' (or 'size'). But the text is uncertain." v. 6 "(even)" is Charles's round-bracket supply. The v. 3 "Chaotic" note (sighted): "Eth. = ἀόρατος, which is the LXX rendering of תהו in Gen. 1^2." The CVIII headnote (sighted): "This final chapter forms an independent addition. Its writer was acquainted with sections 1–36 and 91–104... The writer is Essene in tone." and "108 is more nearly akin to 91–104 than any other section in the book. The object of this chapter is to encourage the righteous still to hope on despite the long delay of the advent of the kingdom." The v. 11 note (sighted): "Verses 11 and 12 are represented as being spoken by God." No square brackets, no corner or angle brackets in the CVIII main text.

**Material transcription-vs-print corrections (print is the authority):** one — the thick-type "**fire shall they burn**" (v. 3) is Charles's emendation (ba'ĕsât naddû → ba'ĕsât jĕnaddû), invisible in the transcription, marked in the base above. Otherwise the transcription matched the print word-for-word. The transcription's "CHAPTER CVIII." is a normalization of the inline "CVIII. 1."; there is no display head for this chapter in print.

## Clear-English draft (fresh, plain register, from the Charles 1912 base above — the appendix rendered fully, flagged as an appendix)

**[LATER APPENDIX — not part of the Epistle of Enoch.]**

1. Another book that Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah, and for those who will come after him and keep the law in the last days. 2. You who have done good, wait for those days, until an end is made of those who do evil, and an end of the power of the wrongdoers. 3. Yes, wait until sin is gone, for their names will be wiped out of the book of life and out of the holy books. Their children will be destroyed forever, their spirits will be killed, and they will cry and wail in a place that is a wild wasteland — and in the **fire they will burn**, for there is no earth there. 4. I saw there something like a cloud you cannot see through; because it was so deep I could not †see across† it. I saw a flame of fire blazing brightly, and things like shining mountains circling and sweeping back and forth. 5. I asked one of the holy angels who was with me: "What is this shining thing? It is not a sky, only the flame of a blazing fire — and I hear weeping and crying and wailing and terrible pain." 6. He said to me: "This place you see — here are thrown the spirits of sinners and blasphemers, and of those who do wickedness, and of those who twist everything the Lord has spoken through the prophets — (even) the things that are to come. 7. Some of them are written down in heaven above, so that the angels may read them and know what will happen to the sinners" — and to the spirits of the humble, and of those who punished their bodies and were rewarded by God, and of those who were shamed by wicked men: 8. who love God, and loved neither gold nor silver nor any of the good things in the world, but gave their bodies over to be tortured. 9. From the time they came into being, they did not crave earthly food, but counted everything as a passing breath, and lived that way. The Lord tested them hard, and their spirits were found pure, so that they would bless His name. 10. I have written down in the books all the blessings meant for them. He has given them their reward, because they were found to love heaven more than their life in the world — and though wicked men trampled them underfoot, insulted and mocked them, and shamed them, they blessed Me. 11. Now I will call the spirits of the good who belong to the generation of light, and I will change those who were born in darkness — who in the flesh were not rewarded with the honor their faithfulness deserved. 12. I will bring out into shining light those who have loved My holy name, and I will set each one on the throne of his honor. 13. They will shine for ages without number, for righteousness is God's judgment — to the faithful He will give faithfulness in the home of straight paths. 14. They will see those born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous shine. 15. The sinners will cry out loud and see them shining, and they will go where days and seasons are appointed for them.

## Notes — forks, brackets, and things not smoothed away

- **⚠ LATER APPENDIX — flagged three times:** in the banner, in the chapter line, and in the draft's opening bracket. Charles's headnote (sighted): "This final chapter forms an independent addition. Its writer was acquainted with sections 1–36 and 91–104... The writer is Essene in tone." It is "more nearly akin to 91–104 than any other section" but it is NOT part of the Epistle — it must not be presented as ch. 91–105's continuation. Whether the published form sets it apart typographically (e.g. as an appendix) stands as printed, by the editor's read-through ruling of 2026-10-14.

## Editor's Epilogue

This book was made from one lawful source: the English translation of R. H. Charles, printed at Oxford in 1912 and now in the public domain. Charles made that translation from his own Ethiopic edition of 1906, a text he built by comparing twenty-three manuscripts. The book itself is 1 Enoch, an ancient work ascribed to Enoch, seventh from Adam. A passage from it is quoted in the New Testament, in the letter of Jude, and in Ethiopia the book has kept its place in the canon of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church down to this day. Outside Ethiopia it was lost to the West for centuries, until James Bruce returned from Abyssinia in 1773 bringing copies written in Ge'ez, the classical language of Ethiopia. The whole book survives only in Ge'ez, and only in Ethiopia was it kept whole while other lands let it go. Everything in these pages stands or falls on that footing, and the footing is stated here so that no reader has to guess at it.

The chain behind those copies must be told plainly. The Ge'ez text is itself a translation, made from a Greek version that is now lost as a whole. That Greek version was itself made from Hebrew and Aramaic originals, and those originals are lost as well. Pieces of the earlier forms do survive: Aramaic fragments were found among the scrolls at Qumran, and Greek fragments survive in a handful of manuscripts and quotations, but each covers only part of the book. Where those fragments survive, they stand as controls. Where they do not survive, no control is claimed. One long stretch needs a plain warning still: the Book of Parables, chapters thirty-seven to seventy-one, has no witness in any earlier language at all, and for those chapters the Ge'ez text stands alone. This rendering was made from Charles's English, honestly and openly, by an editor in Hays, Kansas, who does not read Ge'ez and says so here without dressing it up. It is a translation of a translation, and it is labelled as such on every page. The work was to turn Charles's older English into plain, clear English that an ordinary reader can follow, keeping the strangeness where the text is strange.

This book carries its DRAFT banner, and it carries its disclosure of help from artificial intelligence, and neither is tucked away where a reader might miss it. The book was audited chapter by chapter, and the fingerprints of the build — the record of that checking — are printed in the Verification Record at the back of the workshop edition, so that any reader can see what was done and can walk the trail again for himself. The editor has read it through and has ruled it ready as what it is: an audited draft. It is not put forward as a finished edition, and it asks no one to treat it as more than that. Nothing in these pages asks to be believed on authority. The honesty of the book lies in showing its footing, its limits, and its record, and then letting the reader judge.

Of this book's place among other renderings, only what can be shown will be said. Its coverage can be stated plainly: all one hundred and eight chapters are rendered here, and none has been skipped or abridged. And the book rendered is the First Book of Enoch only: the Second and Third Books of Enoch are separate, later works, by other hands, and no part of them stands in these pages. Beyond that coverage, no larger claim is made. This edition does not claim a heavy scholarly apparatus, and it does not ask to stand in the place of Charles, whose learning made it possible. It claims only to be plain, to show its work, and to open a book to readers who have neither Ge'ez nor Greek, and who would otherwise have no way in.

It is given away freely, under an open license, under its author's own name, as all such rescues should be. Anyone may download this edition, copy it, print it, and share it, in whole or in part, without asking permission. Attribution to the editor is requested as a courtesy; it is not a condition, and the gift is not withdrawn if that courtesy is omitted. No price is set on it, and no one needs to write and ask leave to pass it on. The editor's part was the framing, the labour of the audit, and the presenting of it to the world. The words are Enoch's, as the long chain of hands handed them down.

This edition was prepared with the assistance of artificial intelligence, under the editor's direction and subject to his rulings at every gate. The decisions, the sign-offs, and the errors that remain are the editor's own.

A living translation, holding itself accountable.

**Robert Tilford, editor**
Hays, Kansas
October 2026

## Verification Record

### 1. What this book is and its lawful base

This book is a clear-English edition of 1 Enoch, in 108 chapters. It contains the First Book of Enoch only. The Second and Third Books of Enoch are separate, later works — 2 Enoch surviving in Slavonic, 3 Enoch a Hebrew mystical text — and are not part of this edition. It is a translation of a translation, and the record states the chain plainly so a reader can check it.

Route A was the route taken. Clear English was drafted from R. H. Charles, *The Book of Enoch, or 1 Enoch* (1912, public domain). Charles's 1912 English was itself made from his 1906 Ethiopic edition, *The Ethiopic Version of the Book of Enoch*, edited from 23 manuscripts (1906, public domain).

Charles 1906, Dillmann 1851, Laurence 1821, and the public-domain Greek fragments were open as controls. All modern translations were check-only. They were not used as a base and were not followed as a skeleton.

The five pre-build design questions, D1–D5 in the source audit, were never separately ruled. The build proceeded under Route A and was completed, so they stand overtaken by the finished build. This record states Route A as the route actually taken.

Route B, a formal Ethiopic control column on every worksheet, was not performed and is not claimed. No Ge'ez reader serves this lane.

Charles 1912 is public domain. The editor's own edition is given under the open license ruled on 2026-10-14 and recorded in section 5 below.
